articles.title: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

paras.en: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

Carlisle Brake & Friction has broken ground to expand its Chennai, India manufacturing operations in one of the world’s fastest-growing industrial regions. Having produced mechatronic products in the region for more than 15 years, Carlisle CBF will relocate to add production at a larger site for off-highway paper wet friction discs and steel separator plates. The new facility is scheduled to open in 2027.

The move to expanded space is designed to accommodate manufacturing capabilities needed to serve the growing demand across the agriculture, construction and especially mining industries in India and Southeast Asia. Local production will improve supply chain responsiveness while supporting original equipment and aftermarket requirements in cost-sensitive markets.

Carlisle Brake & Friction is establishing a state-of-the-art wet friction manufacturing facility on par with proven global manufacturing processes in the new Chennai plant, to build a more resilient regional platform. This expansion strengthens our ability to deliver durable wet friction products that help keep critical off-highway equipment productive.

articles.title: Why the Right Car Accident Lawyer Changes the Outcome of a Claim
articles.author: Tyrepress Advertorial

paras.en: Why the Right Car Accident Lawyer Changes the Outcome of a Claim

A car crash can turn an ordinary day into months of medical appointments, insurance calls, and difficult decisions. In 2025, Missouri recorded 909 traffic fatalities, a 4.8% decrease from 2024. In the St. Louis region, 157 people died in traffic crashes that year, with 25% of those fatalities involving pedestrians or bicyclists. These figures show that serious collisions remain a concern even as roadway deaths continue to decline.

For people dealing with injuries, vehicle damage, lost income, or other consequences after a crash, the claims process can feel just as challenging as the recovery itself. A car accident lawyer in St. Louis can help assess the circumstances, identify potentially responsible parties, handle insurer communications, and pursue compensation supported by the available evidence. When injured parties know how legal decisions can shape a claim, they can take an important step in determining what comes next.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Early Decisions Affect Available Evidence

Evidence often determines whether an insurance dispute ends quickly or requires further action. A lawyer examines the crash report, photographs, traffic signals, road conditions, vehicle damage, and witness accounts.
Physical evidence can disappear after repairs, weather changes, or vehicle storage. Legal counsel can request records promptly and preserve information that supports the claimant’s account.

Insurance companies also review recorded statements and social media posts. A claimant who speaks publicly without legal guidance can minimize symptoms, accept blame, or create inconsistencies that damage credibility.
Liability Requires More Than a Police Report

A police report provides useful information, but it does not resolve every issue in a civil claim. The report might omit witnesses, overlook road conditions, or provide limited detail about the collision.

A lawyer compares the report with photographs, medical records, vehicle damage, and witness testimony. That review helps establish how each driver acted before the crash and whether another factor contributed.
- Comparative Fault Rules Cannot Be Ignored

Missouri uses comparative fault rules. If a claimant shares responsibility, the final recovery can decrease according to that percentage. A clear liability record therefore affects the amount the claimant eventually receives.
Medical Records Connect Injuries to Financial Losses
A claim needs medical proof connecting the crash to the reported injuries. Treatment records, diagnostic results, physician notes, and follow-up appointments show the following:
Consistent treatment also creates a reliable timeline. Gaps in care can lead an insurer to argue that the injury was minor, unrelated, or resolved sooner than the records indicate.

Damages include more than emergency bills. A complete claim accounts for ongoing treatment, lost income, reduced work capacity, medication costs, transportation, and pain-related limits on ordinary activities. Each category requires supporting documentation.
Insurance Tactics Can Shift the Claim’s Value

An insurer’s first settlement proposal rarely reflects every documented loss. This is because a carrier may evaluate only the early information available at that stage, which often excludes future care and the full extent of lost earnings. However, a lawyer calculates damages after reviewing medical progress and employment records. This process prevents a claimant from accepting payment before doctors understand the likely course of recovery.

Insurance adjusters also seek statements about prior injuries, current symptoms, and work limitations. Accurate answers matter, but speculation creates avoidable disputes. Legal guidance keeps communications focused on documented facts.
A claim must follow applicable filing deadlines and procedural requirements. Missing a deadline can prevent a claimant from pursuing compensation, even when the evidence supports fault.

A lawyer tracks those dates while handling communications, records requests, settlement discussions, and court filings. This organization lets the claimant focus on medical care instead of managing demands from several parties.

Local knowledge also helps counsel assess road conditions, traffic patterns, reporting practices, and court procedures in the St. Louis area. These details provide useful context during liability analysis and settlement negotiations.
Settlement or Trial Requires Careful Timing

Most injury claims resolve through negotiation, but a settlement should follow a complete review of liability and damages. A lawyer evaluates the insurer’s position, identifies missing damages, and explains the financial effects of accepting a settlement.
If negotiations fail, the evidence gathered during the claim can support a lawsuit. A prepared case helps the claimant choose between a fair resolution and asking a court to decide disputed issues.

The right lawyer changes a car accident claim by preserving evidence, testing liability, documenting medical losses, and resisting premature settlement pressure. A claimant should save photographs and records, follow medical instructions, avoid detailed insurer statements, and arrange a case review promptly.

Early legal analysis helps locate missing proof before it disappears and identifies deadlines before they become obstacles. These steps give the claim a documented foundation and help the claimant choose between settlement and litigation.

articles.title: Fix Auto Avondale Showcases $200K Custom Build at SEMA Show
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Fix Auto USA has recognized Fix Auto Avondale and owner Troy Buck for two recent initiatives highlighting the team’s craftsmanship and community involvement.

At the 2026 SEMA Show, Fix Auto Avondale presented a custom vehicle completed through a frame-off restoration. The project was finished in 60 days, with four employees contributing approximately 4,000 hours. The build is valued at more than $200,000.
The vehicle featured custom modifications, including a shaved firewall, shaved cowl panel, sectioned fenders, molded-in spoiler and custom Kandy paint. The vehicle received a strong response at SEMA.

“Seeing the response to the car at SEMA was incredibly rewarding for all of us,” said Buck. “Our team put an unbelievable amount of time and effort into this build, and completing something of this scale in only 60 days took everyone working together. I’m extremely proud of what our team accomplished and the craftsmanship they brought to every detail.”

Ahead of Alice Cooper’s annual charitable concert on Dec. 12, Buck also created an original Alice Cooper painting to raise funds for Alice Cooper’s Solid Rock Teen Centers. The piece continues Buck’s involvement with the organization.

Earlier this year, Buck collaborated with teen artists from the center to create the 10th and final installation in the City of Goodyear’s “HeART of Goodyear” public art project. The sculpture is displayed outside the Solid Rock Teen Center.

Fix Auto Avondale made a $1,500 cash donation to Alice Cooper’s Solid Rock Teen Centers and a $1,500 cash donation to Your Heart Our Hands, which supports youth who have aged out of the foster care system. Over the past three years, Fix Auto Avondale has provided more than $80,000 in charitable donations.

“Solid Rock is an organization I’ve been fortunate to support year after year, and it’s something that means a lot to me personally,” said Buck. “Creating these paintings gives me a chance to combine my love of art with an opportunity to give back and support young people in our community. Whether it’s through the annual concert, working alongside the teens or finding other ways to contribute, I’m grateful to be involved. Our team believes strongly in giving back to the communities that support us, and I’m proud of what we’ve been able to accomplish.”

articles.title: Study: Thanksgiving Drivers Add 510 Crashes Due to Distraction
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Thanksgiving motorists face increased risks from distracted driving, speeding and hard braking, with new research estimating that higher levels of driver distraction during the holiday contribute to approximately 510 additional crashes and 290 injuries nationwide in a typical year.

The findings come from Cambridge Mobile Telematics (CMT), whose new U.S. Fall & Winter Holiday Road Risk Report examined more than 312 million vehicle trips across five holiday seasons to identify changes in driver behavior during major holidays.

According to the report, Thanksgiving produces the sharpest single-day increase in speeding and distracted driving among the seven holidays examined, raising concerns as millions of Americans prepare to travel for family gatherings.

The findings are particularly relevant as the collision repair industry continues to monitor changes in accident frequency and insurance claims volume. Although repairable claims have declined over the past two years, the study highlights how seasonal driving patterns and risky behavior can influence collision frequency.
Thanksgiving Day Presents Elevated Risks

CMT’s research identified two particularly hazardous travel periods surrounding Thanksgiving: the early morning hours following Thanksgiving Eve and the late-morning to early-afternoon rush to holiday gatherings.
Between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. on Thanksgiving Day, drivers’ phone screen time increases 22.7% compared to the same hours on a typical Thursday.
Researchers attributed the increased distraction to drivers managing navigation, communicating estimated arrival times and handling holiday-related calls and messages while traveling.
The findings suggest that the pressure to arrive at holiday gatherings on time can contribute to behaviors that increase crash risks.
Another particularly concerning period occurs between midnight and 4 a.m. on Thanksgiving Day, following Thanksgiving Eve celebrations.

During those hours, CMT identified overlapping increases in phone use, speeding and hard braking. Hard-braking incidents increased 25.5% compared to typical driving conditions during the same period, even though hard braking declined across the Thanksgiving holiday overall.

Thanksgiving Eve has traditionally been associated with concerns about impaired driving, but the CMT findings suggest that distraction and aggressive driving behaviors create additional hazards during the overnight hours.
Holiday Travel Adds to Driving Pressures
The report comes as higher travel costs and changing transportation preferences may influence how Americans reach their Thanksgiving destinations.
For families choosing to drive rather than fly, long-distance travel can introduce additional challenges, including congestion, fatigue, unfamiliar routes and pressure to maintain tight schedules.
Those factors can contribute to distracted driving and speeding, particularly when motorists attempt to coordinate travel plans or communicate with family members while behind the wheel.

The research also highlights the broader dangers associated with Thanksgiving travel. According to statistics cited in the study’s promotional materials, fatal crashes on Thanksgiving are nearly 10% higher than average.

While the CMT findings identify significant increases in risky driving behaviors, the company’s estimate of 510 additional crashes and 290 injuries represents a modeled assessment of the impact of increased distraction, rather than a count of crashes directly observed during the study.
For collision repair businesses, the research provides additional insight into how changes in driver behavior can affect accident frequency and repair demand.
Although the industry has experienced declining insurance claims volumes in recent years, seasonal increases in speeding and distracted driving remain important factors influencing collision risk.

The findings also reinforce the importance of distinguishing between overall vehicle travel, collision frequency and repairable insurance claims. An increase in risky driving behavior does not necessarily translate into a proportional increase in collision repair volume, particularly as vehicle repair costs and total-loss rates continue to influence which damaged vehicles are repaired.

CMT’s research suggests that reducing distractions, avoiding unnecessary speeding and planning travel to minimize fatigue and time pressures could help motorists lower their risk of a crash during the Thanksgiving holiday.
The complete findings are available in Cambridge Mobile Telematics’ U.S. Fall & Winter Holiday Road Risk Report.

articles.title: Waymo banned from California freeways following recent traffic incidents
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: Multiple news outlets report that recent traffic accidents involving Waymo robotaxis have led the California Department of Motor Vehicles to ban them from state freeways.

Waymo has temporarily stopped all driverless freeway service, according to the Associated Press. The rides had been offered in the San Francisco Bay Area and Los Angeles, as well as in Phoenix, Arizona; Miami, Florida; and Austin, Texas.
A Waymo spokesperson told the AP that the company would be “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel.”
“The suspension was implemented last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they didn’t say how long it would last,” the article states.

According to CBS News, the DMV said on Tuesday it issued restrictions on Nov. 11 because the vehicles “pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present.”

DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman said the ban followed two incidents, one in which three Waymo driverless vehicles drove into a construction zone on Nov. 5, according to the AP. He added that “similar incidents” occurred on May 18.
On Nov. 6, a Waymo vehicle reportedly tried to bypass California Highway Patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break, the AP reports.
Earlier this week, The Guardian shared footage of the Nov. 6 incident:

“Waymo in June because of multiple instances in April and May of their self-driving software failing to recognize ramp closures and construction zones in Arizona and California,” CBS News reports. “The move followed the company’s pause on freeway rides in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix and Miami, Florida to improve its vehicles’ performance and response in freeway construction zones.

“In addition, the Mountain View, California-based company in May paused service in Georgia and Texas because its . In December 2025, Waymo recalled about 3,000 vehicles after when its red lights were flashing and stop arm extended. In San Francisco, Waymo’s self-driving software struggles also include and .”
On Tuesday, USA Today shared video of an incident involving a Waymo robotaxi at a San Diego railroad crossing.
“Witness Holly Hudson said the self-driving car initially stalled while the way was clear and only moved through the crossing as the barriers came down,” reports USA Today.

Waymo’s homepage includes videos that show how its vehicles have responded to certain scenarios. Among them are a Waymo vehicle avoiding a police vehicle with its lights on, a vehicle running a red light, and a skateboarder running into the road. The site doesn’t mention the freeway ban.
In September, Waymo said at least 841 people have avoided injuries in traffic crashes across 270 million autonomous miles through the end of June.

A report on the safety performance of Waymo’s self-driving car technology, Waymo Driver, analyzes five major metropolitan service areas: Atlanta, Georgia; Austin, Texas; Los Angeles, California; Phoenix, Arizona; and San Francisco, California.

“Across these cities, the Waymo Driver continues to outperform human benchmarks,” a Waymo press release states. “Regardless of fault, it was involved in 841 fewer injury-causing crashes — an 82% reduction compared to human drivers.”
It adds that in more severe collisions, the Waymo Driver was involved in 95%, or 19 times fewer, serious injury or worse crashes than humans.

articles.title: LexisNexis: Auto policy shopping continues but also decelerating
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: U.S. auto policy shopping and new business growth were positive but continued to decelerate in the third quarter, according to LexisNexis Insurance Demand Meter.
Quarterly year-over-year shopping growth clocked in at 0.7%, down from 1.4% in Q2. New business growth was 3.2%, down slightly from last quarter’s 3.3%, the report states.

“While shopping activity remained strong, new business growth outpaced it for the fourth consecutive quarter,” the report states. “This highlights consumer commitment to securing new, more favorable policies in a competitive and price-sensitive market.”
Forty-seven percent of policies-in-force had been shopped at least once in the previous 12 months at the end of Q3. This matched Q2 and is slightly down from Q1.

“Consistency in the annual shop rate may reflect a broader shift in how policyholders approach shopping,” the report adds. “Sustained, elevated shopping levels suggest that some consumers are evaluating their policy options on a more regular basis, particularly if the opportunity for more favorable premiums arises.”

The exclusive distribution channel saw higher growth than the direct and independent channels, the report finds. Exclusive channel growth was up 4.5%, down from 6.8% in the previous quarter. Direct channel growth dropped to 1.8% from 4.6%. The independent channel grew 1.5%, up from -6.4% last quarter.
“Non-standard shopping surged ahead of standard shopping and posted positive growth for the first time in 2026,” the report states.
It adds that non-standard shoppers grew 5.4%, up from -9% in Q2. Standard shopping grew at 1.3%, a dip from 2.6% in Q2.

Policyholders aged 66 and older continued to be the strongest shopping growth among all ages for the 15th consecutive quarter. The 36 to 45 age group was the only other policyholder group to see positive gains quarter over quarter, increasing by 0.4% to 0.6%.
Twenty-eight states witnessed positive growth in Q3, compared to 42 states in the second and 37 states in the first. Fourteen states recorded a decline.
“The wider range of growth rates coincides with a mix of positive, negative, and rate-neutral filings across the market,” the report states.
Michigan led all states in Q3 with 7% shopping growth, followed by New Jersey (6.8%), Connecticut (6.6%), Georgia (6.6%), and Nevada (6.2%).
Lost policies account for 18% of active policies annually, according to the report. It adds that nearly 30% of the lost policies exit the market and about 70% remain active.
“The active cohort either switches carriers, returns to the original carrier or moves from having dual coverage to a single insurer,” according to the report.
Overall, switching rose from 49% in 2024 to 53% in 2026, and market exits declined from 32% to 39%, the report states.

“First-year policyholders are a particularly vulnerable segment,” the report states. “They represent 40% of lost policies and more than 50% of market exits. Among these policyholders, switching increased from 35% to 42%, and exits fell from 44% to 38%.”
It adds that this could point to a retention cliff at first renewal or a lack of policyholder loyalty, consumer price sensitivity, or continued active engagement in shopping.

“Third quarter trends remained consistent with what the market experienced in the first half of the year,” the report states. “Shopping and switching remain at record highs, and while growth in each has slowed, volumes continue to reach higher levels. The fourth quarter typically experiences a shopping lull; however, against a backdrop of consumer affordability pressures, the prevalence of AI and the onset of agentic shopping, the market may once again buck that trend.”
Feature and embedded graphs courtesy of LexisNexis.

articles.title: Shops raise concerns over Allstate ADAS calibration pricing practices
articles.author: Lurah Lowery

paras.en: Collision repair shops have raised concerns that Allstate and National General are limiting ADAS calibration payments based on information from Kinetic, a software and robotics company.

A shop owner and Repairer Driven News reader who preferred not to use their name told RDN that after posting their thoughts on the subject on an online forum, several other shops shared similar experiences. The reader said they personally questioned Allstate, in part, on behalf of a body shop they sublet for.
RDN attempted to reach Allstate several times with questions, but the company didn’t respond.

“Allstate basically said, ‘We’re not paying the calibration prices,’ and then they updated the RO with the pricing,” the anonymous reader said. “I’m like, ‘Wow, that looks kind of low, not terrible, but it’s lower than what I typically see.'”
They added that after providing Allstate with documentation to support the operations, the insurer continued pushing the reimbursement prices they wanted to pay, then mentioned Kinetic.
They provided an Oct. 12 email from an Allstate Claims Division representative:

The reader likened Allstate’s pricing with Kinetic to following direct repair program terms without actually being in a DRP. They said: “They’re not just dictating what calibrations need to be done. They shouldn’t do that. Now, they’re dictating pricing.”
Emails provided by other RDN readers also show similar instances occurring:
Documents shared with RDN from repair facilities show that reports Allstate provided to them list Allstate Insurance Company as the customer.

RDN spoke to Kinetic CEO and co-founder Nikhil Naikal. While he wouldn’t share specific information related to Kinetic’s relationship with Allstate, Naikal wanted to emphasize Kinetic doesn’t set insurer calibration pricing, and said Kinetic ID, his company’s ADAS calibration identification software, “is intended to support and not replace the repair professional’s evaluation of that vehicle and any applicable OEM procedures.”

“We follow OEM procedures, so what we help the user that is using the software do is to interpret the OEM calibration requirements, not override them, but to interpret them based on the repair estimate that they’ve already written,” he said. “Our data comes from technical resources like OEM documentation and I-CAR and places like that. Our software is a tool to help repair professionals identify the necessary procedures. It is not a substitute for OEM repair documentation or any professional judgment of the repairer or the repair facility.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Naikal added that insurance carriers set their own pricing.

“When we receive that specific insurance pricing, we program that into our system, so it’s not our pricing,” he said. “We are not setting insurance pricing. We are a tiny company that has no say in pricing decisions. We are just following the pricing that the carriers are determining themselves if they choose to disclose it to us.”
Naikal explained that Kinetic ID provides a technical assessment based on vehicle information and repair operations that are available at the time of the analysis.

“If a repair facility identifies additional requirements supported by OEM documentation, those findings should be considered as part of the repair assessment,” he said. “Kinetic’s technical conclusion can be reviewed when additional repair information becomes available. The decisions regarding any sort of reimbursement, be it from an insurer or charging a customer who’s paying out of pocket, they’re made by the payer, not by Kinetic. The applicable payer determines the process for reviewing and disputing any payment decisions. That has nothing to do with Kinetic.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: He added that the software produces the same output, regardless of who the user is, whether that’s a repairer, an insurer, or a consumer.

“We are not implementing different hierarchies or decision profiles on what the software produces and then output based on who the user is; it’s one uniform user,” Naikal said. “We are not in cahoots with anyone. We are an independent company that’s trying to do our best to make repairs safer.”
If the software deviates from what shops are seeing, Naikal said context can be added to explain why repairers think the software is wrong, and the software will consider it and reevaluate.
When asked, Naikal did confirm that Allstate Strategic Ventures has invested in Kinetic.

In June 2024, Kinetic said in a press release that it was “pleased to have received strategic investments from the venture arms of Liberty Mutual Insurance and Allstate Insurance.” The release says Kinetic received $21 million in Series B funding, but doesn’t share how much came from Allstate and Liberty Mutual.
There is also a website with an Allstate-specific Kinetic login. Naikal wouldn’t confirm to RDN that Allstate has a unique Kinetic profile.
“I cannot talk about individual commercial relationships between Kinetic and any customer at this time,” he said.
RDN readers have also told us about a separate industry issue involving Allstate, and the company hasn’t returned our request for information.
In September, an Allstate Good Hands Repair Network (GHRN) senior damage consultant emailed a group of repair facilities directing them to bill 0.5 mechanical hours for pre- and post-scans:

A document attached to the email establishes the payment methodology but also states GHRN facilities should determine the need for scanning on a case-by-case basis, considering vehicle age, damage, ADAS equipment, restraint deployment, and vehicle-specific OEM procedures.

The document also states, “Allstate expects our Good Hands Repair Network facilities to maintain up-to-date vehicle scanning equipment capable of scanning most vehicles, including those requiring OE licensed data across multiple vehicle brands.”
Allstate’s basis for specifying a set limit on mechanical hours is unclear. RDN’s several attempts to reach Allstate were unreturned.

articles.title: Autel Expands Nissan Diagnostic and ADAS Access
articles.author: ImportCar Staff Writers

paras.en: Autel U.S. has released diagnostic and ADAS software updates for Nissan vehicles using the Consult 4 platform. The updates expand bidirectional control and ADAS calibration access across supported North American vehicles.
The Nissan diagnostic software is available on supported MaxiSYS Ultra and Ultra S2 tablets. ADAS calibration capability is available on these tablets with ADAS calibration software installed.
Available functions depend on the vehicle and system. They include ECU information, code reading and clearing, live data, Active Tests and ADAS calibration procedures.

Supported Autel tablets access protected vehicle functions through AutoAuth. The independent service works with manufacturers and aftermarket tool providers to verify shops, technicians and tools for secure vehicle access.
Authenticated Access for Newer Nissan Platforms

Nissan began incorporating security-gateway protections into select North American vehicles with the 2020 model year. These protections restrict designated bidirectional functions unless the technician, shop and diagnostic tool receive proper authentication.
Autel has offered AutoAuth-based Nissan security-gateway access for several years. The access applies to vehicles supported by Nissan’s Consult-III plus diagnostic platform.
Nissan introduced its newer web-based Consult 4 diagnostic software for the 2023 Nissan Ariya. The automaker now uses the software on a growing number of newer vehicle platforms.
Supporting protected functions required Autel to develop and validate a compatible authorization process. The process works with the vehicles’ newer electronic architectures.
Autel’s new capability expands diagnostic and ADAS calibration access across supported Nissan vehicles using Consult 4.
Available functions depend on the vehicle and system. They include ECU information, code reading and clearing, live data, Active Tests and ADAS calibration procedures.
North American Nissan vehicles using Consult 4 include:
- 2025 and newer Nissan Kicks, Murano, Pathfinder and Armada
Autel issued the expanded capabilities through the Nissan_V7.40 diagnostic software and Nissan_ADAS V5.20 software released on Sept. 9.
Access requires an active Autel software subscription and an active AutoAuth account for Nissan access. ADAS calibration also requires applicable Autel software, equipment, targets and accessories.
Supported Consult 4 vehicle coverage does not require a separate AutoAuth service tier. Eligible users can obtain the software releases through the standard update process on their Autel tablet.

articles.title: The Downside of Regenerative Braking
articles.author: Joe Keene

paras.en: Regenerative braking allows electric vehicles to recover energy during deceleration. Instead of converting all vehicle momentum into heat at the brake rotors, the electric motor acts as a generator. This slows the vehicle while returning some energy to the battery.
The process can significantly reduce the use of conventional friction brakes. However, reduced brake usage can also create maintenance challenges involving corrosion and component operation.
On conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, brake pads regularly contact the rotors during braking. This friction helps remove light surface corrosion from the rotor faces.
EVs with aggressive regenerative braking may use their friction brakes less frequently. Exposure to moisture, road salt and humidity can then allow corrosion to develop on the rotor surfaces.
EV Regenerative Braking and Rotor Corrosion
Light surface rust is not necessarily a problem because normal brake applications can remove it. However, corrosion can progress when friction brakes are not used regularly.
Over time, heavier rust, pitting and scaling can develop on the rotors. Once the rotor surfaces deteriorate significantly, normal brake applications may not restore their condition.
Reduced friction brake usage can also extend brake pad life. However, brake components can develop problems unrelated to friction material wear.

Corrosion may form around brake pad hardware, caliper brackets, slide pins and other components. Pads can become restricted in their brackets, while caliper components may develop problems from limited movement.
As a result, brake components may require replacement because of corrosion or restricted movement rather than normal wear.
How Regenerative and Friction Braking Work Together
Electric vehicles still require conventional hydraulic friction brakes to maintain stopping performance.

Regenerative braking may become reduced or unavailable under certain operating conditions. These include a fully charged battery, very cold battery temperatures, vehicle stability control intervention or certain system faults.
EV braking systems blend regenerative braking with conventional hydraulic friction braking to provide the stopping performance drivers expect.
This makes conventional brake system condition an important consideration, even when regenerative braking reduces normal friction brake usage.
EV Brake Inspection and Maintenance Considerations
Technicians should account for reduced friction brake usage when inspecting electric vehicle braking systems.
Measuring brake pad thickness alone may not provide a complete picture of component condition.

EV regenerative braking improves efficiency by recovering energy and can substantially extend brake pad life. However, reduced friction brake usage can also increase the potential for corrosion and restricted component movement.
Brake condition assessments should account for both friction material wear and the effects of limited brake usage.

articles.title: What Makes the Perfect ADAS Technician?
articles.author: Mitch Becker

paras.en: I was recently asked, “What makes the perfect technician?” Before I could answer, I had to think about whether we were talking about a forward-facing camera specialist in the glass industry, an ADAS technician or a diagnostic technician for vehicle electronics.

Was the person who asked me that question seeking a wish list of skills or a description of what I would want in that person? It really is two trains of thought with a list of variables and bunny trails of conversation to go down no matter who you ask. My answer might be totally different than someone else based on the needs of that person.

I can describe the “unicorn” technician who knows everything, or I can describe the work ethic of someone who will be a diamond in the rough. The factor I personally look at is what’s ahead for the automotive repair industry, not where the industry is today. The perfect technician in my mind will adapt to change as it happens.

As I started writing this article, I started thinking of the things a technician needs to be successful and how to “build” or develop that technician’s abilities — a key factor. Do you find an already-built model technician, or do you build your own and develop him or her to be the best technician? Then you must address whether or not you hire experience or if you have the time and commitment to develop that person into a technician or team and dedicate resources to keep training them and keep moving with new technology? It’s a dilemma that many shops and companies face in the repair industry today. If hiring experience is the course you take, then I hope you remember the one thing that will be a constant throughout all of the industry: change. Also, no one knows it all.

paras.en: The first thing I observe when I see a technician who’s successful or a technician who wants to be successful is the ability or desire to constantly learn. As the changes continue in vehicle electronics, a technician will need to adapt to all the changes we’ve experienced, plus the change we’ll be dealing with in the future. This will require constant learning through reading, training and research. The minute you stop learning and adapting, you start falling behind. This goes hand-in-hand with the ability to solve problems through challenges. The learning constantly being gained gives a solid base of knowledge to draw from when challenges and “situations” arise that complicate repairs and/or calibrations.

paras.en: The technician who’s constantly learning also follows all the processes correctly without taking shortcuts or cutting corners. Recognizing the importance of doing all the steps and processes every time not only provides consistent results but improves diagnostic capabilities and speed in parsing through the multiple causes of, say, a failed calibration to determine the root cause. Those technicians who are not following all the processes and steps will find themselves in quicksand very easily trying to find out why repairs or calibrations are failing to complete.

paras.en: Being a good partner versus merely providing a service to a customer helps a technician actually build a career and grow opportunities within the company. A technician can have all the talent in the world, but if he or she does not understand the customers’ needs, that potential will be limited — and the customers’ business will be negatively affected.

This is also where work ethic comes into play. Being on time and keeping commitments means a great deal to a customer and builds trust that serves both the technician and customer well. This is the start of both the technician and the company establishing a good reputation. If you’re the best technician but not dependable, this creates a counterproductive situation for all. Having the right mindset and also understanding the customer provides a foundation for the technician that’s priceless in the repair industry; the rest is skills and experience needed to do the job.

paras.en: I already mentioned that following the OEM procedures is a key factor for all successful technicians. But there are other pieces of knowledge that all level of vehicle electronics technicians must have to do the tasks required. For example, an understanding of:
Add to this a variety of competencies needed depending on the level of technician needed. These competencies can be broken down into a multitude of skills for a technician:
- Navigating aftermarket and OE software
- Establishing and measuring geometric angles

When you add all this together, you get a technician who will perform at an optimum level and grow him- or herself and your business. This technician will be dependable and will be appreciated by employer and customer alike.

This is a hard business, given that you have to keep up with all the changes in every make and model of vehicle out there. The diagnostic technician position is not for everyone. We’ve all seen companies and individuals who talk a big game but fall short when called upon to perform.
Without the kind of foundation I mentioned that a technician needs, you end up with an interesting situation.

I see all the new equipment being produced that makes it easier and somewhat faster to perform operations such as calibrations with consistency and accuracy. I think that is great, to a point. But what happens when the vehicle fails to calibrate with this equipment? Who will be the one figuring out what’s wrong or doing the diagnostics on the situation? For the work being done, do you need a diagnostic technician or, if you’re in the glass industry, do you need a forward-facing camera specialist? The difference would be in the competencies and skills needed for the position. Collision-industry level of skills would be different than for the auto glass or mechanical industry. Mechanical-industry level would be different than the collision industry, depending on shop services provided.

paras.en: These different levels of technician are interesting angles on what a technician needs in terms of competencies but also in the level of training and experience required to do the tasks and/or job required. I’ve seen where ASE is addressing this with different levels of certification for technicians, which I fully support. ASE is breaking down the levels to a certification for the glass industry for forward-facing cameras, ADAS calibration technicians and diagnostic technicians. This to me shows a career path for potential technicians in all aspects of the repair industry, be it collision or mechanical (either light-duty or heavy-duty).

paras.en: The Auto Glass Safety Council (AGSC) is offering a certification for forward-facing calibration technicians in the auto glass industry. This is exciting, as a new career path is definitely growing in the auto glass repair industry, bringing in new people and a whole new interest. I also want to give SkillsUSA a shout-out, as there is talk of creating a competition at its state-level and national events for diagnostic technicians.

This diagnostic technician repair path, no matter what level, is a mentally and physically challenging career. Having the correct mindset and developing the knowledge foundation will certainly help a technician build his or her skills and develop all the competencies required for a solid career. This will also develop good problem-solving skills, which will be highly respected and coveted by all as experience is gained.

A technician can be taught a lot of the skills needed and will become what you teach; a technician who has the right mindset and desire to learn will be more than what you taught. As a shop manager or owner, it’s wise to listen to your technicians and encourage them to learn — and pay attention to what they tell you they want to learn. You know what they need for training and to grow their knowledge and skills, but be careful not to dismiss requests you may feel are not relevant to position. Keeping technicians interested in learning and encouraging technicians on what they want to learn helps create the mindset you want.

articles.title: Giti Tire Names Michael Markoff Chief Operating Officer
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: Giti Tire USA has promoted Michael Markoff to chief operating officer, effective Nov. 1. The appointment comes as the company launches the Giti brand in the U.S. and builds on momentum for its GT Radial brand. Markoff previously served as executive vice president of sales and marketing. He reports to Dr. Enki Tan, executive chairman of Giti Tire.
In his expanded role, Markoff oversees sales, marketing, logistics, supply chain, technical service, industry relations and product development.

“I am honored to take on this role and build on the strong foundation our team has established,” said Markoff. “I look forward to working with our employees, customers, and partners to strengthen our operations, enhance customer service, and support Giti Tire USA’s continued growth.

During an exclusive interview at the SEMA Show, Markoff discussed his 29 years in the tire industry, including 26 with Goodyear in R&D, marketing and sales roles in the U.S. and Europe. He has also spent more than two years with Giti Tire.
“Moving from head of sales and marketing into chief operating officer [has] been an exciting opportunity,” he said. “We have a very strong team and we’re excited about the future.”

The promotion is part of a planned leadership transition. Phang Wai Yeen, formerly chief executive officer of Giti Tire’s North American operations, will now lead global research and development activities.
Read the full article on tirereview.com.

articles.title: SEMA Names Ryan Mascoli Chief Operations Officer
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: The Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) has named Ryan Mascoli chief operations officer (COO), effective Nov. 16. Mascoli brings more than 15 years of experience in operational strategy, business transformation and growth within manufacturing and supply chain organizations.
Reporting to SEMA CEO Mike Spagnola, he will oversee day-to-day operations and advance strategic initiatives. He also will align teams and resources with the association’s long-term priorities.

“Ryan is a proven operational leader who understands how to translate strategy into measurable results,” said Spagnola. “His experience will strengthen our executive team and help SEMA operate with greater alignment, accountability and effectiveness. By improving how we work across the organization, we will be better positioned to deliver meaningful value to our members and foster the success of the automotive aftermarket.”
SEMA Appointee Brings Manufacturing and Operations Experience

Mascoli most recently served as vice president of operations for Advanced Charging Technologies, leading enterprise operations across manufacturing, supply chain and production. During his tenure, the company grew revenue from $25 million to $60 million while maintaining a 99.6% on-time delivery rate.

He also increased daily production output by 25% and reduced order dwell time from 21 days to two days. Additionally, he led a companywide enterprise resource planning implementation that took three months to complete.
Previously, Mascoli served as general manager and COO at ICE Cable Systems. He oversaw finance, sales, supply chain, marketing, information technology and human resources.
From 2019 to 2021, the company grew revenue from $10 million to $22 million. It also increased profit from $200,000 to $3.7 million.
Earlier in his career, he held supply chain and inventory leadership positions at ICE Cable Systems and Toshiba.
Mascoli to Oversee Strategic Initiatives

“SEMA plays a vital role in creating the conditions for aftermarket businesses and professionals to succeed,” said Mascoli. “I look forward to working with SEMA’s leadership, staff, board and members to strengthen operations, execute strategic priorities and deliver greater value to the industry.”
As COO, Mascoli will establish performance measures, support annual planning and budgeting, improve organizational processes and help manage operational risks.

He also will work with department leaders to support employee development. Additionally, he will align organizational priorities with SEMA’s mission to foster the success of the automotive aftermarket.
Mascoli studied business administration with an emphasis in management at California State University, Fullerton.

articles.title: YANG Launches 2027 Mentorship Program
articles.author: Jeff White

paras.en: The Young Auto Care Network Group (YANG), a community of the Auto Care Association, recently launched its 2027 YANG Mentorship Program. Now in its fifth year, the program averages 125 mentees and 24 volunteer mentors annually. Anyone under age 40 who joins the YANG community can participate for free.

“One of the most valuable aspects of my involvement with YANG has been the relationships I’ve built with individuals who genuinely challenge me to grow, both personally and professionally,” said Brandon Crenshaw, chair, YANG. “The Mentorship Program creates an opportunity to go beyond networking, by building meaningful connections, challenging your own perspectives, and developing the confidence and perspective to lead in new ways. It’s an experience I encourage every young professional in our industry to embrace.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Each YANG mentee will rank industry-specific topics by preference to form mentorship circles. Examples of topics include:
- Navigating change, building influence and earning your seat at the table
- Standing out and the importance of networking
Each mentorship circle consists of approximately five mentees and one mentor focused on a unique topic.

Organizers will assign groups after registration closes Nov. 30. Participants will then join the YANG Mentorship Program kickoff meeting in January 2027. Each mentorship circle will meet once per quarter throughout 2027. The program runs from January through December 2027.

The YANG Mentorship Program aims to help mentees experience all three YANG pillars: networking, professional development and giving back. Through this small-group mentorship program, mentees will benefit from the experience of automotive aftermarket veterans.

The program targets young automotive aftermarket professionals who want to advance their careers. It provides opportunities for members to focus on individual professional goals while developing the skills to become future leaders.

articles.title: NAPA Opens First Highly Automated Reverse Logistics Center
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: NAPA recently celebrated the grand opening of its York Reverse Logistics Center (RLC), marking the debut of the first highly automated facility of its kind within the NAPA network and an important milestone in the company’s ongoing supply chain transformation.

The 400,000-square-foot center combines more than 100 robots and advanced automation technology with a skilled local workforce to process returns, cores and inventory for redistribution across the NAPA Northeast distribution network.

The center began operations earlier this year and is designed to accelerate returns processing, helping get parts back into inventory faster and improving availability for NAPA stores, repair professionals and their customers, the company said. The new facility, which can support 250,000 unique SKUs, is expected to reduce the time needed to prepare inventory for redistribution by 43% and support inventory accuracy up to 99.5%.

Leaders from NAPA and corporate parent Genuine Parts Company (GPC) were joined by York Mayor Sandie Walker, state and local elected officials, the York County Economic Alliance, community partners and teammates for a ribbon-cutting ceremony and tours of the facility at 500 Willow Springs Lane.

“York is the first step in a broader modernization of the NAPA supply chain,” said Justin Ducharme, executive vice president, supply chain, NAPA. “By combining innovative technology with the expertise of our teammates, we’re creating a more efficient operation that helps keep parts moving to the customers and repair professionals who rely on us every day.”

During the ceremony, the GPC Foundation presented a $2,500 Good Neighbor grant to United Way of York County. The grant supports the foundation’s mobility priority and reflects a shared belief that reliable transportation opens access to jobs, health care and stronger family life.

As the first highly automated reverse logistics center within the NAPA network, RLC represents an important milestone in the company’s efforts to enhance operational capabilities and support the growing needs of customers across the Northeast, the company said.

articles.title: Advance Auto Parts Foundation Awards 24 Scholarships
articles.author: Mary DellaValle

paras.en: The Advance Auto Parts Foundation today announced the recipients of its 2026 scholarship program, awarding 24 scholarships to students pursuing higher education. The annual program helps family members of Advance Auto Parts team members continue their education and work toward earning degrees.

This year’s recipients stood out for their academic achievement, leadership, community involvement, personal accomplishments and future goals. Each student will receive a one-time scholarship of $3,500 to support their education.

“Supporting our team members also means supporting their families, and we’re proud to recognize these students and their achievements,” said Anthony Sarlanis, president of the Advance Auto Parts Foundation and senior vice president, professional at Advance Auto Parts. “Their hard work and dedication have earned this recognition, and we’re proud to help them take the next step in their education. We congratulate each recipient and look forward to seeing all they accomplish in the years ahead.”
The 2026 scholarship recipients and the schools they’re attending:

articles.title: An Anthropic mathematician claims to have proven the Riemann hypothesis. We have to rethink how we reward expertise.
articles.author: Kit Yates

paras.en: An Anthropic mathematician using Claude claims to have proven the most famous problem in math — the Riemann hypothesis — in the latest, but potentially most consequential, example of artificial intelligence (AI) producing stunning math results.

AI has steamrolled its way into the math community. Anthropic's proof will certainly and rightly be scrutinized, but rather than picking apart every single result these models produce, we should respond by changing how we evaluate and reward expertise — placing less weight on the volume of results and more on the human judgment required to decide which questions and answers matter.
Without this shift, we risk drowning genuine insight in a flood of plausible but poorly understood mathematics.

Mathematical judgment is the ability to distinguish a result that is correct, but boring, from one that might fundamentally change how we think about the problem or even the whole area of mathematics surrounding the problem.

AI could generate hundreds of thousands of complex variations on a theorem, but these variations might add very little to mathematical knowledge, each one ultimately proving a dead end. A truly consequential result might settle a long-standing unsolved problem or connect to apparently unrelated areas. It is mathematical judgment that allows us to tell the difference between the two.

Earlier this year, an OpenAI system produced a counterexample to the long-standing planar unit distance problem, overturning a conjecture of Paul Erdős that had resisted mathematicians for decades. More recently, OpenAI announced an apparent solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, a celebrated question about whether equations describing fluid flow can develop singularities, or infinite values. It is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute's Millennium Prize Problems — a set of seven well-known and complex math problems, each with a $1 million prize attached.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Whether OpenAI's result ultimately stands up to scrutiny remains to be seen. But what is clear is that AI systems are now operating at a level that many mathematicians did not expect to witness for years, if not decades. OpenAI has since released hundreds of further mathematical results, leaving mathematicians scrambling to assess their correctness and significance.

This does not mean that mathematicians are about to become obsolete. But it does mean we need to carefully reconsider what their precise purpose is.

Traditionally, expertise has been closely associated with production: Experts solve difficult problems, prove theorems, construct models and write papers. If AI can generate proofs, conjectures and probe research areas at unprecedented speed and scale, mathematical production is no longer necessarily the bottleneck. Instead, many pure mathematicians would argue that it is mathematical judgment that will become the scarcer resource.

Human judgment remains necessary because proofs generated by AI are not necessarily illuminating, comprehensible or even reliable. Some proofs may be so long or opaque that checking them requires substantial work by specialists and even more work to reinterpret them in a way that is meaningful to human mathematicians.

A proof can be valid without offering insight into why it is true or how its ideas might be employed elsewhere. The job of human mathematicians will be to become arbiters of the correctness of proofs, but also to scrutinize the reasoning and to extract the underlying ideas, determining whether the result says anything that meaningfully advances the field.

Mathematics, as a research community, needs to react rapidly to this change. Mathematicians and journals must prioritize significance over output. Mathematics involves deciding which results are important as well as generating them. A proof can be correct without being insightful. To give a simplified example, AI might "prove" that the square of a number divisible by two is divisible by four and then prove that the square of a number divisible by three is divisible by nine, and so on with ever larger integers. However, each new "proof" isn't an example of insightful mathematics, just a variation on the same elementary idea.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In contrast, a significant proof might settle a long-standing question, reveal an unexpected connection between disparate fields or develop a technique which is useful in the solution of many other problems.

Journals should therefore require authors to explain clearly what is genuinely new, why it matters — and what role AI played. Reviewers should judge whether a result deepens understanding, rather than merely verifying that the argument works. That does not mean rejecting work whose eventual importance is uncertain. The history of mathematics is full of ideas whose significance became apparent only decades later, so journals must continue to make room for foundational, exploratory and curiosity-driven research.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: But there is a difference between a result with as-yet unknown implications and one that is unlikely ever to be insightful. Mathematical judgement cannot guarantee that nothing valuable is ever overlooked. It can, however, distinguish work that contains genuinely new ideas or possibilities from the automated production of uninteresting dead ends.

Universities and funders should also stop treating publication counts as a convenient proxy for quality. Careers are built around papers, citations, grants and prizes, but these measures were developed when producing sophisticated mathematics demanded substantial human time and effort. In the age of AI, work that might previously have taken years of careful thought could now be produced in weeks or even days.

Consequently, as the cost of generating mathematical results falls dramatically, those measures of quality become less useful. A decreased reliance on traditional metrics may be no bad thing, but institutions need credible alternatives: assessments of a researcher's most important contributions, evidence of intellectual leadership and explanations of how their work has changed understanding. This is urgent because mathematicians are already struggling to evaluate the sheer volume of material being produced.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Finally, mathematical training must continue to reward understanding. Written work alone will become a less reliable guide to individual capability when papers, reports and applications can be written mostly using AI. Seminars, discussions and collaborations can reveal whether someone understands an argument, can defend it and can connect it to other ideas. Demonstrating understanding has always been a more important quality in university students than simply presenting the answer; education and recruitment should now reflect that principle more explicitly.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - AI is solving 'impossible' math problems. Can it best the world's top mathematicians?
- 'Everything we know about space travel is going to change within a decade': The fusion breakthrough that could unlock a path to the stars
- 'Why would you ruin your career?': OpenAI claims to have cracked one of math's greatest unsolved problems, but mathematicians allege it played dirty

Critics might argue that this is an overreaction. Mathematical claims still require proof, peer review already evaluates significance, and AI is simply another tool, like a calculator or computer algebra system. There is a degree of truth to each objection. Yet the explosion in the number of published papers changes the nature of the game. A calculator does not generate hundreds of research claims that specialists must spend precious time checking. AI can create arguments faster than the community can verify, interpret or absorb them. Existing safeguards were not designed for that imbalance.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Recent advances have understandably generated both excitement and anxiety. The right response is neither to reject AI nor to unguardedly celebrate every finding it produces. Journals, universities and funders should adapt their incentives now, before quantity overwhelms judgment completely.

In an environment increasingly capable of automatically generating research-level mathematics, the most valuable experts will be those who know which questions are worth asking, which results deserve trust and which ideas are worth our attention.

articles.title: James Webb telescope spots giant star swallowing its companion in first-ever observations of a stellar merger
articles.author: Joanna Thompson

paras.en: For the first time, astronomers have caught two stars — a supergiant and a star slightly smaller than the sun — in the act of merging. After orbiting each other for thousands of years, the pair came together in just under seven years — a span short enough that researchers could watch the drama play out from start to finish. The discovery was described in a study published Nov. 18 in the journal Nature.

"Stellar mergers are very, very difficult to observe in real time because they are hard to predict," Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University and first author of the study, said in a NASA statement. "However, we noticed something unusual was going on in 2023 and continued to monitor the system to see what it would do."

The stars' imminent merger was originally picked up by NASA's now-retired Near-Earth Object Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer — a spacecraft that was designed to spot asteroids but also discovered many other interesting changes in the night sky.

Researchers noticed that a previously stable binary star system in the Andromeda galaxy, the closest major galaxy to ours, had begun to brighten. Follow-up observations from the Wide-Field Infrared Transient Explorer — a near-infrared instrument at the Palomar Observatory in California — revealed that the galaxy had also started spewing dust. Karambelkar’s team backed up these observations with data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) in December 2025.

The researchers dubbed the binary pair "Bao" (after its formal name, AT 2025abao) and started keeping tabs. They found that sometime in 2018, the smaller component of Bao bumped into the surface of the supergiant Bao. From there, things escalated quickly. The stars started exchanging gas in a process known as common envelope evolution. The larger Bao dragged its smaller companion closer and closer, until it was finally sucked into the supergiant's core, releasing a gigantic burst of energy.
- 'A collision within a collision': Neutron star merger hiding in mini-galaxy could answer 2 big astrophysics questions
- Universe-shaking collision of black hole and neutron star could upend our understanding of monster cosmic mergers
- Never-before-seen 'strange quark star' may have formed after cosmic collision, physicists say
This dramatic culmination was "almost like a bomb exploding inside a living star," study co-author Kishalay De, an astronomer at Columbia University, said in the statement.

The researchers were surprised by not only the speed of this interaction but also its outcome. Bao could have easily exploded into a supernova, transformed into a neutron star or collapsed into a black hole. Instead, it seems to have settled back into a single massive star. Future observations will give scientists a sense of how the new, rejuvenated Bao is holding up after its act of cosmic cannibalism.

The team's analysis could also help inform future studies of supergiant stars and binary systems. Getting a clearer picture of how common envelope evolution works could allow astronomers to reconstruct how previous mergers went down. Thanks to NASA's new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, Karambelkar predicts Bao will be far from the last merging stars scientists spot.

Joanna Thompson is a science journalist and runner based in New York. She holds a B.S. in Zoology and a B.A. in Creative Writing from North Carolina State University, as well as a Master's in Science Journalism from NYU's Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program. Find more of her work in Scientific American, The Daily Beast, Atlas Obscura or Audubon Magazine.

articles.title: Waterfall of fog spills over Mallorca cliffs in stunning winning image for Weather Photographer of the Year 2026
articles.author: Elise Poore

paras.en: The first light of dawn illuminates a sea of fog spilling over the rugged cliffs of Mallorca, Spain, in this year's winning Weather Photographer of the Year 2026 image. Photographer Francisco Bailón Rodríguez captured the scene from the Albercutz Watchtower, looking toward the Formentor Peninsula, after several days of high pressure and humid nights created the perfect conditions for fog to blanket the landscape.

On Nov. 17, the photograph, titled "Mares de Niebla (Seas of Fog)," was named overall winner of the Royal Meteorological Society's competition, which attracted more than 5,500 entries from photographers around the world.

The competition celebrates the ephemeral scenes created by weather, which can for brief moments transform landscapes into something extraordinary. Take a look at this year's winning photographs below and let us know your favorites in the comments.

Photographer Weilu Chen took second place in the main category with this spectacular image of golden light shining over the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge that runs for 34 miles (55 kilometers) across the Pearl River estuary in southern China.
"A Supercell in the Sandhills of Nebraska"

A striking bolt of lightning illuminates a horizontal cloud during a thunderstorm, earning third place in the main category. These clouds are called arcus clouds that have a distinct shelf-like shape. "Mother Nature was kind enough to give us a supercell and lightning at night," photographer Laura Hedien said in a statement.
"Misty Sunrise over the Long Coc Tea Hills"
Photographer Mahmudul Hasan won first place in the public vote category for this image of the rolling tea hills of Long Coc, Vietnam, emerging through layers of mist.
Watching from Bayonne, New Jersey, photographer Dan Martland captured this triple lightning strike above New York City, earning second place in the public vote category.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
Photographer Aung Soe Min captured the Kuthodaw Pagoda emerging through the morning mist in Myanmar, as the sunrise light filters through the trees in this winning mobile category image.
Photographer Anthony Bird took second place in the mobile category with this spectacular rainbow stretching across Loch Duck in the Scottish Highlands.
Climate-award winning photographer Erfan Samanfar shot this haunting image of a farmer trying to protect his farmland from a raging fire in Marvdasht, Iran, in 2025.
Earning second place in the climate award category, photographer Andres Miraglia captured the moment a floating iceberg was seen in the sunset off Antarctica's Paradise Harbor.
Elise studied marine biology at the University of Portsmouth in the U.K. She has worked as a freelance journalist focusing on the aquatic realm.

articles.title: For the First Time, Astronomers Witnessed a Giant Star Gobble Up Its Smaller Stellar Companion

paras.en: In 2023, astronomers realized that a red giant star in our neighboring Andromeda galaxy was doing something strange. Sure enough, two years later, the astronomical object exploded.

The researchers rushed to observe the phenomenon, and they sifted through older data to piece together what had happened. Analyses suggest the huge star had gobbled up its smaller stellar companion, marking the first direct observation of this kind of star merger. The findings were described November 18 in the journal Nature.

The eruption, called AT 2025abao, occurred because the two stars shared what’s called a common envelope. Some stars approaching the end of their lives balloon to a huge size, entering a giant phase. As an object expands, its outer layer of gas—or envelope—engulfs anything orbiting it, resulting in odd interactions.

However, common envelopes are tough to observe because they happen over relatively short timescales of months to years, and usually, just a few stars exist in this phase at a time within a galaxy, writes Jason Nordhaus, an astrophysicist at the Rochester Institute of Technology who did not participate in the work, in commentary accompanying the study.
Experts estimate that nearly a third of all stars go through a common envelope phase at some point during their lives, reports New Scientist.

To investigate the strange event, which occurred in October 2025, researchers obtained data captured just 47 days later by NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope. They also had follow-up observations from other ground- and space-based instruments, as well as data from roughly the past 30 years, which revealed the big star had started brightening in 2018.

Using all that data, the team was able to “reconstruct what happened with quite significant confidence,” Sven Buder, an astrophysicist at the Australian National University who did not participate in the study, tells the Australian Broadcasting Corporation’s Jacinta Bowler.

Computer simulations hinted that the two stars had orbited each other for millennia. Before the eye-catching explosion, the primary star—dubbed “Big Bao” after the eruption’s name—had become enormous. It was seven times more massive, 350 times the radius and 18,000 times brighter than our sun. Its companion, “Little Bao,” on the other hand, probably contained 0.7 times the mass of our sun and was smaller and fainter.

The smaller star spiraled into the bigger one’s envelope, and the two objects took about seven years to unite, which is quite quick in astronomical terms. The merger occurred when the red giant dragged its companion into its core, resulting in a dramatic event resembling “a bomb exploding inside a living star,” study co-author Kishalay De, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, says in a statement.

“We were able to see all different phases of this process—we were able to see the quiescent system, we were able to see the moment the stars touched each other, we were able to see the inspiral, and we were able to see the big outburst in 2025,” lead author Viraj Karambelkar, also an astrophysicist at Columbia University, tells New Scientist’s Leah Crane. “So we now know how this process works far better than we ever had before.”

Now, however, the system is too dusty for scientists to observe the aftermath directly, and it will likely remain so for years, reports Science News’ Meghan Bartels. In the meantime, Karambelkar says they can work to “catch more of these systems even before they erupt.”

articles.title: Rembrandt's 'Night Watch' Is Teeming With Life. Researchers Reveal a Hidden World of Microbes All Over the Masterpiece

paras.en: For nearly four centuries, viewers have admired the bustling militia figures frozen in oil paint on Rembrandt van Rijn’s 1642 masterpiece, The Night Watch. Now, scientists in Amsterdam have revealed that the iconic canvas is teeming with an invisible, living world of its own.

Researchers from the Rijksmuseum and ARTIS-Micropia (which claims to be the world’s only museum dedicated to microbes) are collecting 60 samples from 10 different areas of the painting to catalog its surface microbiome. Early laboratory cultures have turned up myriads of common bacteria and one puzzling outlier: Microbacterium saccharophilum, a bacterial species first identified in 2013 at a sugar refinery in Japan.

“This is the first time The Night Watch, or any work of art, has been analyzed in this way, and we’ve found bacteria that appear on human skin and in soil, and are even associated with plants,” Eline van Bloois, a microbiologist at Artis-Micropia tells El País’ Isabel Ferrer.

The ongoing investigation is featured in “The Night Watch Lives,” an exhibition at ARTIS-Micropia running through May 2027. Centered around a life-size reproduction of Rembrandt’s painting marked with numbered sampling dates, the display showcases living bacterial colonies growing inside glass-encased Petri dishes.
“To get that close to the painting was very scary,” van Bloois tells Hyperallergic's Noëlle de Leeuw. “After all, it's a piece of art that is so well-known to so many people.”

The microbial census forms a new chapter of “Operation Night Watch,” the Rijksmuseum’s sweeping research and conservation initiative launched in 2019. Inside a glass chamber in the museum’s Gallery of Honor, conservators are currently working in full view of visitors to painstakingly remove a yellowed layer of varnish applied in the 1970s. It’s a delicate process, using organic-fabric gauze, small tissues and tiny amounts of solvent that will take years to complete.

Decades before Dutch microbiologist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first described microorganisms in the 1670s, Rembrandt was already using chemistry to protect his work against microscopic threats. Previous Operation Night Watch analyses revealed that Rembrandt had applied a layer of lead-laden oil beneath the primer to shield the painting from moisture and mold in Amsterdam’s damp buildings. The canvas was later trimmed in 1715 to fit inside Amsterdam City Hall and has suffered numerous conservation treatments and deep cleanings roughly once every 50 years.
