paras.en: The findings, published in Science Advances, suggest a promising new direction for treating obesity, diabetes, and fatty liver disease. The experimental compound also appeared to enhance the benefits of popular weight-loss medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy when the treatments were used together. However, its effectiveness and safety have not yet been established in humans.
paras.zh: 发表在《科学进展》上的研究结果为治疗肥胖、糖尿病和脂肪肝疾病提出了一个有希望的新方向。当 Ozempic 和 Wegovy 等流行减肥药物一起使用时，该实验化合物似乎还可以增强这些药物的功效。然而，其在人类中的有效性和安全性尚未确定。

paras.en: A Different Approach to Weight Loss Than Ozempic
paras.zh: 与 Ozempic 不同的减肥方法

paras.en: Over the past five years, medications known as GLP-1 drugs have transformed the treatment of obesity and other metabolic conditions, including diabetes and fatty liver disease. Drugs marketed as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound have helped many patients achieve substantial weight loss while improving their ability to regulate blood sugar.
paras.zh: 在过去的五年里，GLP-1 药物已经改变了肥胖和其他代谢疾病（包括糖尿病和脂肪肝疾病）的治疗方法。以 Ozempic、Wegovy、Mounjaro 和 Zepbound 等商品名销售的药物已帮助许多患者实现了大幅减肥，同时提高了他们调节血糖的能力。

paras.en: Despite these benefits, the medications have important limitations. Nausea and other digestive problems can make treatment difficult for some patients. Because these drugs reduce appetite and food consumption, they can also increase the risk of inadequate nutrition and loss of muscle mass. Over time, losing too much muscle can contribute to weakness, frailty, and other health complications.
paras.zh: 尽管有这些好处，这些药物也有重要的局限性。恶心和其他消化问题可能会给一些患者带来治疗困难。由于这些药物会降低食欲和食物消耗，因此还会增加营养不足和肌肉质量损失的风险。随着时间的推移，失去过多的肌肉会导致虚弱、虚弱和其他健康并发症。

paras.en: Berkeley researchers wanted to investigate a fundamentally different strategy. Rather than focusing on reducing calorie intake, they explored whether it would be possible to increase the amount of energy the body burns.
paras.zh: 伯克利的研究人员想要研究一种完全不同的策略。他们没有专注于减少卡路里摄入量，而是探索是否有可能增加身体燃烧的能量。

paras.en: This process, known as energy expenditure, includes the calories used to maintain basic bodily functions, regulate metabolism, and support everyday activities. Increasing energy expenditure could potentially help people lose weight without relying exclusively on eating less.
paras.zh: 这一过程称为能量消耗，包括用于维持基本身体功能、调节新陈代谢和支持日常活动的卡路里。增加能量消耗可能会帮助人们减肥，而不必完全依赖于少吃。

paras.en: "Body weight responds to two levers: taking in fewer calories, or spending more energy," said Anders Näär, a professor of metabolic biology and nutrition at UC Berkeley and senior author of the study. "GLP-1s work almost entirely on the first, so we went after the second."
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校代谢生物学和营养学教授、该研究的资深作者安德斯·纳尔 (Anders Näär) 表示：“体重受两个因素影响：摄入更少的卡路里，或消耗更多的能量。” “GLP-1 几乎完全对第一个起作用，所以我们追求第二个。”

paras.en: A Compound That Burns Fat While Preserving Muscle
paras.zh: 一种燃烧脂肪同时保护肌肉的化合物

paras.en: The researchers focused on a molecule called 5-tetradecyloxy-2-furoic acid (TOFA), which has an unusual combination of effects on the body's metabolism.
paras.zh: 研究人员重点研究了一种名为 5-十四烷氧基-2-糠酸 (TOFA) 的分子，它对人体的新陈代谢具有不同寻常的综合作用。

paras.en: TOFA interferes with the production of lipids, a broad category of fatty substances that includes cholesterol and triglycerides. These molecules serve important functions, but excessive levels of certain lipids can contribute to metabolic disorders and cardiovascular disease.
paras.zh: TOFA 会干扰脂质的产生，脂质是一类广泛的脂肪物质，包括胆固醇和甘油三酯。这些分子具有重要的功能，但某些脂质含量过高会导致代谢紊乱和心血管疾病。

paras.en: At the same time, TOFA activates genes involved in taking up and burning fat for energy. This combination allows the compound to influence both how the body produces fat and how it uses fat as fuel.
paras.zh: 同时，TOFA 激活参与吸收和燃烧脂肪以获取能量的基因。这种组合使得该化合物能够影响身体如何产生脂肪以及如何使用脂肪作为燃料。

paras.en: In mice, treatment with TOFA produced several encouraging results. The animals became more sensitive to insulin, the hormone that helps move glucose from the bloodstream into cells. Improved insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to control blood sugar, an important benefit for people with diabetes or insulin resistance.
paras.zh: 在小鼠中，TOFA 治疗产生了一些令人鼓舞的结果。这些动物对胰岛素变得更加敏感，胰岛素是一种有助于将葡萄糖从血液转移到细胞中的激素。改善胰岛素敏感性使身体更容易控制血糖，这对于糖尿病或胰岛素抵抗患者来说是一个重要的好处。

paras.en: The compound also lowered triglyceride levels and improved characteristics of fatty liver disease, a condition in which excess fat accumulates inside liver cells and can eventually interfere with liver function.
paras.zh: 该化合物还可以降低甘油三酯水平并改善脂肪肝疾病的特征，脂肪肝疾病是一种过量脂肪在肝细胞内积聚并最终干扰肝功能的疾病。

paras.en: Perhaps most notably, obese mice treated with TOFA lost weight primarily through reductions in body fat, without experiencing significant losses of lean muscle mass. This distinction could be especially valuable because maintaining muscle is important for strength, mobility, and long-term metabolic health.
paras.zh: 也许最值得注意的是，接受 TOFA 治疗的肥胖小鼠主要通过减少体内脂肪来减轻体重，而没有出现瘦肌肉质量的显着损失。这种区别可能特别有价值，因为保持肌肉对于力量、活动能力和长期代谢健康非常重要。

paras.en: How TOFA Increases Energy Burning by 18%
paras.zh: TOFA 如何将能量燃烧提高 18%

paras.en: Although TOFA was originally discovered in the 1970s, the new research uncovered additional properties that could make it particularly useful for treating metabolic disease.
paras.zh: 尽管 TOFA 最初是在 20 世纪 70 年代发现的，但新研究发现了其他特性，使其对治疗代谢疾病特别有用。

paras.en: The compound belongs to a group of substances known as ACC inhibitors. These compounds interfere with enzymes that help the body manufacture fatty acids, effectively slowing the production of certain fats.
paras.zh: 该化合物属于一组称为 ACC 抑制剂的物质。这些化合物会干扰帮助身体制造脂肪酸的酶，有效减缓某些脂肪的产生。

paras.en: Other ACC inhibitors have previously advanced to mid-stage clinical trials, but none has been approved to treat metabolic diseases. One major obstacle has been an unexpected side effect: many of these compounds increase triglycerides in the blood, potentially raising the risk of heart problems.
paras.zh: 其他 ACC 抑制剂此前已进入中期临床试验，但尚未获批用于治疗代谢性疾病。一个主要障碍是意想不到的副作用：许多这些化合物会增加血液中的甘油三酯，可能会增加患心脏病的风险。

paras.en: The Berkeley team discovered that TOFA does more than inhibit ACC. It also activates two cellular receptors called PPARα and PPARδ, which help regulate the genes responsible for fat metabolism.
paras.zh: 伯克利团队发现 TOFA 的作用不仅仅是抑制 ACC。它还激活两种称为 PPARα 和 PPARδ 的细胞受体，这有助于调节负责脂肪代谢的基因。

paras.en: These receptors function as molecular switches. When activated, they stimulate processes that allow cells to absorb fatty acids and break them down to produce energy. In effect, TOFA simultaneously reduces the production of certain fats and encourages the body to burn fat that is already available.
paras.zh: 这些受体起到分子开关的作用。当被激活时，它们会刺激细胞吸收脂肪酸并将其分解以产生能量的过程。实际上，TOFA 同时减少了某些脂肪的产生，并鼓励身体燃烧已有的脂肪。

paras.en: In mice, this activity increased energy expenditure by as much as 18%, without requiring additional physical activity or raising body temperature. Unlike other ACC inhibitors, TOFA also did not cause triglyceride levels to rise, potentially because of its additional effects on fat metabolism.
paras.zh: 在小鼠中，这种活动使能量消耗增加了 18%，而无需额外的体力活动或提高体温。与其他 ACC 抑制剂不同，TOFA 也不会导致甘油三酯水平升高，可能是因为它对脂肪代谢有额外的影响。

paras.en: "TOFA appears to engage a coordinated metabolic response," said study first author Justin Y. Lee, a postdoctoral student at UCSF who conducted the research as a Ph.D. student at Berkeley. "It is not simply blocking lipid synthesis. It is also activating energy expenditure pathways that may help the body handle excess lipid and glucose more effectively."
paras.zh: “TOFA 似乎参与了协调的代谢反应，”该研究的第一作者 Justin Y. Lee 说，他是加州大学旧金山分校的博士后，在博士期间进行了这项研究。伯克利的学生。 “它不仅仅是阻止脂质合成。它还激活能量消耗途径，可以帮助身体更有效地处理过量的脂质和葡萄糖。”

paras.en: To understand whether these effects could be reproduced with separate treatments, the scientists gave mice a combination of two different compounds. One blocked lipid production, while the other stimulated energy expenditure.
paras.zh: 为了了解这些效果是否可以通过单独的治疗来重现，科学家们给小鼠注射了两种不同化合物的组合。一种阻止脂质产生，而另一种则刺激能量消耗。

paras.en: Surprisingly, this two-compound approach was less effective at improving overall metabolic health than TOFA alone. The finding suggests that TOFA's ability to influence multiple metabolic processes through a single molecule may be an important part of its effectiveness.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，这种两种化合物的方法在改善整体代谢健康方面不如单独使用 TOFA 有效。这一发现表明，TOFA 通过单个分子影响多种代谢过程的能力可能是其有效性的重要组成部分。

paras.en: Could TOFA Make Ozempic and Wegovy More Effective?
paras.zh: TOFA 能否使 Ozempic 和 Wegovy 更加有效？

paras.en: The researchers also investigated whether TOFA could improve the results of existing GLP-1 medications.
paras.zh: 研究人员还调查了 TOFA 是否可以改善现有 GLP-1 药物的效果。

paras.en: They tested the compound alongside semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, as well as tirzepatide, which is marketed as Mounjaro and Zepbound.
paras.zh: 他们将该化合物与索马鲁肽（Ozempic 和 Wegovy 的活性成分）以及替泽帕肽（商品名为 Mounjaro 和 Zepbound）一起进行了测试。

paras.en: These medications primarily help people lose weight by reducing appetite and food intake. TOFA, by contrast, targets the other side of the energy balance equation by increasing how much energy the body expends.
paras.zh: 这些药物主要通过减少食欲和食物摄入来帮助人们减肥。相比之下，TOFA 通过增加身体消耗的能量来实现能量平衡方程的另一侧。

paras.en: When the researchers combined TOFA with these medications in mice, the results were more favorable than those produced by either treatment alone. The combinations led to greater improvements in body weight, blood glucose regulation, insulin levels, and triglycerides.
paras.zh: 当研究人员将 TOFA 与这些药物联合用于小鼠时，结果比单独使用任何一种治疗所产生的结果更好。这些组合显着改善了体重、血糖调节、胰岛素水平和甘油三酯。

paras.en: This suggests that treatments targeting calorie intake and energy expenditure could potentially work together to produce stronger metabolic benefits.
paras.zh: 这表明针对卡路里摄入和能量消耗的治疗可能会共同产生更强的代谢益处。

paras.en: "In our combination experiments, TOFA worked additively or synergistically with the GLP-1 appetite-suppressing drugs, so we view it as complementary rather than as a replacement," Näär said.
paras.zh: “在我们的联合实验中，TOFA 与 GLP-1 食欲抑制药物相加或协同作用，因此我们将其视为补充而不是替代，”Näär 说。

paras.en: In other words, the researchers do not necessarily envision TOFA replacing medications such as Ozempic or Wegovy. Instead, it could eventually become an additional treatment that helps address obesity and related metabolic conditions through a different biological mechanism.
paras.zh: 换句话说，研究人员并不一定认为 TOFA 会取代 Ozempic 或 Wegovy 等药物。相反，它最终可能成为一种额外的治疗方法，通过不同的生物机制帮助解决肥胖和相关代谢状况。

paras.en: A Promising Discovery, but Human Trials Are Still Needed
paras.zh: 一个有希望的发现，但仍需要人体试验

paras.en: Despite the encouraging results, the researchers emphasize that TOFA remains an experimental compound. All the findings so far come from animal studies, and scientists have not yet established whether it is safe or effective in humans.
paras.zh: 尽管取得了令人鼓舞的结果，但研究人员强调 TOFA 仍然是一种实验化合物。迄今为止所有的发现都来自动物研究，科学家尚未确定它对人类是否安全或有效。

paras.en: Further research will be necessary to determine whether the same metabolic improvements can be achieved in people and whether the treatment could offer meaningful advantages over existing medications.
paras.zh: 需要进一步的研究来确定是否可以在人体中实现相同的代谢改善，以及该治疗是否可以比现有药物提供有意义的优势。

paras.en: To help move the research toward potential clinical applications, the Berkeley scientists have established a biotechnology company called ReRx Therapeutics. The effort has received support from the university's life sciences entrepreneurship network, including Nucleate and Berkeley SkyDeck.
paras.zh: 为了帮助将研究推向潜在的临床应用，伯克利大学的科学家成立了一家名为 ReRx Therapeutics 的生物技术公司。这项工作得到了该大学生命科学创业网络的支持，包括 Nucleate 和 Berkeley SkyDeck。

paras.en: If the findings eventually translate to humans, TOFA could represent an important addition to the growing range of treatments for obesity and diabetes. By encouraging the body to use more energy while helping preserve muscle, the compound points toward a potentially different way to achieve healthier weight loss.
paras.zh: 如果这些发现最终转化为人类，TOFA 可能会成为日益丰富的肥胖和糖尿病治疗方法的重要补充。通过鼓励身体使用更多能量，同时帮助保护肌肉，该化合物指出了实现更健康减肥的潜在不同方式。

paras.en: The research was funded through discretionary resources provided by UC Berkeley, with additional support from the UCSF Liver Center and the University of Michigan Animal Phenotyping Core.
paras.zh: 该研究由加州大学伯克利分校提供的酌情资源资助，并得到加州大学旧金山分校肝脏中心和密歇根大学动物表型核心的额外支持。

paras.en: Additional authors include Chi Zhu, Melissa A. Boldridge, Rachelle L. Stark, Lei Xu, Federico Gonzalez, Xin Tang, Kaitlyn T. Dang and Kook Son of Berkeley; Gracia Bonilla, Kashish Chetal and Ruslan I. Sadreyev of Massachusetts General Hospital; Kosuke Watari and Michael Karin of the University of California, San Diego; Christina Papa and Bilal N. Sheikh of the Helmholtz Center Munich; Prabha Ibrahim of ReRx Therapeutics.
paras.zh: 其他作者包括伯克利大学的 Chi Zhu、Melissa A. Boldridge、Rachelle L. Stark、Lei Xu、Federico Gonzalez、Xin Tang、Kaitlyn T. Dang 和 Kook Son；马萨诸塞州总医院的 Gracia Bonilla、Kashish Chetal 和 Ruslan I. Sadreyev；加州大学圣地亚哥分校的 Kosuke Watari 和 Michael Karin；慕尼黑亥姆霍兹中心的 Christina Papa 和 Bilal N. Sheikh； ReRx Therapeutics 的普拉巴·易卜拉欣 (Prabha Ibrahim)。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of California - Berkeley. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由加州大学伯克利分校提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: The view from the tower: Watch Starship come in for chopsticks catch in epic slo-mo video
articles.author: Mike Wall

paras.en: A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage.
paras.zh: 一组新的慢动作视频让我们对 SpaceX 首次回收星舰上级有了新的视角。

paras.en: The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms.
paras.zh: 该公司于周六（11 月 14 日）实现了这一里程碑，当时位于德克萨斯州南部 Starbase 基地的发射塔用“筷子”臂抓住了 Starship 的 Ship 飞船。

paras.en: You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower.
paras.zh: 您可能已经看过从远处展示史诗般障碍的照片和视频。但周二（11 月 17 日），SpaceX 发布了近距离视图——由摄像机在这座 480 英尺（146 米）高的塔顶附近拍摄的一系列慢动作视频。

paras.en: "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above.
paras.zh: “Starbase 塔式筷子接住了他们的第一艘星际飞船。这种独特的架构旨在实现全面、快速的可重用性，能够从同一个发射台重复发射和着陆，”SpaceX 在周二发布的帖子中写道，该帖子分享了这些视频，您可以在上面看到嵌入的视频汇编。

paras.en: Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger.
paras.zh: 星舰是有史以来最大、最强大的火箭。目前的“V3”版本高约 408 英尺 (124 m)，未来的迭代将会更大。

paras.en: As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight.
paras.zh: 正如 SpaceX 在周二的帖子中指出的那样，巨型火箭的设计还可以完全快速地重复使用，这对于轨道发射系统来说尚属首次。该公司计划在发射塔捕获星舰的两个阶段——飞船和超重型助推器，这是一种旨在实现高效检查、翻新和重新飞行的回收策略。

paras.en: SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight, Starship's 15th to date, which launched on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico.
paras.zh: SpaceX 计划在最近的这次试飞中进行这样的双重捕获，这是 Starship 迄今为止的第 15 次试飞，该试飞于周五晚上（11 月 13 日）发射。但“超重”号在发射后约 6.5 分钟返回 Starbase 时遇到了低燃料警告，并自动转向降落在墨西哥湾。

paras.en: That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights. Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does.
paras.zh: 对于 SpaceX 来说，这并不是什么大事，因为它已经在之前的三次试飞中抓住了 Super Heavy 的机会。拦截船更难；上级从轨道返回地球，因此它比助推器来得更快、更热。

paras.en: SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try.
paras.zh: 在 15 号航班之前，SpaceX 甚至从未尝试过用船只捕获船只。但该公司在第一次尝试时就成功完成了这一操作。

paras.en: And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit. The first set was deployed on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28.
paras.zh: Ship 在返回之前在轨道上做了一些工作：它在 15 号航班上部署了 26 颗 SpaceX 的下一代 Starlink V3 宽带卫星，这是该公司发送到近地轨道的第二批卫星。第一套部署在 9 月 28 日发射的 14 号航班上。

paras.en: Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. To find out what his latest project is, you can follow Michael on Twitter.
paras.zh: Michael Wall 是 Space.com 的太空飞行和技术编辑，于 2010 年加入该团队。他主要报道人类和机器人太空飞行、军事太空和系外行星，但以涉足太空艺术领域而闻名。他关于寻找外星生命的书《Out There》于 2018 年 11 月 13 日出版。在成为科普作家之前，迈克尔曾是一名爬行动物学家和野生动物生物学家。他拥有博士学位。澳大利亚悉尼大学进化生物学博士学位、亚利桑那大学学士学位以及加州大学圣克鲁斯分校科学写作研究生证书。要了解他的最新项目是什么，您可以在 Twitter 上关注 Michael。

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

paras.en: On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth.
paras.zh: 2005年11月19日，日本隼鸟号宇宙飞船首次从小行星升空。隼鸟原本应该将小行星样本带回地球。

paras.en: Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway.
paras.zh: 小行星是在太阳系早期形成的太空岩石。我们研究小行星是为了更多地了解太阳系的历史。隼鸟号（发音为 HI-uh-BOOS-uh）在小行星糸川（EE -toh-KA-wah）上两次着陆。每次，航天器都会进入安全模式。控制人员不确定隼鸟号是否收集了任何材料。但他们还是把宇宙飞船送回了地球。

paras.en: Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010. Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa.
paras.zh: 隼鸟号的样本返回舱于2010年6月返回地球。科学家在舱内发现了系川星的尘埃，证明它确实捕获了系川星的样本。

paras.en: The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth.
paras.zh: 日本隼鸟号小行星糸川任务的主要目标从来都不是成为第一艘从太空岩石升空的航天器。该任务的目标始终是从小行星收集样本并将其带回地球。

paras.en: It was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005.
paras.zh: 对于隼来说，通往糸川的道路是艰难的。日本宇宙航空研究开发机构 (JAXA) 于 2003 年 5 月 9 日发射了探测器，计划于 2005 年初夏抵达这颗小行星。

paras.en: That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines.
paras.zh: 由于太阳风暴使隼鸟号的太阳能电池阵列退化，限制了其离子发动机的可用功率，这颗小行星的抵达被推迟到 2005 年 9 月。

paras.en: Still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，隼鸟号还是一瘸一拐地沿着它的路径于 2005 年 9 月 12 日到达了小行星糸川。

paras.en: Hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has said.
paras.zh: 隼鸟号向糸川发射了一个小型着陆器，但该探测器显然丢失了。 JAXA 表示，隼鸟号随后在小行星上投放了一个着陆目标，并最终成功在距标记点约 99 英尺的地方着陆。

paras.en: During its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report. Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft.
paras.zh: 据美联社报道，隼鸟号在 11 月 19 日首次着陆时下降到糸川上方仅 56 英尺的高度，然后沉寂了 3 个小时。一旦恢复联系，日本宇宙航空研究开发机构官员确认探测器已经着陆，并最终升空进行第二次尝试。这是有史以来第一次由航天器从小行星升空。

paras.en: "The spacecraft actually bounced off the surface a few times and spent about 39 minutes resting on the asteroid, but apparently the samplers never fired," Andrew Cheng, a Hayabusa science team member at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, told Space.com at the time. There was hope that some material managed to make it inside the collector anyway.
paras.zh: 约翰·霍普金斯大学应用物理实验室隼鸟科学小组成员安德鲁·程当时告诉 Space.com：“航天器实际上从表面反弹了几次，并在小行星上停留了大约 39 分钟，但显然采样器从未发射。”不管怎样，人们还是希望有一些材料能成功地进入收集器内部。

paras.en: "After all the thrashing about ... there is no way to confirm that," Cheng had said. The second landing on Itokawa occured a few days later on Nov. 26, 2005.
paras.zh: “经过一番折腾……没有办法证实这一点，”程说。几天后，即 2005 年 11 月 26 日，第二次登陆糸川。

paras.en: In November 2010, five months after Hayabusa's sample-return capsule touched down in Australia, JAXA announced some good news: Hayabusa did collect 1,500 dust grains from asteroid Itokawa, samples that were jammed into the collector by the two landings, despite is collector mechanism not firing.
paras.zh: 2010 年 11 月，隼鸟号的样本返回舱在澳大利亚着陆五个月后，JAXA 宣布了一些好消息：隼鸟号确实从小行星糸川收集到了 1,500 个尘埃颗粒，这些样本在两次着陆时被塞进了收集器中，尽管收集器机制并未启动。

paras.en: The ultimate success of Hayabusa spurred the creation of another sample-return mission by Japan: Hayabusa2.
paras.zh: 隼鸟号的最终成功促使日本创建了另一个样本返回任务：隼鸟二号。

paras.en: That probe launched in December 2014 and arrived at asteroid Ryugu (REE-ooh-goo) in 2018. It collected its own samples and returned them to Earth in December 2020.
paras.zh: 该探测器于 2014 年 12 月发射，并于 2018 年抵达小行星龙宫 (REE-ooh-goo)。它收集了自己的样本，并于 2020 年 12 月将其带回地球。

paras.en: The Hayabusa2 probe is now on an extended mission to the asteroid 2015 BM510, which it will fly by in April 2028. It had planned to land on a strange asteroid 1998 KY26, but suffered engine trouble that made that rendezvous impossible
paras.zh: 隼鸟二号探测器目前正在执行对小行星 2015 BM510 的延长任务，将于 2028 年 4 月飞越该行星。它原本计划降落在一颗奇怪的小行星 1998 KY26 上，但由于发动机故障，导致这次会合变得不可能

paras.en: Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
paras.zh: 想要更多太空历史吗？查看我们完整的“太空中的这一天”故事存档，并在 YouTube 上观看“太空中的这一天”视频。

paras.en: Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
paras.zh: Hanneke Weitering 是西北太平洋地区的一名多媒体记者，在 FutureFlight.aero 和 Aviation International News 报道航空业的未来，此前曾担任 Space.com 的航天和天文学新闻编辑。作为一名拥有 10 多年科学新闻经验的编辑，她曾为学术课堂杂志、MedPage Today 和橡树岭国家实验室计算科学研究所撰写文章。在家乡诺克斯维尔的田纳西大学学习物理学后，她在纽约大学获得了科学、健康和环境报告 (SHERP) 研究生学位。 Hanneke 于 2016 年加入 Space.com 团队，担任专职撰稿人和制作人，涵盖航天和天文学等主题。她目前与她的猫和两条蛇住在太空针塔所在地西雅图。在业余时间，汉内克喜欢探索落基山脉，沐浴在大自然中，寻找黑暗的天空凝视宇宙。

articles.title: Voyager 1 team, unbowed by communications glitch, celebrates epic 1-light-day distance milestone
articles.author: Chelsea Gohd

paras.en: PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth, something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary.
paras.zh: 加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳——周四（11 月 19 日），美国宇航局航海者号任务团队在这里欢呼雀跃，擦干眼泪，庆祝一个重要的里程碑——航海者一号刚刚到达距地球一光日的位置，这是其他航天器从未做到过的。尽管探测器出现了通信异常，但人们仍然兴奋不已，团队仍然相信这是暂时的。

paras.en: Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2, flew past Neptune. The gathering served to celebrate Voyager 1's distance milestone: At 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 18), the probe reached one light-day from Earth — the distance a photon travels in one day, which is about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space.
paras.zh: Voyager 团队成员齐聚 NASA 喷气推进实验室 (JPL) 的冯·卡门礼堂，召开关于此次任务的新闻发布会，这是自 1989 年 Voyager 1 的双胞胎 Voyager 2 飞越海王星以来的首次此类活动。这次聚会是为了庆祝航行者一号的距离里程碑：美国东部时间周三（11 月 18 日）凌晨 5 点 16 分（格林威治标准时间 1016 年），探测器到达距离地球一光日的位置——光子一天行进的距离，约为 160 亿英里（260 亿公里）。这意味着现在信号从地球传输到太空中最远的人造物体航海家一号需要一整天的时间。

paras.en: "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. What an incredible milestone," Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker said during Thursday's event.
paras.zh: “我记得 1977 年，我站在好望角观看航行者号发射，我从未想过 49 年后的今天我会在这里庆祝航行者号的一光日。这是一个令人难以置信的里程碑，”航行者号项目科学家 Linda Spilker 在周四的活动中说道。

paras.en: While this day and this week have been chock-full of excitement over the distance milestone, the Voyager mission team has been hard at work, as usual, keeping the two nearly 50-year-old spacecraft alive and functioning.
paras.zh: 虽然这一天和本周人们对这个距离里程碑充满了兴奋，但航行者号任务团队一如既往地努力工作，保持两艘近 50 年历史的航天器的生命和功能。

paras.en: Unfortunately, as JPL spokesperson Raquel Villanueva shared at this celebration, on Saturday (Nov. 14), Voyager 1 stopped transmitting science and engineering data. The team has remained in contact with Voyager 1 while investigating the issue, and they are confident that they'll be able to solve it soon.
paras.zh: 不幸的是，正如 JPL 发言人 Raquel Villanueva 在本次庆祝活动中所分享的那样，周六（11 月 14 日），航行者 1 号停止传输科学和工程数据。该团队在调查该问题时一直与 Voyager 1 保持联系，他们有信心能够很快解决该问题。

paras.en: "We listen to each spacecraft every day," Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd told Space.com at the event. Regarding Voyager 1, "we have an anomaly that is not something unseen before," Dodd said. "We do have a very strong carrier signal. We currently don't have a frame sync, so we're not getting the science or engineering data currently."
paras.zh: “我们每天都会监听每艘航天器的声音，”航行者号项目经理苏珊娜·多德在活动中告诉 Space.com。关于航海者一号，“我们发现了一个以前从未见过的异常​​现象，”多德说。 “我们确实有非常强的载波信号。我们目前没有帧同步，因此我们目前无法获得科学或工程数据。”

paras.en: "But if you recall," Dodd added, "one light-day is very far from us. [It takes] 24 hours to get the signal to the spacecraft, 24 hours for the signal to come down, so it takes two days to diagnose anything on the spacecraft … So we can't do anything fast, and the data rates are very low."
paras.zh: “但是如果你还记得的话，”多德补充道，“一光日距离我们非常远。[需要] 24 小时才能将信号发送到航天器，24 小时信号才能传回，因此需要两天才能诊断航天器上的任何东西......所以我们无法快速做任何事情，而且数据速率非常低。”

paras.en: According to Dodd, this anomaly isn't a major cause for long-term concern. Rather, it's likely just part of the natural aging process for spacecraft.
paras.zh: 多德表示，这种异常现象并不是引起长期关注的主要原因。相反，这可能只是航天器自然老化过程的一部分。

paras.en: "These spacecraft are old," she said. "All of us old people have our aches and pains, and you know, sometimes it takes longer to stretch out your muscles and remember things, and so we are in a realm where we're going to see more anomalies with Voyager just due to the distance and the age."
paras.zh: “这些航天器很旧了，”她说。 “我们所有的老年人都会感到疼痛，你知道，有时需要更长的时间才能伸展肌肉并记住事情，因此，由于距离和年龄的原因，我们将在航行者号上看到更多异常情况。”

paras.en: "But we feel Voyager 1, although it's not sending us the telemetry data, it's pointed at the Earth. It's sending us a strong carrier signal, and I'm confident that it won't be too long, and it will send us data back."
paras.zh: “但我们感觉到航海者一号，虽然它没有给我们发送遥测数据，但它是指向地球的。它正在向我们发送很强的载波信号，我相信不会太久，它会给我们发回数据。”

paras.en: And, for anyone curious how Voyager 1's slower twin Voyager 2 is faring, Dodd shared that it is doing very well on its own journey through interstellar space. "Voyager 2 is very healthy. It's continuing its mission. It has three scientific instruments on it," she told Space.com.
paras.zh: 而且，对于那些好奇航海者 1 号速度较慢的孪生航海者 2 号进展如何的人来说，多德表示，航海者 1 号在自己的星际之旅中表现非常出色。 “航行者二号非常健康。它正在继续执行任务。它上面有三台科学仪器，”她告诉 Space.com。

paras.en: "Each spacecraft is basically setting a record every day for longevity or distance," Dodd added about the twin probes.
paras.zh: “每艘航天器基本上每天都在创下寿命或距离的记录，”多德在谈到这两个探测器时补充道。

paras.en: Despite the communications anomaly — and even though most of the team had been up all night to confirm the one-light-day signal from Voyager 1 — the room was alive with excitement. The Voyagers have been flying for nearly 50 years on a mission expected to last just five years, so the team was beyond ready to celebrate.
paras.zh: 尽管通讯出现异常，尽管团队的大部分成员彻夜未眠，以确认航行者一号发出的一光日信号，但房间里却充满了兴奋。航行者号已经飞行了近 50 年，执行的任务预计只持续五年，因此团队已经做好了庆祝的准备。

paras.en: Amidst the more technical updates about the mission and its current status out in interstellar space, the event included footage of Voyager light-day celebrations from around the world. From children cheering on Voyager to iconic landmarks lighting up gold in honor of the mission's Golden Record, the Voyager love echoed around the world in photos and videos. The footage of this international celebration was enough to move Nicky Fox, NASA's associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate, nearly to tears.
paras.zh: 在有关该任务及其当前星际空间状态的更多技术更新中，该活动包括来自世界各地的航行者光日庆祝活动的镜头。从孩子们为航海者号欢呼，到标志性地标点亮金色以纪念该任务的金唱片，航海者号的爱在照片和视频中回响在世界各地。这场国际庆祝活动的镜头足以让美国宇航局科学任务理事会副局长尼基·福克斯感动得几乎落泪。

paras.en: "I actually thought I was going to start sobbing," Fox joked to Space.com after the media briefing. "I think just hearing children's voices and people saying 'We love you, Voyager,' 'Go Voyager' — it just was amazing."
paras.zh: “我实际上以为我要开始哭泣，”福克斯在媒体吹风会后向 Space.com 开玩笑说。 “我认为只要听到孩子们的声音和人们说‘我们爱你，Voyager’、‘Go Voyager’——那就太棒了。”

paras.en: And Fox and the mission team members weren't the only ones sharing their love for Voyager. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins beamed down her own video message to the Voyager 1 spacecraft from the International Space Station, sharing in the celebration.
paras.zh: 福克斯和任务团队成员并不是唯一表达对航行者号热爱的人。美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 宇航员杰西卡·沃特金斯 (Jessica Watkins) 从国际空间站向航海家一号飞船发送了自己的视频信息，分享庆祝活动。

paras.en: "Dear Voyager 1," Watkins said. "As an orbiting outpost just 250 miles [400 kilometers] above Earth, we often feel distant yet deeply connected to our home planet. The International Space Station has had crew continuously living off of the Earth for 26 years, seen hundreds of visitors from around the world, and enabled thousands of experiments to advance space exploration.
paras.zh: “亲爱的航海者一号，”沃特金斯说。 “作为一个距离地球仅 250 英里（400 公里）的轨道前哨站，我们常常感到遥远，但与我们的家园有着深刻的联系。国际空间站的宇航员在地球之外连续生活了 26 年，接待了来自世界各地的数百名访客，并进行了数千项实验来推进太空探索。

paras.en: "While you have been traveling into the unknown for nearly half a century, helping pave our path, together, our two journeys tell a single story of exploration," she continued. "One remains close to home, and the other reaches ever outward. Voyager 1, you have been a beacon of light, a symbol of exploration, a seeker of truth, a carrier of hope, a brave explorer, traveling further than any human hand has ever reached. You represent the very best of what humanity has to offer.
paras.zh: “近半个世纪以来，你们一直在探索未知世界，帮助我们铺平道路，但我们的两次旅程共同讲述了一个探索的故事，”她继续说道。 “一个离家很近，另一个则不断向外。航海者一号，你是一盏灯塔，是探索的象征，是真理的追寻者，是希望的载体，是勇敢的探险家，你的旅行比任何人的手都更远。你代表了人类所能提供的最好的东西。

paras.en: "As you reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, the entire crew of Expedition 75 and people across the planet send you our admiration and our wishes for a safe and continued journey as you begin your post-one-light-day era. There are so many amazing milestones and discoveries to come. You have a universe ahead of you, and you carry with you our collective hopes and dreams. When we look up from Earth, we will always think of you as you continue forward into the great unknown. May you continue shining bright for all of us. Go Voyager 1!" Watkins said, ending her message with a weightless backflip from aboard the station.
paras.zh: “当你到达距地球一光日的距离时，第 75 号探险队的全体船员和地球各地的人们向你表达我们的钦佩，并祝愿你在开始你的后一光日时代时能有一个安全、持续的旅程。未来会有许多令人惊叹的里程碑和发现。你前面有一个宇宙，你带着我们共同的希望和梦想。当我们从地球上抬起头时，我们将永远想到你，因为你继续前进到伟大的未知世界。愿你继续闪耀光芒。我们所有人都去航海家一号吧！”沃特金斯在空间站上以一个失重后空翻结束了她的信息。

paras.en: In concluding the media briefing, the mission team invited those in the room who, over the past 50 years (or more, with one person sharing their excitement having worked on Voyager before it was even called Voyager) have worked on the mission in one way or another, to stand up to a round of applause. With mission team members today ranging from those in their 20s to their 90s, the people behind this enduring mission span many generations.
paras.zh: 在结束媒体吹风会时，任务团队邀请了在场的那些在过去 50 年（或更长的时间里，其中一个人分享了他们在 Voyager 被称为 Voyager 之前就参与了该任务）以这样或那样的方式参与过该任务的人们起立，并热烈鼓掌。今天的使命团队成员从 20 多岁到 90 多岁，这个持久使命背后的人跨越了好几代人。

paras.en: Interestingly, Fox actually began her light-day celebrations earlier in the week. She, alongside writer/producer Ann Druyan — who was the wife of the late astronomer Carl Sagan, whose work helped create the mission's Golden Record and who took the now-famous "pale blue dot" Voyager image of Earth to the public — together lit up the Empire State Building gold.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，福克斯实际上在本周早些时候就开始了她的光日庆祝活动。她与作家兼制片人安·德鲁扬（Ann Druya​​n）——已故天文学家卡尔·萨根的妻子，其作品帮助创造了该任务的金唱片，并将现在著名的“淡蓝点”航海家号地球图像向公众展示——共同点亮了帝国大厦的金色光芒。

paras.en: "I was actually very privileged to flick the switch and turn on the Empire State Building lights on Tuesday evening [Nov. 17]," Fox, wearing golden Voyager-inspired nail polish crafted by her daughter, told Space.com. "That was just spectacular … I was there with Ann … we were both so giddy with the excitement of doing it … It was amazing. And then going up and standing underneath and seeing the tower was just really, really special."
paras.zh: “实际上，我非常荣幸能够在周二晚上（11 月 17 日）按下开关并打开帝国大厦的灯光，”涂着由女儿亲手制作的金色航海者指甲油的福克斯告诉 Space.com。 “那真是太壮观了……我和安在一起……我们都因为这样做的兴奋而头晕……太棒了。然后上去站在下面，看到这座塔真的非常非常特别。”

paras.en: While the room lit up with excitement for Voyager's light-day milestone on Thursday, the team was also brimming with anticipation for what lies ahead. As Voyager hurtles toward another major milestone, turning 50 in 2027, it remains an active science mission, and the team remains hard at work to push the boundaries of exploration with these aging probes.
paras.zh: 虽然房间里因周四航行者号的光日里程碑而兴奋不已，但团队也对未来充满期待。随着 Voyager 号在 2027 年迎来 50 岁生日，迈向另一个重要里程碑，它仍然是一项活跃的科学任务，团队仍在努力工作，利用这些老化的探测器突破探索的界限。

paras.en: "Voyager right now — the two Voyagers — they're in an area of space that we've never been into. So every single bit of data that comes back is precious because it's unique," Fox said.
paras.zh: 福克斯说：“航海者号——两艘航海者号——它们处于我们从未进入过的太空区域。因此，返回的每一个数据都非常珍贵，因为它是独一无二的。”

paras.en: "Now we're in a region where the sun's influence is a lot different, and we're in this region where we can start to understand: What is it like out past our sun? What is it like in the space between the stars?" Voyager deputy project scientist Jamie Rankin told Space.com. "We're at a very exciting time of starting to connect what we know and what we've seen, living with this star [our sun] to what is out there."
paras.zh: “现在我们处于一个太阳影响力有很大不同的区域，在这个区域我们可以开始了解：太阳过去是什么样子？恒星之间的空间是什么样子？”航行者号副项目科学家杰米·兰金告诉 Space.com。 “我们正处于一个非常激动人心的时刻，开始将我们所知道的和我们所看到的、与这颗恒星（我们的太阳）一起生活的事物与外面的事物联系起来。”

paras.en: "What's next? Voyager is just going to keep on going. You know, people sometimes think, 'When's the mission going to end?' It's never going to end," Fox added to Space.com. "Even when we can no longer talk to Voyager, they're both going to keep going … So there's no end for the Voyager mission."
paras.zh: “下一步是什么？航行者号将继续前进。你知道，人们有时会想，‘任务什么时候结束？’它永远不会结束，”福克斯向 Space.com 补充道。 “即使我们无法再与航海者号交谈，它们也会继续前进……所以航海者号的任务没有结束。”

paras.en: Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. You can follow her online @chelsea.gohd and @foxanne.music
paras.zh: Chelsea Gohd 于 2018 年至 2022 年担任 Space.com 的高级作家，并于 2026 年回归，在文章和视频中报道了从气候变化到行星科学和载人航天的所有内容。拥有硕士学位在生物学领域，Chelsea 曾为 NASA JPL、美国自然历史博物馆、《科学美国人》、Discover 杂志博客、天文学杂志和 Live Science 等机构撰写文章和工作。在创作、编辑或拍摄太空作品之余，Gohd 会创作音乐并以 Foxanne 的身份进行表演，甚至于 2021 年与 Inspiration4 一起向太空推出了一首歌曲。您可以在线关注她@chelsea.gohd 和@foxanne.music

articles.title: Moog Marks 25 Years Since ESPA Design Milestone: Innovating Space Rideshare
articles.author: Moog Inc.

paras.en: East Aurora, N.Y. — Moog Inc. (NYSE: MOG.A and MOG.B) marks 25 years since the Evolved Secondary Payload Adapter (ESPA) ring completed its Critical Design Review in 2001. The pioneering technology helped advance space rideshare by enabling multiple payloads to share a launch and broadening access to orbit for commercial, government, and defense missions.
paras.zh: 纽约州东奥罗拉 — 穆格公司（纽约证券交易所股票代码：MOG.A 和 MOG.B）庆祝演进型辅助有效载荷适配器 (ESPA) 环于 2001 年完成关键设计审查以来 25 周年。这项开创性技术通过支持多个有效载荷共享发射并拓宽商业、政府和国防任务的轨道通道，帮助推进了太空共享出行。

paras.en: Development of ESPA began in 1999 through a collaborative government-industry initiative, culminating in the successful completion of its Critical Design Review on January 18, 2001. The ESPA ring enabled launch vehicles to carry multiple secondary payloads by efficiently using previously unused volume beneath primary satellites. This approach lowered costs and increased mission flexibility, supporting commercial satellite constellations, technology demonstrations, and critical defense operations.
paras.zh: ESPA 的开发始于 1999 年，通过政府与行业的合作倡议，最终于 2001 年 1 月 18 日成功完成了关键设计审查。ESPA 环使运载火箭能够通过有效利用主卫星下方以前未使用的空间来携带多个辅助有效载荷。这种方法降低了成本并提高了任务灵活性，支持商业卫星星座、技术演示和关键防御行动。

paras.en: “ESPA helped redefine access to space by enabling additional payloads to share a launch with primary missions. Its impact continues across commercial, government, and military space—and its story reflects the value of enduring collaboration between Air Force Research Lab (AFRL) and industry partners such as Moog,” said Dr. Darren Raspa, chief historian, AFRL Space and Directed Energy Systems.
paras.zh: AFRL 空间和定向能源系统首席历史学家达伦·拉斯帕 (Darren Raspa) 博士表示：“ESPA 通过启用额外的有效载荷与主要任务共享发射，帮助重新定义了太空访问。它的影响持续遍及商业、政府和军事太空，它的故事反映了空军研究实验室 (AFRL) 与穆格等行业合作伙伴之间持久合作的价值。”

paras.en: Over the past 25 years, the ESPA family has evolved into a versatile, modular platform supporting varied payload sizes and interface configurations. ESPA-derived designs have also served as the structural foundation for spacecraft buses. Today, the platform continues to support mission planning for NASA, the U.S. government, and commercial space ventures worldwide.
paras.zh: 在过去的 25 年里，ESPA 系列已发展成为一个多功能的模块化平台，支持各种有效负载大小和接口配置。 ESPA 衍生设计也成为航天器总线的结构基础。如今，该平台继续支持 NASA、美国政府和全球商业航天企业的任务规划。

paras.en: Moog continues to offer a family of ESPA configurations, including Standard ESPA, ESPA Heavy, and ESPA Grande, designed to accommodate evolving payload and mission requirements. The platform’s modular architecture and adaptable interfaces support rideshare missions, payload integration, and spacecraft applications across the growing space market.
paras.zh: 穆格继续提供一系列 ESPA 配置，包括标准 ESPA、ESPA Heavy 和 ESPA Grande，旨在适应不断变化的有效载荷和任务要求。该平台的模块化架构和适应性强的接口支持不断增长的太空市场中的乘车共享任务、有效载荷集成和航天器应用。

paras.en: “The ESPA ring began as a technical solution to a practical challenge: maximizing every launch opportunity,” said Timothy Pargett, general manager, Moog Payload Adapters and Isolation business. “Today, it stands as a cornerstone of how missions, large and small, gain cost-effective, reliable access to orbit through rideshare. Its enduring legacy reflects visionary innovation and trusted partnerships across the aerospace community.”
paras.zh: “ESPA 环最初是作为应对实际挑战的技术解决方案：最大化每个发射机会，”穆格有效负载适配器和隔离业务总经理 Timothy Pargett 说道。 “如今，它已成为大大小小的任务如何通过拼车获得具有成本效益且可靠的轨道访问的基石。它的持久遗产反映了整个航空航天界的富有远见的创新和值得信赖的合作伙伴关系。”

paras.en: In conjunction with the anniversary, a Moog flight-qualified ESPA ring will be on display at the National Museum of Nuclear Science & History in Albuquerque, N.M., from November 7, 2026, through January 10, 2027.
paras.zh: 为庆祝周年纪念日，一枚符合穆格飞行资格的 ESPA 环将于 2026 年 11 月 7 日至 2027 年 1 月 10 日在新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基的国家核科学与历史博物馆展出。

paras.en: Museum visitors will have the opportunity to see firsthand the hardware that helped advance rideshare and enable diverse space missions.
paras.zh: 博物馆参观者将有机会亲眼目睹有助于推进乘车共享和实现多样化太空任务的硬件。

paras.en: As ESPA enters its next chapter, Moog continues to advance spacecraft payload integration and develop adaptable solutions that expand flexible, cost-effective access to orbit for future space exploration and defense missions.
paras.zh: 随着 ESPA 进入新篇章，穆格将继续推进航天器有效载荷集成，并开发适应性强的解决方案，为未来的太空探索和防御任务扩展灵活、经济高效的轨道接入方式。

paras.en: Moog is a worldwide designer, manufacturer, and systems integrator of high-performance precision motion and fluid controls and control systems. Moog’s high-performance systems control military and commercial aircraft, satellites, and space vehicles, launch vehicles, defense systems, missiles, automated industrial machinery, marine, and medical equipment. Additional information about the Company can be found at www.moog.com or www.moog.com/space.
paras.zh: 穆格是全球高性能精密运动和流体控制及控制系统的设计者、制造商和系统集成商。穆格的高性能系统控制军用和商用飞机、卫星和航天器、运载火箭、防御系统、导弹、自动化工业机械、船舶和医疗设备。有关公司的更多信息，请访问 www.moog.com 或 www.moog.com/space。

articles.title: What role does industry play in Europe’s space sovereignty push?
articles.author: SpaceNews Editor

paras.en: In this episode, SpaceNews’ Jason Rainbow interviews Atle Woello, the CEO and senior vice president of the space systems and surveillance business unit at Kongsberg NanoAvionics. They discuss the role space plays for defense systems that are increasingly interconnected across domains, as well as the role that the European industrial base can play in the continent’s recent political and fundraising push to bolster sovereignty, independence and resilience in space.
paras.zh: 在本集中，SpaceNews 的 Jason Rainbow 采访了 Kongsberg NanoAvionics 空间系统和监视业务部门的首席执行官兼高级副总裁 Atle Woello。他们讨论了太空对于跨领域互联日益紧密的防御系统的作用，以及欧洲工业基础在欧洲大陆最近为加强太空主权、独立和复原力而进行的政治和筹款活动中可以发挥的作用。

paras.en: This episode is sponsored by Xiphos Systems.
paras.zh: 本集由 Xiphos Systems 赞助。

paras.en: Xiphos Systems develops compact, high-performance embedded computing solutions for spacecraft and aerospace applications. Founded in 1996 and based in Montreal, the company specializes in commercial off-the-shelf processing platforms designed for space, combining processors, programmable logic, storage, networking, and RF capabilities in low size, weight, power, and cost designs. Its portfolio includes processor boards, onboard computers, RF payload systems, and AI-capable computing platforms for satellites, launch vehicles, lunar missions, and robotics. With more than two decades of experience and over 1,000 processor cards delivered, Xiphos supports customers from system integration through deployment, helping bring reliable computing closer to the mission.
paras.zh: Xiphos Systems 为航天器和航空航天应用开发紧凑、高性能的嵌入式计算解决方案。该公司成立于 1996 年，总部位于蒙特利尔，专注于为太空设计的商用现成处理平台，将处理器、可编程逻辑、存储、网络和射频功能与低尺寸、重量、功耗和成本设计相结合。其产品组合包括处理器板、机载计算机、射频有效载荷系统以及用于卫星、运载火箭、月球任务和机器人的人工智能计算平台。 Xiphos 拥有二十多年的经验和交付的 1,000 多个处理器卡，为客户提供从系统集成到部署的支持，帮助实现可靠的计算更接近使命。

paras.en: Space Minds is a new audio and video podcast from SpaceNews that focuses on the inspiring leaders, technologies and exciting opportunities in space.
paras.zh: Space Minds 是 SpaceNews 推出的新音频和视频播客，重点关注太空中鼓舞人心的领导者、技术和令人兴奋的机会。

paras.en: The weekly podcast features compelling interviews with scientists, founders and experts who love to talk about space, covers the news that has enthusiasts daydreaming, and engages with listeners. Join Mike Gruss and journalists from the SpaceNews team for new episodes every Thursday.
paras.zh: 每周播客对热爱谈论太空的科学家、创始人和专家进行引人注目的采访，报道让爱好者们做白日梦的新闻，并与听众互动。每周四与 Mike Gruss 和 SpaceNews 团队的记者一起观看新剧集。

paras.en: Watch a new episode every Thursday on SpaceNews.com and on our YouTube, Spotify and Apple channels.
paras.zh: 每周四在 SpaceNews.com 以及我们的 YouTube、Spotify 和 Apple 频道上观看新剧集。

paras.en: Be the first to know when new episodes drop! Enter your email, and we’ll make sure you get exclusive access to each episode as soon as it goes live!
paras.zh: 成为第一个知道新剧集何时发布的人！输入您的电子邮件，我们将确保您在每集上线后立即获得独家访问权限！

paras.zh: 注意：注册即表示您同意接收来自 SpaceNews 和我们合作伙伴的通信。

articles.title: Commercial Space Federation Welcomes CesiumAstro as a New Associate Member
articles.author: Commercial Space Federation

paras.en: November 13, 2026— Washington, D.C.—The Commercial Space Federation (CSF) is pleased to welcome CesiumAstro as its newest Associate Member. A global leader in advanced connectivity solutions for the space and defense sectors, CesiumAstro delivers advanced space systems that connect, detect, and defend across commercial, government, and national security missions. CesiumAstro’s addition further strengthens CSF’s diverse membership and the Federation’s work to advance a competitive, innovative, and sustainable U.S. commercial space economy.
paras.zh: 2026 年 11 月 13 日——华盛顿特区——商业航天联合会 (CSF) 很高兴欢迎 CesiumAstro 成为其最新准会员。 CesiumAstro 是太空和国防部门先进连接解决方​​案的全球领导者，提供先进的太空系统，可跨商业、政府和国家安全任务进行连接、检测和防御。 CesiumAstro 的加入进一步加强了 CSF 的多元化成员资格以及联合会推动竞争性、创新性和可持续的美国商业太空经济的工作。

paras.en: CesiumAstro is a lobal leader in advanced connectivity solutions for space and defense sectors, CesiumAstro delivers advanced space systems that connect, detect, and defend across commercial, government, and national security missions. Its full-stack, multi-mission, end-to-end hardware and software solutions encompass satellites, high-performance communications payloads and advanced computing systems. CesiumAstro maintains complete vertical integration with in-house design, manufacturing, and testing capabilities certified to AS9100D/ISO 9001:2015 standards. Headquartered near Austin, Texas, the company operates additional facilities in Colorado, California, Washington, D.C., Florida, the United Kingdom, Germany, Singapore, Taiwan, and Japan.
paras.zh: CesiumAstro 是太空和国防部门先进连接解决方​​案的全球领导者，CesiumAstro 提供先进的太空系统，可跨商业、政府和国家安全任务进行连接、检测和防御。其全栈、多任务、端到端硬件和软件解决方案涵盖卫星、高性能通信有效载荷和先进计算系统。 CesiumAstro 保持与内部设计、制造和测试能力的完全垂直整合，并通过了 AS9100D/ISO 9001:2015 标准认证。该公司总部位于德克萨斯州奥斯汀附近，在科罗拉多州、加利福尼亚州、华盛顿特区、佛罗里达州、英国、德国、新加坡、台湾和日本设有其他工厂。

paras.en: CesiumAstro recently announced the closing of $730 million in Series D financing, valuing the company at more than $4.5 billion, and unveiled Synchronicity, a planned 737-satellite, AI-enabled constellation. The new capital will support advanced technologies, expansion of U.S. manufacturing capacity, development and production of next-generation spacecraft, Synchronicity deployment, and international growth.
paras.zh: CesiumAstro 最近宣布完成 7.3 亿美元的 D 轮融资，公司估值超过 45 亿美元，并推出了 Synchronicity，这是一个计划中的 737 颗卫星、支持人工智能的星座。新资金将支持先进技术、美国制造能力的扩张、下一代航天器的开发和生产、同步部署和国际增长。

paras.en: In the past 12 months, CesiumAstro has expanded its capabilities through three strategic acquisitions: Jariet Technologies, 1Aardvark, and Vidrovr, strengthening the company’s capabilities across semiconductor technology, mission software, and artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 在过去的 12 个月中，CesiumAstro 通过三项战略收购扩大了其能力：Jariet Technologies、1Aardvark 和 Vidrovr，增强了公司在半导体技术、任务软件和人工智能方面的能力。

paras.en: CesiumAstro’s full-stack, multi-mission, end-to-end hardware and software solutions encompass satellites, high-performance communications payloads, and advanced compute systems. The company maintains complete vertical integration with in-house design, manufacturing, and testing capabilities certified to AS9100D/ISO 9001:2015 standards.
paras.zh: CesiumAstro 的全栈、多任务、端到端硬件和软件解决方案涵盖卫星、高性能通信有效载荷和先进计算系统。该公司与通过 AS9100D/ISO 9001:2015 标准认证的内部设计、制造和测试能力保持完整的垂直整合。

paras.en: “A thriving commercial economy in low Earth orbit needs reliable communications and a clear path from development to operations. CesiumAstro is joining CSF’s Commercial LEO Council to bring our communications expertise to that effort. We look forward to advancing policies that encourage investment, expand government use of commercial services, and support companies building the next generation of space infrastructure.”
paras.zh: “近地轨道蓬勃发展的商业经济需要可靠的通信以及从开发到运营的清晰路径。CesiumAstro 正在加入 CSF 的商业 LEO 委员会，将我们的通信专业知识用于这一努力。我们期待推进鼓励投资、扩大政府对商业服务的使用以及支持企业建设下一代空间基础设施的政策。”

paras.en: – Josh Ingersoll, Director of Spectrum and Regulatory Affairs at CesiumAstro
paras.zh: – Josh Ingersoll，CesiumAstro 频谱和监管事务总监

paras.en: Founded in 2006, the Commercial Space Federation (CSF) and its members are laying the foundation for democratizing access to outer space for scientists, students, civilians, and businesses. All while working towards the goal of expanding the U.S. Commercial Space Economy. Through the promotion of technological innovation, CSF and its diverse membership are guiding the bolstering of U.S. leadership in aerospace and inspiring America’s next generation of engineers and explorers. CSF also serves as the commercial space industry’s primary advocate with the U.S. Congress and the Administration, helping inform the development and implementation of policy priorities. By engaging with congressional players, CSF is able to provide recommendations on commercial space issues that will impact the commercial space industry in the short and long term.
paras.zh: 商业太空联盟 (CSF) 及其成员成立于 2006 年，正在为科学家、学生、平民和企业进入外太空的民主化奠定基础。同时努力实现扩大美国商业太空经济的目标。通过促进技术创新，CSF 及其多元化成员正在指导巩固美国在航空航天领域的领导地位，并激励美国下一代工程师和探险家。 CSF 还担任美国国会和政府商业航天业的主要倡导者，帮助为政策优先事项的制定和实施提供信息。通过与国会参与者合作，CSF 能够就商业航天问题提供建议，这些问题将在短期和长期影响商业航天行业。

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
articles.author: Jessica Taveau

paras.en: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局 (NASA) 的航行者 1 号探测器是人类飞行最远的航天器，经过 49 年多的不断旅行，现已到达距地球一光日的位置。一光日是光在 24 小时内传播的距离，约等于 161 亿英里（259 亿公里）。该航天器于 11 月 18 日太平洋标准时间凌晨 2 点 16 分（美国东部标准时间凌晨 5 点 16 分）实现了这一里程碑。

paras.en: Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday.
paras.zh: 周四早些时候，加州理工学院管理的美国宇航局南加州喷气推进实验室的 Voyager 团队成员在 24 小时后收到了探测器的消息，即航天器的无线电信号以光速传播到达地球所需的时间。

paras.en: “Traveling a light-day is a singular feat for a spacecraft, but Voyager is so much more than a distant traveler. The Voyager mission would be remarkable just for what it contributed to planetary science with the Grand Tour of the outer planets,” said Joe Westlake, director, Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. “But it went on to become central to NASA’s fleet of heliophysics missions offering insights into the star that we all revolve around, the Sun.”
paras.zh: “航行一光日对于航天器来说是一项非凡的壮举，但航行者号不仅仅是一个遥远的旅行者。航行者号任务将是非凡的，因为它通过外行星大巡游为行星科学做出了贡献，”美国宇航局华盛顿总部太阳物理学部主任乔·韦斯特莱克说。 “但它后来成为美国宇航局太阳物理学任务的核心，为我们提供对我们围绕的恒星——太阳的深入了解。”

paras.en: Scientists use light to measure the vast distances of space. Light travels at about 186,000 miles (299,000 kilometers) a second in a vacuum. A ray of sunlight passing Earth takes about 1.3 seconds to reach the Moon, about four hours to reach Neptune, and another 20 hours to reach Voyager 1. For comparison, a light-year is 5.88 trillion miles (9.46 trillion kilometers).
paras.zh: 科学家利用光来测量广阔的太空距离。光在真空中的传播速度约为每秒 186,000 英里（299,000 公里）。一束阳光穿过地球大约需要 1.3 秒才能到达月球，大约需要 4 小时才能到达海王星，再需要 20 小时才能到达航海者 1 号。相比之下，一光年为 5.88 万亿英里（9.46 万亿公里）。

paras.en: Even though the team has not received science and engineering data from Voyager 1 since Nov. 14, the spacecraft is sending what is called a carrier signal, which typically conveys that data to Earth. Mission engineers used the carrier signal and trajectory calculations to confirm the light-day milestone. They continue to analyze the issue impacting the science and engineering data.
paras.zh: 尽管该团队自 11 月 14 日以来尚未收到航行者 1 号的科学和工程数据，但该航天器正在发送所谓的载波信号，通常会将这些数据传送到地球。任务工程师利用载体信号和轨迹计算来确认光日里程碑。他们继续分析影响科学和工程数据的问题。

paras.en: Humanity’s only probes in interstellar space, Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, launched in 1977 to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment. Managed by JPL, they were only the third and fourth spacecraft to visit Jupiter and Saturn, and the first to return high-resolution imagery, transforming our understanding of these worlds and their moons. Voyager 2 went on to study the ethereal ice giants, Neptune and Uranus. Both spacecraft continue to measure changes in the Sun’s magnetic field across vast distances.
paras.zh: 航海者 1 号及其孪生航海者 2 号是人类在星际空间中唯一的探测器，于 1977 年发射，以利用罕见的行星排列。在喷气推进实验室的管理下，它们是第三和第四艘访问木星和土星的航天器，也是第一艘返回高分辨率图像的航天器，改变了我们对这些世界及其卫星的理解。航海家二号继续研究了空灵的冰巨星海王星和天王星。这两艘航天器继续在远距离测量太阳磁场的变化。

paras.en: “Voyager 1 crossing the light-day threshold is yet another historic feat on an extraordinary voyage of discovery,” said Dave Gallagher, JPL director. “Above all, this milestone stands as a testament to the exceptional teams who built, programmed, and fly these spacecraft today, and who have overcome countless challenges to keep them connected to Earth across the vastness of space. As NASA pushes toward new frontiers in human and robotic exploration, Voyager and the people behind its success continue to inspire us to reach farther and dream bigger.”
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室主任戴夫·加拉格尔 (Dave Gallagher) 表示：“旅行者一号跨越光日门槛是非凡发现之旅中的又一历史性壮举。” “最重要的是，这一里程碑证明了今天建造、编程和驾驶这些航天器的杰出团队，他们克服了无数的挑战，使它们在浩瀚的太空中与地球保持联系。随着美国宇航局 (NASA) 向人类和机器人探索的新领域推进，航海者号及其成功背后的人们继续激励我们走得更远，梦想更大。”

paras.en: In addition to their suite of scientific instruments, the Voyager probes carry a Golden Record, a gold-plated copper phonograph compiling images and sounds from Earth, as a message to any advanced civilization that might one day find it.
paras.zh: 除了一套科学仪器外，航海者号探测器还携带一张金唱片，这是一台编译来自地球的图像和声音的镀金铜留声机，作为向任何有一天可能发现它的先进文明的信息。

paras.en: “Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, the Voyager mission continues to push the boundaries of human exploration. Its epic journey reflects the vision of Ed Stone, the Caltech physicist and JPL director who guided the mission for decades, and the curiosity and tenacity of generations of scientists and engineers who have carried that vision forward,” said Ray Jayawardhana, president, Caltech. “Beyond its immense contributions to science, Voyager also captures something profound about the human spirit. We may never know where its journey will ultimately lead, but it will venture on, an enduring affirmation that humanity was here and we yearned to explore.”
paras.zh: 加州理工学院校长雷·贾亚瓦德哈纳 (Ray Jayawardhana) 表示：“离开地球近半个世纪后，旅行者号任务继续突破人类探索的界限。其史诗般的旅程反映了数十年来指导该任务的加州理工学院物理学家兼喷气推进实验室主任埃德·斯通 (Ed Stone) 的愿景，以及推动这一愿景的几代科学家和工程师的好奇心和坚韧。” “除了对科学的巨大贡献之外，航海者号还捕捉到了人类精神的一些深刻的东西。我们可能永远不知道它的旅程最终将通向何方，但它会继续冒险，持久地证明人类就在这里，我们渴望探索。”

paras.en: Traveling about 38,000 mph (61,155 kph), Voyager 1 in 2012 became the first spacecraft to leave the heliosphere, the bubble of particles and magnetic fields created by the Sun that deflects cosmic radiation, and enter interstellar space. Voyager 2, taking a different trajectory, crossed the boundary in 2018.
paras.zh: 航行者一号于 2012 年以约 38,000 英里/小时（61,155 公里/小时）的速度行驶，成为第一艘离开日光层（由太阳产生的粒子和磁场气泡，使宇宙辐射偏转）进入星际空间的航天器。航海家二号则采取了不同的轨迹，于 2018 年跨越了边界。

paras.en: “The Voyagers are revolutionizing our understanding of interstellar space, a previously unexplored region outside the heliosphere,” said Linda Spilker, Voyager project scientist at JPL. “One big surprise is the extent to which our Sun continues to affect interstellar space, all the way out to Voyager 1. Where does the Sun’s influence end and pristine interstellar space begin? Perhaps Voyager may endure long enough to answer that question.”
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室航海者号项目科学家琳达·斯皮尔克 (Linda Spilker) 表示：“航海者号正在彻底改变我们对星际空间的理解，星际空间是日光层之外以前未经探索的区域。” “一个大惊喜是我们的太阳对星际空间的影响程度，一直到航海者一号。太阳的影响在哪里结束，原始星际空间从哪里开始？也许航海者号可以坚持足够长的时间来回答这个问题。”

paras.en: Creative engineering solutions have enabled the probes to conserve energy and overcome challenges related to aging hardware, including clogged thrusters and a malfunctioning computer on the spacecraft. Earlier this year, engineers successfully turned off three devices on Voyager 1 and substituted them with three lower-power alternatives — a move not without risk — to help the spacecraft make the most of its 50-year-old radioisotope thermal generator. Essentially a nuclear battery, the generator converts heat from decaying plutonium into electricity.
paras.zh: 创造性的工程解决方案使探测器能够节省能源并克服与硬件老化相关的挑战，包括推进器堵塞和航天器上的计算机故障。今年早些时候，工程师成功关闭了航行者一号上的三个设备，并用三个功率较低的替代品代替它们——此举并非没有风险——以帮助航天器充分利用其已有 50 年历史的放射性同位素热发生器。发电机本质上是一个核电池，将衰变的钚产生的热量转化为电能。

paras.en: With the plutonium supply continually depleting, both Voyager probes lose about 4 watts of power each year. The latest energy-saving effort is expected to provide enough power for both spacecraft to keep their current suite of science instruments operating until at least their 50th launch anniversaries next summer.
paras.zh: 随着钚供应不断耗尽，两个 Voyager 探测器每年都会损失约 4 瓦的电力。最新的节能工作预计将为这两个航天器提供足够的电力，以保证其当前的科学仪器套件至少在明年夏天发射 50 周年之前保持运行。

paras.en: As with all NASA spacecraft that venture to and beyond the Moon, communication between Earth and the Voyager probes is managed by the agency’s Deep Space Network, large antennas located at three facilities around the world.
paras.zh: 与所有前往和超越月球的美国宇航局航天器一样，地球和旅行者号探测器之间的通信由该机构的深空网络管理，该网络是位于世界各地三个设施的大型天线。

paras.en: “We listen to Voyager 1 every day and send commands to the spacecraft weekly. It just takes a little longer to communicate than it used to,” said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL. “Even traveling at the speed of light, signals now take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and 24 hours to reach us. One day in the future, when it can no longer communicate with Earth, Voyager 1 will become humanity’s silent ambassador to the stars.”
paras.zh: “我们每天都会收听航行者 1 号，每周都会向航天器发送命令。只是沟通时间比以前要长一点，”喷气推进实验室航行者号项目经理苏珊娜·多德 (Suzanne Dodd) 说道。 “即使以光速行进，信号现在也需要 24 小时才能到达飞船，也需要 24 小时才能到达我们。在未来的某一天，当它不再能与地球通讯时，航海家一号将成为人类无声的星际大使。”

articles.title: The Stormy Southwest Pacific

paras.en: Even as the unusually quiet 2026 storm season winds down in the North Atlantic, seas have begun to stir on the other side of the world in the Southwest Pacific. On November 15, 2026, the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades.
paras.zh: 尽管 2026 年北大西洋异常平静的风暴季节即将结束，但世界另一端西南太平洋的海水却开始骚动起来。 2026 年 11 月 15 日，斐济气象局开始发布有关萨摩亚和库克群岛东北部缓慢移动的热带扰动的最新信息。短短几天内，它就成为该地区几十年来最强烈的 11 月热带气旋之一。

paras.en: Named Xavier, the system intensified rapidly, thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones. Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati, a short-lived storm that emerged in October.
paras.zh: 该系统被命名为“泽维尔”，它的强度迅速增强，在风切变最小、海面温度高达 29 摄氏度（84 华氏度）的环境中蓬勃发展，远高于维持和加强正在发展的热带气旋所需的阈值。泽维尔是该盆地本季第二个被命名的风暴，仅次于 10 月份出现的短暂风暴瓦蒂。

paras.en: As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data showed the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June.
paras.zh: 随着泽维尔的发展，美国宇航局卫星数据显示，这场风暴沿着从南美洲西海岸到太平洋中部的巨大温水舌的西南边缘翻腾，这是自六月以来该地区出现的厄尔尼诺现象的明显迹象。

paras.en: When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale.
paras.zh: 当美国宇航局 Aqua 卫星上的 MODIS（中分辨率成像光谱仪）于 2026 年 11 月 17 日世界时间 02:53（库克群岛时间 11 月 16 日下午 4:53）拍摄到这张图像时，预报员估计泽维尔的最大风速约为每小时 195 公里（120 英里）。当天晚些时候，风速达到每小时 220 公里（140 英里）的峰值强度，根据该地区使用的气旋强度等级为 5 级风暴，根据萨菲尔-辛普森等级为 4 级风暴。

paras.en: The storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach. Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also shows that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace.
paras.zh: 科罗拉多州立大学飓风专家 Phil Klotzbach 指出，这场风暴是国际日期变更线以东有记录以来最强的 11 月热带气旋。泽维尔在库克群岛北部附近的日期变更线以东形成是不寻常的，但其偏东的位置与研究一致，表明该地区的风暴活动通常在厄尔尼诺年期间向东北方向移动。研究还表明，厄尔尼诺现象往往会加剧风暴，并以异常快的速度增强。

paras.en: According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa.
paras.zh: 据新闻报道，泽维尔在经过库克群岛北部时损坏了房屋并造成电力中断。随后遇到干燥空气和不太有利的风切变环境，在向西推进的过程中逐渐减弱，减少了对萨摩亚和美属萨摩亚的威胁。

paras.en: Xavier is likely one of the first of several storms to affect the region in the coming months. A seasonal outlook from the Fiji Meteorological Service projects that the region could see between 11 and 15 named tropical cyclones this season, with the greatest risk east of the international date line. Storm activity in the Southwest Pacific basin typically peaks in February.
paras.zh: 泽维尔可能是未来几个月影响该地区的几场风暴中的第一场。斐济气象局的季节性展望预计，本季节该地区可能会出现 11 至 15 个热带气旋，其中国际日期变更线以东的风险最大。西南太平洋盆地的风暴活动通常在二月达到顶峰。
