Rebecca Lindsey predicts it would take at least seven employees and $1.8 million annually to resume 80 percent of the old site’s work. “Climate.gov was more than just a website; it was a climate literacy program,” she says. To rescue the full mission, they still have a long way to go.
paras.zh: 尽管他们对自己的工作感到自豪，但该项目只是一个补丁，而不是修复。丽贝卡·林赛 (Rebecca Lindsey) 预计，每年至少需要 7 名员工和 180 万美元才能恢复旧站点 80% 的工作。 “Climate.gov 不仅仅是一个网站；它还是一个气候知识项目，”她说。要想完成完整的救援任务，他们还有很长的路要走。

paras.en: The Lindsey sisters are far from the only tale of makeshift resilience. Over the last year, untold numbers of U.S. scientists and their supporters have rebuilt data dashboards, formed recommendation groups for childhood vaccines and screenings, and doled out research funds for hundreds of stranded early-career scientists. They’ve reconstituted committees to advise space missions, rehomed key reports on climate and Arctic science, and even turned to social media to spread public health alerts in the wake of a massive realignment of the federal science enterprise.
paras.zh: 林赛姐妹并不是唯一一个临时恢复的故事。去年，无数美国科学家及其支持者重建了数据仪表板，成立了儿童疫苗和筛查推荐小组，并为数百名陷入困境的早期职业科学家发放了研究资金。他们重组了委员会来为太空任务提供建议，重新调整有关气候和北极科学的重要报告，甚至在联邦科学事业大规模重组后利用社交媒体来传播公共卫生警报。

paras.en: “I don’t think anyone could have foreseen the amount of destruction and deliberate breaking down of norms and infrastructure” over the last two years, says Christina Madison, a clinical pharmacist and public health communicator known on social media as The Public Health Pharmacist.
paras.zh: 在社交媒体上被称为“公共卫生药剂师”的临床药剂师和公共卫生传播者克里斯蒂娜·麦迪逊（Christina Madison）表示，“我认为没有人能够预见到过去两年中破坏的程度以及对规范和基础设施的故意破坏”。

paras.en: Since January 2025, the second Trump administration has frozen or rescinded billions of dollars in research funding on topics from climate change to vaccine hesitancy and is trying to redirect it — often without congressional approval — to administration priorities such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing. During deliberations for the FY2026 and FY2027 budgets, the White House proposed slashing future science funding by one-third.
paras.zh: 自 2025 年 1 月以来，特朗普第二届政府冻结或取消了数十亿美元的研究经费，涉及气候变化、疫苗犹豫等话题，并试图将其（通常未经国会批准）转向人工智能和量子计算等政府优先事项。在审议 2026 财年和 2027 财年预算时，白宫提议将未来的科学经费削减三分之一。

paras.en: “When this was first starting, it really, truly felt like an alternate universe,” says Sean O’Leary, a pediatric infectious disease researcher at the University of Colorado Anschutz. “The science was always what drove the decision making, and now we’re at a place where it’s not.”
paras.zh: 科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校的儿科传染病研究员肖恩·奥利里 (Sean O’Leary) 表示：“当这一切刚开始时，真的感觉就像是另一个宇宙。” “科学始终是推动决策的因素，但现在我们却处于一个并非如此的境地。”

paras.en: In 2025 alone, the federal government shed some 20 percent
paras.zh: 仅 2025 年，联邦政府就削减了约 20%

paras.en: of its science workforce. And in May 2026, the Office of Management and Budget proposed a sweeping set of rules to expand the authority of federal political appointees in selecting science grants.
paras.zh: 其科学劳动力。 2026 年 5 月，管理和预算办公室提出了一套全面的规则，以扩大联邦政治任命人员在选择科学拨款方面的权力。

paras.en: Approximate proportion of the scientific workforce who left federal service in 2025
paras.zh: 2025 年离开联邦服务的科学工作者的大致比例

paras.en: Yet some researchers see the destruction as an opportunity to rebuild their corners of U.S. science — or even reimagine it, says Michael Osterholm, an epidemiologist at the University of Minnesota in Minneapolis. “If there’s any good that can come out of what has been a horrible situation, it’s that it’s given us time and provided a pause to think through clearly: Is this the way we want to continue?”
paras.zh: 然而，明尼阿波利斯明尼苏达大学的流行病学家迈克尔·奥斯特霍尔姆表示，一些研究人员将这次破坏视为重建美国科学角落的机会，甚至重新构想它。 “如果说可怕的局势能带来什么好处的话，那就是它给了我们时间，让我们有时间停下来清楚地思考：这是我们想要继续的方式吗？”

paras.en: University of Ottawa ecologist Julien Martin spent a decade building a respected lab that probed how social behaviors affect the evolution of bushy-tailed, cat-sized rodents called marmots. So when the National Science Foundation began its sweeping grant cuts, Martin found himself doing something unexpected: uploading cute marmot videos to OnlyFans, an online video subscription platform better known for hosting pornography.
paras.zh: 渥太华大学生态学家朱利安·马丁花了十年时间建立了一个受人尊敬的实验室，该实验室研究社会行为如何影响毛尾、猫大小的啮齿动物（土拨鼠）的进化。因此，当国家科学基金会开始大幅削减拨款时，马丁发现自己做了一些意想不到的事情：将可爱的土拨鼠视频上传到 OnlyFans，这是一个以托管色情内容而闻名的在线视频订阅平台。

paras.en: The effort, called OnlyMarms, netted $6,000 — a mere drop in the funding bucket. But the project went viral, leading outside supporters to launch a cryptocurrency token that earned the lab an additional $150,000. And direct donations, including an anonymous $300,000 gift, gave the lab enough to fund one Ph.D. student’s entire degree.
paras.zh: 这项名为 OnlyMarms 的项目筹集了 6,000 美元——这只是资金桶中的九牛一毛。但该项目迅速走红，导致外部支持者推出了加密货币代币，为实验室额外赚取了 15 万美元。直接捐赠，包括匿名的 30 万美元捐赠，为实验室提供了足够的资金资助一名博士生。学生的整个学位。

paras.en: “When you see that so much money could be obtained by doing essentially nothing about science, it’s quite shocking,” Martin says. He welcomes the support, but having to spend so much time on non-research tasks has also felt demeaning. “Sometimes, you have to question: Is the science funding broken? Are we just competing for pennies?”
paras.zh: “当你看到对科学基本上不做任何事情就能获得这么多钱时，这是相当令人震惊的，”马丁说。他对这种支持表示欢迎，但不得不在非研究任务上花费如此多的时间也让他感到有失尊严。 “有时候，你不得不问：科学资助是否被打破？我们只是为了几分钱而竞争吗？”

paras.en: In 2025, the National Institutes of Health and the NSF canceled or suspended more than 7,800 existing grants, totaling billions of dollars. (Some 5,200 grants were later reinstated.) Each agency issued roughly a quarter fewer grants in 2025 than their previous 10-year averages.
paras.zh: 2025 年，美国国立卫生研究院和美国国家科学基金会取消或暂停了 7,800 多项现有拨款，总额达数十亿美元。 （后来恢复了约 5,200 项拨款。）每个机构在 2025 年发放的拨款比之前 10 年平均水平大约减少四分之一。

paras.en: Universities and research centers were hit hard. “It was really dire,” says Emily Young, who leads medical research grantmaking at the San Diego-based Prebys Foundation. In phone calls with researchers, many told her they had halted ongoing experiments, such as developing measles vaccines for people with autoimmune disorders.
paras.zh: 大学和研究中心受到重创。 “这真的很可怕，”圣地亚哥普雷比斯基金会医学研究资助负责人艾米丽·杨 (Emily Young) 说。在与研究人员的电话中，许多人告诉她，他们已经停止了正在进行的实验，例如为患有自身免疫性疾病的人开发麻疹疫苗。

paras.en: But the thing that really stood out, Young says, was how the sudden drop in funding was affecting postdocs and early-career researchers. “Young people were going from feeling like they had an avenue for a really promising career … to feeling like they were in a worthless career.”
paras.zh: 但杨说，真正引人注目的是资金的突然减少对博士后和早期职业研究人员的影响。 “年轻人从感觉自己有一条通往真正有前途的职业的道路……到感觉自己的职业毫无价值。”

paras.en: So, in May 2025, the foundation awarded $7 million total in emergency grants to seven local institutions, including San Diego State University, the University of California, San Diego and Scripps Research. The grants targeted more than 80 research programs involving early- and mid-career scientists that were facing hundreds of millions of dollars in lost federal funding.
paras.zh: 因此，2025 年 5 月，该基金会向圣地亚哥州立大学、加州大学圣地亚哥分校和斯克里普斯研究中心等 7 个当地机构提供了总计 700 万美元的紧急赠款。这些赠款针对了 80 多个研究项目，涉及职业生涯早期和中期的科学家，这些项目面临着数亿美元的联邦资金损失。

paras.en: Larger science philanthropies also stepped into the breach. The Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation gave $55 million total to 30 universities to support 400 postdoctoral researchers. The Alfred P. Sloan and Spencer foundations, among others, partnered to provide 83 quick-turnaround grants of around $25,000 each to researchers whose NSF education grants had been canceled.
paras.zh: 更大的科学慈善机构也介入了这一缺口。戈登和贝蒂摩尔基金会向 30 所大学总共捐赠了 5500 万美元，支持 400 名博士后研究人员。 Alfred P. Sloan 和 Spencer 基金会等合作，向 NSF 教育补助金被取消的研究人员提供了 83 笔快速周转补助金，每人约 25,000 美元。

paras.en: Some wealthy universities also offered bridge funding to their researchers; Johns Hopkins University gave awards up to $250,000 to individuals with unexpected funding gaps, and the Yale School of Medicine arranged to fund up to 90 percent of terminated or frozen NIH grants.
paras.zh: 一些富裕的大学还为其研究人员提供过桥资助；约翰·霍普金斯大学向出现意外资金缺口的个人提供了高达 25 万美元的奖励，耶鲁大学医学院则安排为 90% 的终止或冻结的 NIH 拨款提供资金。

paras.en: After the first bout of funding chaos, science philanthropy Schmidt Sciences announced a more ambitious approach: to develop the science themselves. In January 2026, they revealed plans to construct three ground-based observatories and a space telescope larger than NASA’s Hubble by the end of the decade. The space telescope alone will cost hundreds of millions of dollars and provide open-access data to scientists worldwide, with a special focus on exoplanets and transient events like supernovas.
paras.zh: 在第一轮资金混乱之后，科学慈善机构施密特科学公司宣布了一个更加雄心勃勃的方法：自行发展科学。 2026 年 1 月，他们透露了计划在本世纪末建造三个地面观测站和一个比 NASA 哈勃望远镜还要大的太空望远镜。仅太空望远镜就将耗资数亿美元，并向全世界科学家提供开放获取的数据，特别关注系外行星和超新星等瞬态事件。

paras.en: In November 2026, the philanthropy opened its first round of funding for early-career scientists using the observatory system; individual awards will total up to $2.5 million each.
paras.zh: 2026 年 11 月，该慈善机构为使用天文台系统的早期职业科学家启动了第一轮资助；每项个人奖金总额最高可达 250 万美元。

paras.en: “Originally, the hope was we would play a more classic philanthropic role,” says Arpita Roy, an astronomer who directs the Astrophysics & Space Center at Schmidt Sciences. But given the federal funding landscape, she says, “it became pretty clear to us, if we really think these things need to exist in the world … then we need to build them out.”
paras.zh: “最初，我们希望能够扮演一个更经典的慈善角色，”施密特科学公司天体物理与太空中心的天文学家阿皮塔·罗伊 (Arpita Roy) 说。但考虑到联邦资金的情况，她说，“我们很清楚，如果我们真的认为这些东西需要存在于世界上……那么我们就需要建造它们。”

paras.en: While private funding can be a lifeline, Young says, it’s still a temporary measure at best. “We are not going to fill the vacuum of federal funding,” she says. “There is simply not enough philanthropic resource out there to do that.”
paras.zh: 杨说，虽然私人资金可以成为生命线，但它充其量也只是一种临时措施。 “我们不会填补联邦资金的真空，”她说。 “根本没有足够的慈善资源来做到这一点。”

paras.en: In 1995, the American Academy of Pediatrics and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention made a consequential decision: Rather than publish independent recommendations for childhood vaccines, as they had since the 1960s, they would issue one set jointly. Over the next 30 years, a group called the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices advised the CDC, with academy input, to expand its recommendations to include chickenpox, hepatitis A and pneumococcal infections. Cases of the three dropped by more than 90 percent, saving thousands of lives.
paras.zh: 1995 年，美国儿科学会和疾病控制与预防中心做出了一项重大决定：他们不再像 20 世纪 60 年代以来那样发布针对儿童疫苗的独立建议，而是联合发布一套。在接下来的 30 年里，一个名为免疫实践咨询委员会的组织建议 CDC 在学术界的投入下扩大其建议范围，将水痘、甲型肝炎和肺炎球菌感染包括在内。这三人的病例下降了 90% 以上，挽救了数千人的生命。

paras.en: But in June 2025, Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an outspoken vaccine critic, fired all 17 members of ACIP and replaced many with vaccine skeptics. Kennedy also dismissed the academy representatives that informed the group.
paras.zh: 但在 2025 年 6 月，直言不讳的疫苗批评者、卫生与公众服务部部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪解雇了 ACIP 的全部 17 名成员，并用疫苗怀疑论者取代了许多成员。肯尼迪还解雇了向该组织通报情况的学院代表。

paras.en: “Essentially, we had no voice anymore,” recalls O’Leary, the pediatric infectious disease researcher at the University of Colorado Anschutz. He also serves as the AAP’s immunization schedule editor. “So we made a decision to not participate until we could say, ‘OK, this is a body that can be trusted.’ ”
paras.zh: “从本质上讲，我们不再有发言权了，”科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校的儿科传染病研究员奥利里回忆道。他还担任 AAP 的免疫接种计划编辑。 “所以我们决定不参加，直到我们可以说，‘好吧，这是一个可以信任的机构。’”

paras.en: In July 2025, the academy and other public health groups sued over the ACIP firings. The committee was unable to meet due to the lawsuit, and over the next six months, the CDC removed recommendations from its childhood vaccination schedule including hepatitis A and B, COVID-19 and meningococcal disease. The American Academy of Pediatrics issued its own schedule including those vaccines in January 2026.
paras.zh: 2025 年 7 月，学院和其他公共卫生组织就 ACIP 解雇事件提起诉讼。由于诉讼，该委员会无法召开会议，在接下来的六个月里，疾病预防控制中心从其儿童疫苗接种计划中删除了建议，包括甲型和乙型肝炎、COVID-19 和脑膜炎球菌病。美国儿科学会于 2026 年 1 月发布了自己的时间表，其中包括这些疫苗。

paras.en: The loss of trustworthy federal recommendations leaves “an impossible gap to fill,” O’Leary says. But when it came to stepping in, “from my perspective, there was not an alternative.” The academy has since collaborated with the Vaccine Integrity Project, a new group led by Osterholm, to conduct the scientific reviews that inform vaccine recommendations.
paras.zh: 奥利里说，失去值得信赖的联邦建议留下了“一个无法填补的空白”。但当谈到介入时，“从我的角度来看，没有其他选择。”此后，该学院与奥斯特霍尔姆领导的新组织疫苗完整性项目合作，进行科学审查，为疫苗建议提供信息。

paras.en: Vaccines weren’t the only childhood health matter to get a shakeup. In April 2025, HHS terminated the Advisory Committee on Heritable Disorders in Newborns and Children, which formulates newborn screening recommendations for genetic disorders, many of which can be deadly or disabling. Currently, some 98 percent of U.S.-born infants are screened at birth.
paras.zh: 疫苗并不是唯一一个需要改变的儿童健康问题。 2025 年 4 月，HHS 终止了新生儿和儿童遗传性疾病咨询委员会，该委员会负责制定针对遗传性疾病的新生儿筛查建议，其中许多遗传性疾病可能是致命的或致残的。目前，约 98% 的美国出生婴儿在出生时接受了筛查。

paras.en: When the genetics community raised concerns, Cynthia Powell, a retired pediatric geneticist at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine in Chapel Hill, gathered around 15 representatives of professional medical societies to create the Newborn Screening Collaborative. With support from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics, the group began meeting in early 2026.
paras.zh: 当遗传学界提出担忧时，北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校医学院的退休儿科遗传学家 Cynthia Powell 召集了大约 15 名专业医学会的代表，创建了新生儿筛查合作组织。在美国医学遗传学和基因组学学院的支持下，该小组于 2026 年初开始召开会议。

paras.en: While the collaborative cannot give direct recommendations to HHS, it hopes to conduct evidence reviews for states and the small, parent-led advocacy groups that form around rare diseases, Powell says. It plans to focus on conditions that already have treatments under development, like a rare metabolic disorder known as Sanfilippo syndrome type A.
paras.zh: 鲍威尔说，虽然该合作组织无法向美国卫生与公众服务部提供直接建议，但它希望为各州以及围绕罕见疾病组成的小型、由家长领导的倡导团体进行证据审查。它计划重点关注已经有正在开发的治疗方法的疾病，例如一种被称为 A 型 Sanfilippo 综合征的罕见代谢性疾病。

paras.en: Approximate number of NIH and NSF grants canceled or suspended in 2025. Some 5,200 have since been reinstated
paras.zh: 2025 年取消或暂停的 NIH 和 NSF 拨款的大约数量。此后约有 5,200 项拨款已恢复

paras.en: “This Newborn Screening Collaborative is another effort not to leave a complete void,” says Jewel Mullen, an epidemiologist at the University of Texas at Austin who was lead editor on a May 2025 newborn screening report for the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的流行病学家 Jewel Mullen 说：“这个新生儿筛查合作组织是为了不留下完全空白而做出的另一项努力。”他是美国国家科学、工程和医学院 2025 年 5 月新生儿筛查报告的主编。

paras.en: Other researchers are filling gaps in awareness about public health threats. A philanthropy-backed group called the Evidence Collective posted about the diarrhea-causing cyclosporiasis outbreak before the CDC’s Health Alert Network did. The collective, made up of more than 30 medical communicators, has more than 10 million followers across social media and notched 11 billion impressions in 2025.
paras.zh: 其他研究人员正在填补人们对公共卫生威胁的认识空白。一个名为 Evidence Collective 的慈善组织在疾病预防控制中心的健康警报网络发布之前发布了有关导致腹泻的环孢子虫病爆发的信息。该团体由 30 多名医疗传播者组成，在社交媒体上拥有超过 1000 万粉丝，到 2025 年曝光量将达到 110 亿次。

paras.en: “I don’t think that we will ever be able to fully replace the infrastructure that was there through the federal government,” says Madison, a founding member of the collective. But “there is a concerted effort now to look at: How do we take the momentum that we have with these organizations, and then make it sustainable?”
paras.zh: “我认为我们永远无法完全取代联邦政府现有的基础设施，”该集体的创始成员麦迪逊说。但“现在需要共同努力：我们如何利用与这些组织的合作势头，然后使其可持续发展？”

paras.en: Although stopgap measures are succeeding so far, scientists see them as Band-Aids at best. “We’re going to do it for as long as we’re needed,” Osterholm says. But “I look forward to the day when we’re not going to be needed anymore.”
paras.zh: 尽管权宜之计到目前为止取得了成功，但科学家们认为它们充其量只是创可贴。 “只要需要，我们就会这样做，”奥斯特霍尔姆说。但“我期待着有一天不再需要我们。”

paras.en: In April 2025, nearly 400 scientists working on the National Climate Assessment, a recurring, congressionally mandated report, received an email that it was being reevaluated and they were being released from their work. One of them — Rutgers University climate scientist Bob Kopp — wasn’t surprised. “I don’t think you have to speculate very far” to know why, Kopp says. He cites a directive in the White House’s 2027 budget request to “stop wasting biological and environmental research resources on climate change.”
paras.zh: 2025 年 4 月，近 400 名从事国家气候评估（国会授权的定期报告）工作的科学家收到一封电子邮件，称该报告正在重新评估，他们的工作将被解除。其中一位——罗格斯大学气候科学家鲍勃·科普——对此并不感到惊讶。科普说，“我认为你不必进行太多推测”就能知道原因。他引用了白宫 2027 年预算请求中的一项指令，即“停止在气候变化问题上浪费生物和环境研究资源”。

paras.en: However, “there was an immediate and deep sentiment by the science community to continue the work,” says environmental engineer Costa Samaras of Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh, who had also been involved with the climate report. He and colleagues asked the American Geophysical Union and the American Meteorological Society to help organize the U.S. Climate Collection, a new set of papers from scientists about climate research, risks and solutions that will keep the public informed until federal assessments resume.
paras.zh: 然而，“科学界立即强烈地希望继续这项工作，”匹兹堡卡内基梅隆大学的环境工程师科斯塔·萨马拉斯说，他也参与了气候报告的编写。他和同事请求美国地球物理联盟和美国气象学会帮助组织美国气候收集，这是一组由科学家撰写的关于气候研究、风险和解决方案的新论文，将在联邦评估恢复之前向公众通报情况。

paras.en: While the work is promising, “a volunteer effort of 170 scientists cannot substitute for a $30 million effort of 600 people,” Kopp says.
paras.zh: 尽管这项工作前景广阔，但“170 名科学家的志愿者努力无法替代 600 人花费 3000 万美元的努力，”Kopp 说。

paras.en: The American Geophysical Union similarly stepped in with crucial financing for the Arctic Report Card, an annual report from NOAA that has provided information about the changing Arctic since 2006. Its editors were blindsided when they found out during a routine meeting in August 2026 that NOAA was withdrawing its support.
paras.zh: 美国地球物理联盟同样介入，为《北极报告卡》提供了重要资金，这是 NOAA 的一份年度报告，提供了自 2006 年以来有关北极变化的信息。当其编辑在 2026 年 8 月的例行会议上发现 NOAA 正在撤回其支持时，他们大吃一惊。

paras.en: AGU’s in-kind offer to support the project just one month later was “tremendous,” says Twila Moon, a glaciologist at the National Snow and Ice Data Center in Boulder, Colo., who edits the report card. “But [it] is not a kind of model that is sustainable into the future.”
paras.zh: 科罗拉多州博尔德国家冰雪数据中心的冰川学家、负责编辑报告单的特威拉·穆恩 (Twila Moon) 表示，仅仅一个月后，AGU 就为该项目提供了“巨大的实物支持”。 “但[它]并不是一种可以持续到未来的模式。”

paras.en: AGU President Brandon Jones agrees. Nevertheless, at the time, the organization “had this sense of what was moral, what was right, what was ethical,” Jones says. And given AGU’s resources, “it seemed like it was our turn to show up and step up and act like the union that we’ve always been.”
paras.zh: AGU 主席布兰登·琼斯对此表示同意。尽管如此，琼斯说，当时该组织“对什么是道德、什么是正确、什么是道德有这种感觉”。考虑到 AGU 的资源，“看来现在轮到我们站出来，像我们一直以来的工会一样行事了。”

paras.en: The Planetary Society, a nonprofit space advocacy organization based in Pasadena, Calif., took the lead on several committees that NASA dropped. In January, the agency cited executive orders as it withdrew financial and logistical support from eight groups of space scientists and experts that advised NASA’s planning teams on exploring asteroids, comets and planets.
paras.zh: 行星协会是一家总部位于加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳的非营利性太空倡导组织，它在美国宇航局放弃的几个委员会中发挥了带头作用。一月份，该机构援引行政命令，撤回了八组空间科学家和专家的财务和后勤支持，这些专家组为 NASA 规划团队探索小行星、彗星和行星提供建议。

paras.en: “It was pretty well-managed and organized [before], and then really fell apart because of the intrusion of the executive orders,” says Jack Kiraly, chief of advocacy at the Planetary Society. The organization now hosts the advisory groups’ websites, documents and meetings. “We’ve basically been having to reinvent this whole system.”
paras.zh: 行星协会的宣传主管杰克·基拉利（Jack Kiraly）表示：“（之前）管理和组织得相当好，但后来由于行政命令的介入而真正崩溃了。”该组织现在托管咨询小组的网站、文件和会议。 “我们基本上不得不重新发明整个系统。”

paras.en: Climate.us isn’t the only site saving federal data. In November 2024, many environmental organizations “started preparing for the worst,” says Brittany Janis, executive director of the Open Environmental Data Project. Her group and nine others banded together to create the Public Environmental Data Partners, a network of 400 volunteers that archive environmental data and tools they suspected “would probably be on the chopping block.”
paras.zh: Climate.us 并不是唯一保存联邦数据的网站。开放环境数据项目执行董事布列塔尼·贾尼斯 (Brittany Janis) 表示，2024 年 11 月，许多环保组织“开始为最坏的情况做准备”。她的团队和其他九个人联合起来创建了公共环境数据合作伙伴，这是一个由 400 名志愿者组成的网络，负责归档他们怀疑“可能会被砍掉”的环境数据和工具。

paras.en: In February 2025, the Environmental Protection Agency deleted a tool called EJScreen, which maps places where people face high levels of risk from environmental burdens such as hazardous waste and ozone. Within 48 hours, the partnership had stood up EJScreen on a new website, using open-source files to reverse engineer and refine the data pipelines. It has since received 1,000 views a month, Janis says.
paras.zh: 2025 年 2 月，环境保护局删除了一个名为 EJScreen 的工具，该工具绘制了人们面临危险废物和臭氧等环境负担高风险的地方。 48 小时内，合作伙伴就在新网站上建立了 EJScreen，使用开源文件进行逆向工程和完善数据管道。 Janis 说，此后每月有 1,000 次浏览。

paras.en: Nearly $2 million in philanthropic funding has helped the project pay staff, host data and hire engineers. It has restored the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Future Risk Index, which projects county-level economic losses from climate change; the White House Council on Environmental Quality’s Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool, which identifies communities overburdened by pollution; and the Department of Homeland Security’s Homeland Infrastructure Foundation-Level Data tool, which maps infrastructure at risk of natural disasters.
paras.zh: 近 200 万美元的慈善资金帮助该项目支付员工工资、托管数据和雇用工程师。它恢复了联邦紧急事务管理局的未来风险指数，该指数预测了气候变化造成的县级经济损失；白宫环境质量委员会的气候和经济正义筛查工具，该工具可识别污染负担过重的社区；国土安全部的国土基础设施基础级数据工具，用于绘制面临自然灾害风险的基础设施地图。

paras.en: “We should not misunderstand the administration’s closing off of this data [to mean] that they don’t think data is important,” Janis says. “They recognize how important it is — and how valuable it is to causes that they disagree with.”
paras.zh: “我们不应该误解政府关闭这些数据[意味着]他们认为数据不重要，”贾尼斯说。 “他们认识到它的重要性，以及它对于他们不同意的事业的价值。”

paras.en: At the University of Chicago, the Data Mirror Project preserves datasets larger than one terabyte, including those from the U.S. Census Bureau and the National Park Service. The project has a guiding principle: LOCKSS, which stands for lots of copies keeps stuff safe, says colead Lisa Chinn, who is head of research data services at the university library. An agency doesn’t have to delete its data to create problems, she adds. Firing website staff can lead to wonky links, corrupted files and pages that degrade into Wingdings gibberish.
paras.zh: 在芝加哥大学，数据镜像项目保存了超过 1 TB 的数据集，包括来自美国人口普查局和国家公园管理局的数据集。该项目有一个指导原则：LOCKSS，代表大量副本，保证资料安全，该大学图书馆研究数据服务主管、共同负责人丽莎·钦 (Lisa Chinn) 说。她补充说，机构不必删除其数据来制造问题。解雇网站员工可能会导致链接不稳定、文件损坏以及页面退化为 Wingdings 乱码。

paras.en: The thought of losing all that data can be stressful, Janis says, but “there’s a lot of parachutes that have gone out.”
paras.zh: 贾尼斯说，一想到丢失所有数据就会感到压力很大，但“有很多降落伞已经失效了。”

paras.en: Even as researchers, volunteers and scientific organizations pick up the pieces of the federal science enterprise, some are already imagining new ways of shaping it. “The world was not perfect in 2024,” says Rutgers’ Kopp. “Reconstruction is an opportunity to improve upon the way things are done.”
paras.zh: 尽管研究人员、志愿者和科学组织正在收拾联邦科学事业的碎片，但有些人已经在想象塑造它的新方法。 “2024 年的世界并不完美，”罗格斯大学的科普说。 “重建是改进工作方式的机会。”

paras.en: To Mullen, the epidemiologist at the University of Texas at Austin, transparency is key. New bodies like the Vaccine Integrity Project and the Newborn Screening Collaborative should make their meetings and deliberations as open as possible, she says, especially when “people think that those with the loudest voices or the biggest wallets are going to be the ones that have the greatest influence behind the scenes.”
paras.zh: 对于德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的流行病学家马伦来说，透明度是关键。她说，像疫苗完整性项目和新生儿筛查合作组织这样的新机构应该让他们的会议和审议尽可能公开，尤其是当“人们认为那些声音最大或财力最大的人将是在幕后影响力最大的人”时。

paras.en: Powell, of the Newborn Screening Collaborative, is hoping for greater efficiency in the disease recommendation process. Previously, it could take as long as three years to bring a condition from an initial vote to a final recommendation; with the collaborative, she hopes it could take one to three months.
paras.zh: 新生儿筛查合作组织的鲍威尔希望提高疾病推荐过程的效率。此前，一项条件从最初投票到最终建议可能需要长达三年的时间；通过合作，她希望能够花费一到三个月的时间。

paras.en: Janis, of the Open Environmental Data Project, hopes to develop more creative and flexible data tools for researchers based on their needs. And Madison from the Evidence Collective and Martin of OnlyMarms believe that the science infrastructure needs to diversify its funding sources to prevent future shocks.
paras.zh: 开放环境数据项目的Janis希望根据研究人员的需求，为他们开发更具创意、更灵活的数据工具。 Evidence Collective 的麦迪逊和 OnlyMarms 的马丁认为，科学基础设施需要使其资金来源多样化，以防止未来的冲击。

paras.en: However, Janis notes that there are inherent risks in having the private sector support public goods such as open information. And Kopp warns that “attempts to replace something that was well-functioning … are not going to necessarily end up with something that is better or even as good as what was there before.”
paras.zh: 然而，贾尼斯指出，让私营部门支持开放信息等公共产品存在固有的风险。科普警告说，“尝试取代运行良好的东西……最终不一定会得到比以前更好甚至一样好的东西。”

paras.en: At the end of the day, one of the key elements in establishing a new science system is “faith that you will still exist in a year or 10 years or maybe even 20 years,” says Katharine Jacobs, an environmental scientist who directed a previous National Climate Assessment under President Obama. Without stable institutional funding, “we are all essentially wasting our time, bashing our heads against the wall, trying to create a system that we can’t support,” Jacobs says.
paras.zh: 归根结底，建立新科学体系的关键要素之一是“相信一年、十年甚至二十年后你仍然会存在”，曾指导奥巴马总统领导下的国家气候评估的环境科学家凯瑟琳·雅各布斯 (Katharine Jacobs) 说。雅各布斯说，如果没有稳定的机构资金，“我们基本上都是在浪费时间，把头撞在墙上，试图创建一个我们无法支持的体系。”

paras.en: For the Lindsey sisters, being involved in public service — even outside the government aegis — has been empowering, especially during what they see as an otherwise dark period for science.
paras.zh: 对于林赛姐妹来说，参与公共服务——即使是在政府支持之外——一直是一种赋权，尤其是在她们认为科学的黑暗时期。

paras.en: They have raised more than $600,000 from individual donations since August 2025. And in February, they received a one-time grant from the Doris Duke Foundation and others that will cover their salaries and benefits until February 2027.
paras.zh: 自 2025 年 8 月以来，他们已通过个人捐款筹集了超过 60 万美元。今年 2 月，他们收到了 Doris Duke 基金会和其他机构的一次性赠款，该赠款将支付他们直到 2027 年 2 月的工资和福利。

paras.en: “If we can get the money, I can see us doing this indefinitely,” Rebecca Lindsey says. She still hopes to retire one day, and she fights off worries that the government might come knocking about their unsanctioned work. But “we had a public that trusted us,” she says about jumping into the fray. “It was a risk worth taking.”
paras.zh: “如果我们能拿到钱，我可以看到我们无限期地这样做，”丽贝卡·林赛说。她仍然希望有一天能退休，并消除了政府可能会批评他们未经批准的工作的担忧。但“我们有一群信任我们的公众，”她在谈到加入这场争论时说道。 “这是一个值得冒的风险。”

articles.title: U.S. demand for menopause hormone therapy has more than doubled recently
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: More U.S. women are taking menopause hormone therapy, new prescription data suggest.
paras.zh: 新的处方数据显示，越来越多的美国女性正在接受更年期激素疗法。

paras.en: Monthly dispensing of hormone therapy for women aged 40 to 74 more than doubled since 2023, growing from 2 million to 4.9 million, researchers report November 19 in JAMA. The analysis of U.S. pharmacy dispensing data revealed that this increase began in 2024. The rise continued in 2025, before and after the Food and Drug Administration’s November removal of the black box warning from packaging, and into 2026.
paras.zh: 研究人员 11 月 19 日在《美国医学会杂志》上报告称，自 2023 年以来，每月为 40 至 74 岁女性发放激素治疗的人数增加了一倍多，从 200 万增加到 490 万。对美国药房配药数据的分析显示，这种增长始于 2024 年。这种增长持续到 2025 年，即食品和药物管理局 11 月从包装上去除黑框警告之前和之后，一直持续到 2026 年。

paras.en: Although the data in the new study are aggregate, the researchers used population data to estimate the dispensing rate for this age group, which jumped from 28 prescriptions per 1,000 women to 67 prescriptions per 1,000 over the period studied.
paras.zh: 尽管新研究中的数据是汇总的，但研究人员使用人口数据来估计该年龄组的配药率，在研究期间，配药率从每 1,000 名女性 28 处方跃升至每 1,000 名女性 67 处方。

paras.en: The new study wasn’t designed to determine what’s behind the increase. It’s possible that the evidence regarding hormone therapy’s safety and effectiveness for the treatment of menopause symptoms, such as hot flashes, is reaching more women. Medical groups such as the Menopause Society have recommended menopause hormone therapy for women with symptoms who are younger than 60 or within 10 years of the start of menopause, absent certain risk factors including prior breast cancer and stroke.
paras.zh: 这项新研究的目的并不是为了确定这一增长背后的原因。有关激素疗法治疗潮热等更年期症状的安全性和有效性的证据可能正在惠及更多女性。更年期协会等医疗团体建议年龄小于 60 岁或绝经开始后 10 年内有症状的女性接受更年期激素治疗，且不存在某些危险因素，包括既往乳腺癌和中风。

paras.en: “Greater attention to women’s health, updated medical guidance supporting individualized menopause hormone therapy and social media may all be contributing to increased interest,” says Dana Sarnak, who studies sexual and reproductive health at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine. Anecdotally, her clinician colleagues report more patients seeking menopause care, she says.
paras.zh: “对女性健康的更多关注、支持个体化更年期激素治疗的最新医疗指南和社交媒体都可能有助于增加人们的兴趣，”约翰·霍普金斯大学医学院研究性健康和生殖健康的达纳·萨纳克 (Dana Sarnak) 说。她说，有趣的是，她的临床医生同事报告说，越来越多的患者寻求更年期护理。

paras.en: Many women and physicians turned away from hormone therapy in the early 2000s after a large study called the Women’s Health Initiative raised safety concerns, which were later considered overblown. Research since then has provided a more nuanced understanding of the benefits and risks of menopause hormone therapy at different ages.
paras.zh: 2000 年代初，一项名为“女性健康倡议”的大型研究提出了安全问题，之后许多女性和医生放弃了激素治疗，但后来认为该研究有些夸大其词。此后的研究对不同年龄的更年期激素治疗的益处和风险提供了更细致的了解。

paras.en: There are safer formulations, including patches and gels, of estrogen today then at the time of the Women’s Health Initiative, for which participants took a pill. The new study found that product use increased for transdermal and vaginal estrogen and for progesterone products — women who have their uterus need to take progesterone along with estrogen. The use of oral formulations remained stable. There has been a shortage of estrogen patches in the United States this year, which the U.S. Food and Drug Administration attributes to increasing demand.
paras.zh: 现在有更安全的雌激素配方，包括贴剂和凝胶，而在妇女健康倡议时期，参与者服用的是药丸。这项新研究发现，透皮和阴道雌激素以及黄体酮产品的使用量有所增加——有子宫的女性需要在服用雌激素的同时服用黄体酮。口服制剂的使用保持稳定。今年美国出现雌激素贴剂短缺的情况，美国食品和药物管理局将其归因于需求增加。

articles.title: A brain region known for listening helps us speak
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: WASHINGTON — A part of the brain famous for listening is important for talking, too.
paras.zh: 华盛顿——大脑中以倾听闻名的部分对于说话也很重要。

paras.en: Data collected from people as they listen and try to talk show that this brain region, a small spot inside a larger area called Wernicke’s area, has a more expansive job than researchers thought when it comes to communicating. The results may help efforts to restore people’s voices. The results presented November 15 at the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience and published November 19 in Science.
paras.zh: 从人们倾听和尝试说话时收集的数据表明，这个大脑区域是一个名为韦尼克区的较大区域内的一个小点，在交流方面比研究人员想象的更广泛。研究结果可能有助于恢复人们的声音。研究结果于 11 月 15 日在神经科学学会年会上公布，并于 11 月 19 日发表在《科学》杂志上。

paras.en: The study provides convincing evidence that this brain spot is critical for speech production, says neurologist and language researcher Jeffrey Binder of the Medical College of Wisconsin in Milwaukee. “My hope is that this study will help scientists and clinicians accept a more accurate interpretation of this focal area” as an early stop on the pathway to saying a word.
paras.zh: 密尔沃基威斯康星医学院的神经学家和语言研究员杰弗里·宾德说，这项研究提供了令人信服的证据，证明这个大脑斑点对于言语产生至关重要。 “我希望这项研究能够帮助科学家和临床医生接受对这个重点领域的更准确的解释”，作为说话之路的早期终点。

paras.en: A small part of the brain, just above the left ear, was first described in 1874 by a neurologist Carl Wernicke as necessary for making sense of speech. People with damage there had trouble comprehending words. But some people also had trouble producing them. “Sounds were swapped, words were replaced with near misses,” Edward Chang of the University of California, San Francisco, said in a news briefing. “The basic question has been, ‘Why would damage to a hearing area of the brain break the ability to speak?’ That question has been open for 150 years.”
paras.zh: 1874 年，神经学家卡尔·韦尼克 (Carl Wernicke) 首次将大脑左耳上方的一小部分描述为理解言语所必需的部分。那里受到伤害的人无法理解言语。但有些人在生产它们时也遇到了困难。加州大学旧金山分校的爱德华·张（Edward Chang）在新闻发布会上表示：“声音被调换了，语言也被差点儿取代了。” “基本问题是，‘为什么大脑听力区域受损会导致说话能力丧失？’这个问题已经存在了 150 年。”

paras.en: The new research offers an answer: A small bit of Wernicke’s area (to be extremely specific, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus or lpSTG ) becomes active just before a word is spoken. “Every word that you have said today began in that small part above your left ear about a quarter of a second before you said it,” Chang said.
paras.zh: 这项新研究提供了答案：韦尼克区的一小部分（非常具体地说，是左后颞上回或 lpSTG）在说出单词之前变得活跃。 “你今天所说的每一个字都是在你说之前大约四分之一秒开始于你左耳上方的那个小部分的，”张说。

paras.en: The finding adds to growing evidence that brain areas are more complex than people have appreciated, says neuroscientist Leigh Hochberg at Brown University in Providence, R.I. “I believe that one of the things we are going to learn over the next five, 10 years of this research, is that each part of the brain that, we were taught as a med student or a grad student, does this, probably does that and a whole lot more.”
paras.zh: 罗德岛州普罗维登斯布朗大学的神经科学家 Leigh Hochberg 表示，这一发现进一步证明大脑区域比人们想象的更为复杂。“我相信，在接下来的五年、十年的研究中，我们将了解到的一件事是，我们作为医学生或研究生所学到的大脑的每个部分都可以做这个，也可能做那个，甚至更多。”

paras.en: Scientists measured brain activity in 28 people before they had surgery for epilepsy or tumors. They were able to see that this brain region kicked on as a person listened to words, and also just before they attempted to speak. Cells there had preferences for certain sorts of words, long ones, for instance. “It’s more active when you’re about to say the word caterpillar than when you’re about to say the word cat,” said Matthew Leonard, a cognitive neuroscientist at UCSF.
paras.zh: 科学家测量了 28 名接受癫痫或肿瘤手术的人的大脑活动。他们能够看到，当一个人听单词时，以及在他们试图说话之前，这个大脑区域就会启动。那里的细胞对某些类型的单词有偏好，例如长单词。加州大学旧金山分校的认知神经科学家马修·伦纳德 (Matthew Leonard) 表示：“当你要说‘毛毛虫’这个词时，它比当你要说‘猫’这个词时更活跃。”

paras.en: Electrical stimulation to this small bit of brain also interfered with people’s ability to talk. “What we found was that stimulation, really only in this lpSTG area, disrupted this speech production when it was delivered just prior to speaking,” said UCSF bioengineer Alexander Silva.
paras.zh: 对这一小块大脑的电刺激也会干扰人们的说话能力。加州大学旧金山分校生物工程师亚历山大·席尔瓦 (Alexander Silva) 表示：“我们发现，只有在 lpSTG 区域的刺激才会在说话之前扰乱这种言语的产生。”

paras.en: Some efforts to make implanted devices that can help restore speech to people who no longer talk focus on the motor cortex, a part of the brain that controls the movements required for speech. This bit of Wernicke’s area offers an additional spot to consider, Silva said. “What if you could target a single brain region and gain access to the full spectrum of speech, from listening all the way up to speech production?”
paras.zh: 一些制造植入设备的努力可以帮助不再说话的人恢复言语，这些努力集中在运动皮层上，运动皮层是大脑中控制言语所需运动的部分。席尔瓦说，韦尼克的这一区域提供了另一个值得考虑的地方。 “如果你可以针对单个大脑区域并获得从聆听到言语产生的全部语音范围，会怎么样？”

paras.en: Experimental brain implants in two volunteers with paralysis were able to detect both what they heard and what they were trying to say, the researchers report in the study.
paras.zh: 研究人员在研究中报告说，两名瘫痪志愿者的实验性大脑植入物能够检测到他们听到的内容和他们想说的话。

paras.en: The discovery may help scientists better understand situations that involve both hearing and speaking, such as speech or comprehension differences in people with autism, or how children first begin learning to talk, Chang said.
paras.zh: 张说，这一发现可能有助于科学家更好地了解涉及听力和口语的情况，例如自闭症患者的言语或理解差异，或者儿童如何开始学习说话。

articles.title: New Anesthetic Candidate Dulled Pain Responses in Mice Without Putting Them to Sleep
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Losing consciousness during surgery and having pain controlled can seem like the same thing, although anesthesiologists often use different drugs to achieve them.
paras.zh: 尽管麻醉师经常使用不同的药物来实现手术期间失去意识和控制疼痛似乎是同一件事。

paras.en: This leads to the question: could an anesthetic also control pain at a dose low enough to leave an animal awake?
paras.zh: 这就引出了一个问题：麻醉剂能否以足够低的剂量来控制疼痛，使动物保持清醒？

paras.en: Researchers developing a compound called nidradine found signs of that possibility in mice.
paras.zh: 研究人员开发了一种名为尼拉定的化合物，在小鼠身上发现了这种可能性的迹象。

paras.en: At higher doses, the compound produced anesthesia. At a lower dose, the animals remained awake and coordinated, while responding less often to painful heat.
paras.zh: 在较高剂量下，该化合物会产生麻醉作用。在较低剂量下，动物保持清醒和协调，同时对令人痛苦的高温反应较少。

paras.en: "What was most exciting was that the analgesic activity was completely unexpected," University of California, San Francisco researcher Matthew McCarroll told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “最令人兴奋的是镇痛活性完全出乎意料，”加州大学旧金山分校研究员马修·麦卡罗尔告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: The study began with a different goal: finding new general anesthetics. Testing thousands of chemicals in mammals would be slow and costly, so the researchers began their search in tiny zebrafish larvae.
paras.zh: 这项研究始于一个不同的目标：寻找新的全身麻醉剂。在哺乳动物身上测试数千种化学物质既缓慢又昂贵，因此研究人员开始在微小的斑马鱼幼虫中进行研究。

paras.en: These young fish fit into laboratory plates containing 96 small wells. Researchers could add chemicals to the water and automatically record the animals' movements, testing many groups at once.
paras.zh: 这些幼鱼适合放入包含 96 个小孔的实验室平板中。研究人员可以向水中添加化学物质并自动记录动物的动作，同时测试许多组。

paras.en: The team, which included researchers at UCSF and the University of California, San Diego, was looking for one distinctive clue in how the larvae behaved.
paras.zh: 该团队包括加州大学旧金山分校和加州大学圣地亚哥分校的研究人员，他们正在寻找一条有关幼虫行为的独特线索。

paras.en: Under certain test conditions, established anesthetics such as propofol and etomidate make larvae respond more strongly to gentle tapping. Any chemical that reproduced that pattern was worth a closer look.
paras.zh: 在某些测试条件下，已确定的麻醉剂（例如异丙酚和依托咪酯）使幼虫对轻柔的敲击反应更强烈。任何重现这种模式的化学物质都值得仔细研究。

paras.en: Of 12,000 compounds screened, 69 initially matched. Follow-up experiments narrowed the field, including tests in adult fish to identify candidates that also produced anesthesia at a later developmental stage.
paras.zh: 在筛选的 12,000 种化合物中，有 69 种最初匹配。后续实验缩小了研究范围，包括对成年鱼进行测试，以确定在后期发育阶段也能产生麻醉作用的候选者。

paras.en: The researchers then explored related molecules and synthesized 28 chemical variants. One became nidradine.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后探索了相关分子并合成了 28 种化学变体。一种变成了尼拉定。

paras.en: The next step was to find out whether the anesthetic effects extended to mammals. Nidradine reached the brains of mice and temporarily disrupted their righting reflex: animals placed on their backs couldn't turn themselves upright. Researchers commonly use this response to assess anesthetic effects.
paras.zh: 下一步是查明麻醉效果是否适用于哺乳动物。尼拉定到达小鼠大脑并暂时扰乱它们的翻正反射：仰卧的动物无法将自己翻正。研究人员通常使用这种反应来评估麻醉效果。

paras.en: A paw-pinch test revealed another property. At a dose near the level needed to disrupt that reflex, nidradine also prevented mice from withdrawing a paw from a strong pinch. Etomidate did not prevent withdrawal at the comparison dose tested.
paras.zh: 爪子捏测试揭示了另一个特性。当剂量接近破坏这种反射所需的水平时，尼拉定还可以防止小鼠在用力捏时缩回爪子。依托咪酯在测试的比较剂量下不能防止戒断。

paras.en: This raised the possibility that nidradine could reduce pain-related responses even while the animals remained awake.
paras.zh: 这提出了尼拉定即使在动物保持清醒时也可以减少与疼痛相关的反应的可能性。

paras.en: To investigate, the team tested a lower dose and checked that mice could balance on a rotating rod. This helped establish that the animals retained the coordination needed to respond.
paras.zh: 为了进行研究，研究小组测试了较低的剂量，并检查小鼠能否在旋转杆上保持平衡。这有助于确定动物保留了反应所需的协调能力。

paras.en: The researchers then delivered a brief, painful heat stimulus using an infrared laser. Each mouse underwent five trials. The median proportion of trials producing a pain-related response was 40 percent with nidradine, compared with 90 percent in controls. A separate comparison found no statistically significant reduction with etomidate.
paras.zh: 然后研究人员使用红外激光发出短暂而痛苦的热刺激。每只小鼠都经历了五次试验。尼拉定产生疼痛相关反应的试验中，产生疼痛相关反应的中位数比例为 40%，而对照组为 90%。一项单独的比较发现依托咪酯没有统计学上显着的减少。

paras.en: Zebrafish larvae also responded less to a noxious stimulus at concentrations below those causing sedation and anesthesia.
paras.zh: 当浓度低于引起镇静和麻醉的浓度时，斑马鱼幼虫对有害刺激的反应也较小。

paras.en: Cell experiments helped explain nidradine's anesthetic action. A chemical messenger called GABA usually reduces nerve-cell activity. Nidradine boosts its effect through a protein on these cells called the GABA-A receptor.
paras.zh: 细胞实验有助于解释尼拉定的麻醉作用。一种称为 GABA 的化学信使通常会降低神经细胞的活性。尼拉定通过这些细胞上一种称为 GABA-A 受体的蛋白质来增强其作用。

paras.en: The researchers used high-resolution images of rapidly frozen samples, a method called cryo-electron microscopy, to see how nidradine fits into this protein.
paras.zh: 研究人员使用快速冷冻样品的高分辨率图像（一种称为冷冻电子显微镜的方法）来观察尼拉定如何融入这种蛋白质。

paras.en: Its binding site overlapped with those of propofol and etomidate, but nidradine extended deeper into the pocket, making contact with amino acids – the protein's building blocks – beyond the reach of the other two drugs.
paras.zh: 它的结合位点与丙泊酚和依托咪酯的结合位点重叠，但尼拉定延伸到口袋更深处，与氨基酸（蛋白质的组成部分）接触，超出了其他两种药物的范围。

paras.en: "We do not yet know the mechanism responsible for the analgesic effect," McCarroll told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “我们还不知道镇痛作用的机制，”麦卡罗尔告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: This different fit could offer a clue, although its connection to pain relief remains unproven. The team also found that nidradine did not bind to the opioid receptors tested, the proteins through which painkillers such as morphine act.
paras.zh: 这种不同的配合可以提供线索，尽管它与缓解疼痛的联系尚未得到证实。研究小组还发现，尼拉定不会与所测试的阿片受体结合，阿片受体是吗啡等止痛药发挥作用的蛋白质。

paras.en: Nidradine showed another potentially useful feature. Etomidate can suppress production of the stress hormone cortisol; nidradine didn't, in the tests reported here, including experiments with human adrenal tissue outside the body.
paras.zh: 尼拉定显示了另一个潜在有用的功能。依托咪酯可以抑制应激激素皮质醇的产生；在此报告的测试中，包括体外人体肾上腺组织的实验中，尼拉定没有出现这种情况。

paras.en: An anesthetic that also relieves pain could be useful for procedures requiring lighter anesthesia, including emergency care.
paras.zh: 一种能减轻疼痛的麻醉剂可能适用于需要较轻麻醉的手术，包括紧急护理。

paras.en: The low-dose mouse pain experiment involved only four animals per group, however. Reduced defensive responses can't establish exactly what an animal experiences, and the findings do not establish safety or effectiveness in patients.
paras.zh: 然而，低剂量小鼠疼痛实验每组仅涉及四只动物。防御反应减少并不能准确确定动物所经历的情况，而且研究结果也不能确定对患者的安全性或有效性。

paras.en: "Nidradine is still an early-stage research compound, so substantial preclinical work would be needed before considering human trials," McCarroll told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “尼拉定仍然是一种早期研究化合物，因此在考虑人体试验之前需要进行大量的临床前工作，”麦卡罗尔告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: That includes examining how the body processes the compound, its effects on the heart and breathing, and the gap between effective and harmful doses.
paras.zh: 这包括检查身体如何处理该化合物、其对心脏和呼吸的影响，以及有效剂量和有害剂量之间的差距。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the team's continuing search has identified additional molecules with promising anesthetic properties. Researchers are investigating which effects carry over into mammals and which compounds offer the strongest prospects for further development.
paras.zh: 与此同时，该团队的持续研究已经发现了具有前景麻醉特性的其他分子。研究人员正在研究哪些效应会延续到哺乳动物身上，以及哪些化合物最有可能进一步发展。

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: This One Sleep Factor Matters More Than How Many Hours You Get, Study Suggests
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: When it comes to sleep, it's easy to get caught up on numbers.
paras.zh: 当谈到睡眠时，人们很容易陷入数字之中。

paras.en: After all, there's a lot of advice out there on how many hours you should be getting for a healthy heart, or to lower your dementia risk, or to slow down the effects of aging.
paras.zh: 毕竟，关于应该花多少小时来保持心脏健康，或者降低患痴呆症的风险，或者减缓衰老的影响，有很多建议。

paras.en: There's even research on how much sleep you shouldn't be getting, and why more isn't always better.
paras.zh: 甚至还有关于你不应该睡多少睡眠的研究，以及为什么睡得越多并不总是越好。

paras.en: But there's a lot more to sleep than just the duration of it.
paras.zh: 但睡眠的意义远不止于睡眠时间。

paras.en: In fact, new research suggests the consistency of your sleeping schedule is a more important consideration for heart health than the amount of time you spend in bed.
paras.zh: 事实上，新的研究表明，对于心脏健康来说，睡眠时间的一致性比躺在床上的时间更重要。

paras.en: "While we often focus on getting a full eight hours of sleep every night, having a regular sleep schedule – consistent bedtimes, wake times, and sleep duration from night to night – is a practical, actionable step anyone can take that may help protect their heart and blood vessels," says lead researcher and neuroscientist Minh Tuan Viet Nguyen from Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard Medical School.
paras.zh: 波士顿儿童医院和哈佛医学院的首席研究员兼神经科学家 Minh Tuan Viet Nguyen 表示：“虽然我们通常注重每晚获得充足的 8 小时睡眠，但有规律的睡眠时间表——一致的就寝时间、起床时间和每晚的睡眠时间——是任何人都可以采取的实用、可行的步骤，可能有助于保护他们的心脏和血管。”

paras.en: In a new study in Circulation: Population Health and Outcomes, Nguyen and co-author Anh Khoa Tran, a medical researcher from the University of Maryland, analyzed Fitbit tracker data and electronic health records from over 10,000 American adults (median age 53) enrolled in the National Institutes of Health All of Us Research Program.
paras.zh: 在《Circulation: Population Health and Outcomes》中的一项新研究中，Nguyen 和合著者、马里兰大学医学研究员 Anh Khoa Tran 分析了参加美国国立卫生研究院全民研究计划的 10,000 多名美国成年人（中位年龄 53 岁）的 Fitbit 追踪器数据和电子健康记录。

paras.en: What Nguyen and Tran wanted to know was which aspects of sleep are most strongly associated with cardiovascular and metabolic diseases when measured over a number of months.
paras.zh: Nguyen 和 Tran 想知道的是，经过几个月的测量，睡眠的哪些方面与心血管和代谢疾病的相关性最强。

paras.en: It's an important question. When the American Heart Association (AHA) added sleep health to its Life's Essential 8 guidelines for how to optimize cardiovascular health in 2022, its scoring system only measured sleep duration.
paras.zh: 这是一个重要的问题。当美国心脏协会 (AHA) 将睡眠健康纳入其 2022 年如何优化心血管健康的 Life's Essential 8 指南时，其评分系统仅测量睡眠持续时间。

paras.en: Since then, the AHA has clarified that sleep health is "multidimensional", in response to a growing body of research showing that factors such as sleep consistency are important for health, and suggesting they could be a major factor in cardiovascular health in particular.
paras.zh: 此后，美国心脏协会澄清睡眠健康是“多维的”，以回应越来越多的研究表明睡眠一致性等因素对健康很重要，并表明它们尤其可能是心血管健康的主要因素。

paras.en: The new study adds further weight to the case.
paras.zh: 这项新研究进一步增加了此案的分量。

paras.en: The researchers examined several measures of sleep recorded by the participants' Fitbit activity trackers over six months – including sleep duration, sleep quality, sleep regularity, sleep timing, and sleep cycles – and compared these patterns with subsequent medical diagnoses, over a median follow-up period of 3.7 years.
paras.zh: 研究人员检查了参与者的 Fitbit 活动追踪器在六个月内记录的多项睡眠指标，包括睡眠持续时间、睡眠质量、睡眠规律、睡眠时间和睡眠周期，并将这些模式与随后的医疗诊断进行比较，中位随访时间为 3.7 年。

paras.en: The results showed that average sleep duration was not significantly associated with a greater risk of major cardiovascular conditions – including heart attack, heart failure, cardiomyopathy, and ischemic stroke (collectively called the CVD composite).
paras.zh: 结果显示，平均睡眠时间与主要心血管疾病（包括心脏病发作、心力衰竭、心肌病和缺血性中风（统称为心血管疾病复合疾病））的风险增加并没有显着相关。

paras.en: Irregular sleep, on the other hand, did show a link, with each one-standard-deviation increase (29 minutes) in night-to-night variability in people's sleep duration corresponding to a 24 percent higher risk of the CVD composite.
paras.zh: 另一方面，不规律的睡眠确实显示出一种联系，人们的睡眠时间每晚的变化每增加一个标准差（29 分钟），CVD 复合风险就会增加 24%。

paras.en: Other indicators of inconsistent sleeping patterns also showed associations with cardiovascular problems, with greater variability in bedtime, waking time, and sleep midpoint being linked to approximately 20–23 percent higher risk.
paras.zh: 睡眠模式不一致的其他指标也显示出与心血管问题的关联，就寝时间、醒来时间和睡眠中点的较大变化与心血管问题的风险增加约 20-23% 相关。

paras.en: Variation in sleep duration was also associated with a 32 percent higher relative risk of heart failure, 16 percent higher risk for hypertension, and 20 percent higher risk for developing type 2 diabetes.
paras.zh: 睡眠时间的变化还与心力衰竭相对风险增加 32%、高血压风险增加 16% 以及患 2 型糖尿病风险增加 20% 相关。

paras.en: While the findings are observational in nature and don't demonstrate that inconsistent sleep causes people to develop cardiovascular issues, the researchers suggest it's biologically plausible that it would have an impact on health.
paras.zh: 虽然这些发现本质上是观察性的，并没有证明睡眠不一致会导致人们出现心血管问题，但研究人员认为，睡眠对健康产生影响在生物学上是合理的。

paras.en: "Irregular schedules impose recurrent circadian misalignment, which raises blood pressure and impairs glucose regulation under experimental conditions," the team writes in their paper, "and disrupted sleep alters autonomic balance and inflammation."
paras.zh: 研究小组在论文中写道：“不规律的作息时间会造成反复的昼夜节律失调，从而导致血压升高并损害实验条件下的血糖调节，而睡眠紊乱会改变自主神经平衡和炎症。”

paras.en: The results suggest we should evaluate sleep regularity alongside duration in cardiovascular health assessments, the researchers say, with the hope that future research might be able to further investigate how stabilizing sleep schedules may help reduce cardiometabolic risks.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，结果表明我们应该在心血管健康评估中评估睡眠规律和持续时间，希望未来的研究能够进一步研究稳定睡眠时间表如何有助于降低心脏代谢风险。

paras.en: In the meantime, it wouldn't hurt to try to make your sleep routines as consistent as possible, even though things like weekends and shift work can invariably get in the way.
paras.zh: 与此同时，尝试让你的睡眠习惯尽可能一致也没什么坏处，尽管周末和轮班工作等事情总是会妨碍你。

paras.en: "Sometimes the quality of sleep is something we cannot control," Nguyen says.
paras.zh: “有时睡眠质量是我们无法控制的，”阮说。

paras.en: "But the regularity, consistent bedtimes throughout the week and waking up at the same time every morning, is something some people can control."
paras.zh: “但是规律性、一周一致的就寝时间以及每天早上同一时间起床，是一些人可以控制的。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in Circulation: Population Health and Outcomes.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《循环：人口健康和结果》中。

articles.title: Bigger Abs May Not Protect Against Back Pain After All, Surprising CT Study Finds
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: A six-pack is no guarantee against back pain.
paras.zh: 六块腹肌并不能保证不会背痛。

paras.en: A surprising new study has found that those with bigger abdominal muscles on CT scans are just as likely to suffer from lower back pain.
paras.zh: 一项令人惊讶的新研究发现，CT 扫描中腹部肌肉较大的人同样可能遭受腰痛。

paras.en: The findings, published in PLOS Digital Health, suggest that weak abdominal muscles are not necessarily the cause of low back pain, and strengthening them may not be a sufficient solution on its own.
paras.zh: 发表在《PLOS Digital Health》上的研究结果表明，腹部肌肉无力不一定是腰痛的原因，加强腹部肌肉本身可能并不是一个充分的解决方案。

paras.en: "We were surprised that our low back pain group did not have less overall muscle than the controls," says mechanical engineer Kathryn Marusich from Stanford University.
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学的机械工程师凯瑟琳·马鲁西奇 (Kathryn Marusich) 表示：“令我们惊讶的是，腰痛组的整体肌肉并不比对照组少。”

paras.en: "This finding doesn't dismiss muscle as unimportant, but it does underscore the complexity of low back pain and how any differences in muscle size may be more localized."
paras.zh: “这一发现并不认为肌肉不重要，但它确实强调了腰痛的复杂性，以及肌肉大小的差异可能更加局部化。”

paras.en: Marusich and colleagues used a deep learning model to sift through more than 33,500 abdominal CT scans from 23,508 patients.
paras.zh: Marusich 及其同事使用深度学习模型筛选了 23,508 名患者的 33,500 多张腹部 CT 扫描结果。

paras.en: Using electronic health records, the authors found that 2,622 participants had been diagnosed with lower back pain.
paras.zh: 作者利用电子健康记录发现 2,622 名参与者被诊断患有腰痛。

paras.en: This group was then compared with 2,577 participants of the same sex, age, and BMI who did not have lower back pain.
paras.zh: 然后将该组与 2,577 名没有腰痛的相同性别、年龄和体重指数的参与者进行比较。

paras.en: Most prior imaging studies on low back pain are roughly 25 times smaller in size.
paras.zh: 大多数先前关于腰痛的影像学研究的规模大约要小 25 倍。

paras.en: "In the largest investigation of its kind, enabled by AI, we did not see differences in muscle quantity or distribution of abdominal fat between the low back pain and control groups," the study authors conclude.
paras.zh: 研究作者总结道：“在人工智能支持的此类最大规模的调查中，我们没有发现腰痛组和对照组之间的肌肉数量或腹部脂肪分布存在差异。”

paras.en: These results are unexpected, as they run counter to a common hypothesis about what might cause lower back pain.
paras.zh: 这些结果是出乎意料的，因为它们与可能导致腰痛的常见假设背道而驰。

paras.en: Marusich and their team expected that those with lower back pain would have weaker abdominal and back muscles.
paras.zh: 马鲁西奇和他们的团队预计，患有下背痛的人腹部和背部肌肉会较弱。

paras.en: This could strain the lower back muscles as they are more burdened with keeping the spine upright and stable.
paras.zh: 这可能会拉伤下背部肌肉，因为它们在保持脊柱直立和稳定方面负担更大。

paras.en: Several prior studies have found that core strengthening exercises in patients with non-specific lower back pain may be a favorable treatment option.
paras.zh: 先前的几项研究发现，对于非特异性腰痛患者来说，核心强化练习可能是一种有利的治疗选择。

paras.en: But Marusich's team found something unexpected.
paras.zh: 但马鲁西奇的团队发现了一些意想不到的事情。

paras.en: It appeared that patients with back pain were no more likely to have weaker abdominal muscles.
paras.zh: 背痛患者的腹部肌肉似乎并没有变弱。

paras.en: "However," the authors add, "on average, the low back pain group had a significantly lower ratio of muscle to abdominal fat."
paras.zh: “然而，”作者补充道，“平均而言，腰痛组的肌肉与腹部脂肪的比例明显较低。”

paras.en: This suggests that even though participants with back pain were matched to someone with a similar BMI, they may not have had the same muscle-to-fat ratio in their abdomen.
paras.zh: 这表明，即使患有背痛的参与者与体重指数相似的人相匹配，他们的腹部肌肉与脂肪的比例可能并不相同。

paras.en: Perhaps body composition is more important for lower back pain than the sheer strength of the core.
paras.zh: 也许对于腰痛来说，身体成分比核心的纯粹力量更重要。

paras.en: Low back pain is a common and debilitating condition that can impact even the fittest athletes.
paras.zh: 腰痛是一种常见且令人虚弱的病症，即使是最健康的运动员也可能受到影响。

paras.en: In fact, some studies estimate up to two-thirds of adults will suffer from low back pain at some point in their lives.
paras.zh: 事实上，一些研究估计多达三分之二的成年人在一生中的某个阶段会遭受腰痛的困扰。

paras.en: As many as 90 percent of cases are not tied to any specific cause, such as a strain, infection, or fracture.
paras.zh: 多达 90% 的病例与任何特定原因无关，例如拉伤、感染或骨折。

paras.en: That makes treating symptoms all the more difficult.
paras.zh: 这使得治疗症状变得更加困难。

paras.en: Weakness of the deep trunk muscles is commonly considered a possible cause, and as a result, healthcare providers often suggest core stabilization exercises.
paras.zh: 躯干深层肌肉无力通常被认为是一个可能的原因，因此，医疗保健提供者经常建议进行核心稳定练习。

paras.en: But while some small studies have demonstrated clinical benefit to these exercises, the long-term effects are not yet understood.
paras.zh: 但是，虽然一些小型研究已经证明这些练习的临床益处，但其长期影响尚不清楚。

paras.en: CT scans can only reveal so much about abdominal strength, but the recent findings suggest that larger muscles don't necessarily help.
paras.zh: CT 扫描只能揭示有限的腹部力量，但最近的研究结果表明，较大的肌肉不一定有帮助。

paras.en: Strengthening this muscle group as a whole may only do so much.
paras.zh: 加强整个肌肉群的作用可能有限。

paras.en: "Our findings suggest that on average, overall muscle size is not smaller in those with low back pain, aligning with physical therapy studies that highlight the importance of motor control over strength in differentiating healthy and pain populations," the authors explain.
paras.zh: 作者解释道：“我们的研究结果表明，腰痛患者的总体肌肉大小平均而言并不更小，这与强调运动控制在区分健康人群和疼痛人群方面比力量更重要的物理治疗研究结果一致。”

paras.en: They argue that future research should focus on individual muscles and regional changes rather than bulk muscle quantity.
paras.zh: 他们认为，未来的研究应侧重于个体肌肉和局部变化，而不是整体肌肉量。

paras.en: The research has been published in PLOS Digital Health.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在 PLOS Digital Health 上。

articles.title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs

paras.en: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
paras.zh: 深海猪的皮下生活着一些奇怪的东西

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered a strange bacterium hiding beneath the skin of deep-sea creatures known as sea pigs, revealing an unexpected biological partnership. The microbe has an unusually tiny genome, yet more than a quarter of its DNA is devoted to making surface proteins, some of them exceptionally large. Researchers suspect it depends heavily on its host for survival, but what the sea pigs gain in return remains a mystery.
paras.zh: - 科学家们在被称为海猪的深海生物的皮肤下发现了一种奇怪的细菌，揭示了一种意想不到的生物伙伴关系。这种微生物的基因组异常微小，但其超过四分之一的 DNA 用于制造表面蛋白，其中一些蛋白异常大。研究人员怀疑它的生存很大程度上依赖于宿主，但海猪得到的回报仍然是个谜。

paras.en: Deep beneath the ocean's surface, strange, translucent creatures known as sea pigs crawl across the seafloor. Now, researchers at the University of Tokyo have discovered that these unusual animals are hiding something even stranger beneath their "skin." Living within their body walls is a previously unknown bacterium with an extraordinarily small genome and a surprising collection of genes responsible for producing enormous proteins.
paras.zh: 在海洋表面深处，被称为海猪的奇怪半透明生物在海底爬行。现在，东京大学的研究人员发现，这些不寻常的动物在它们的“皮肤”下面隐藏着更奇怪的东西。它们的体壁内生活着一种以前未知的细菌，它的基因组非常小，但其基因组却令人惊讶，它们负责产生巨大的蛋白质。

paras.en: The researchers identified the bacterium, which they named Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola, and used fluorescence imaging to pinpoint its location inside sea pig tissues. Genetic analysis revealed that its genome contains just 649,000 DNA bases, yet more than a quarter of its genetic material is devoted to producing groups of proteins associated with the bacterial surface. Some of these "giant" proteins contain more than 5,000 amino acids and may help the bacteria interact with their hosts or form clusters (clustering into groups). The discovery offers new insights into how bacteria adapt to living in close association with other organisms and which biological functions they retain as they become increasingly dependent on their hosts.
paras.zh: 研究人员鉴定出了这种细菌，并将其命名为 Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola，并使用荧光成像来确定其在海猪组织内的位置。遗传分析显示，其基因组仅包含 649,000 个 DNA 碱基，但其遗传物质的四分之一以上专门用于产生与细菌表面相关的蛋白质组。其中一些“巨型”蛋白质含有超过 5,000 个氨基酸，可能有助于细菌与其宿主相互作用或形成簇（聚集成组）。这一发现为细菌如何适应与其他生物体密切联系的生活以及它们在越来越依赖宿主时保留哪些生物功能提供了新的见解。

paras.en: Meet the Strange Sea Pigs of the Deep Ocean
paras.zh: 认识深海中的奇怪海猪

paras.en: Sea lions, seahorses, and sea cows may be familiar marine animals, but sea pigs are considerably less well known. These small, gelatinous creatures are actually a type of sea cucumber that inhabits the deep ocean. Using numerous tube-shaped feet, they slowly travel across the seafloor, gathering decaying organic material and delivering it to their mouths with specialized tentacles.
paras.zh: 海狮、海马和海牛可能是熟悉的海洋动物，但海猪却鲜为人知。这些小型凝胶状生物实际上是一种栖息在深海的海参。它们使用许多管状的脚，缓慢地穿过海底，收集腐烂的有机物质，并用专门的触手将其输送到嘴里。

paras.en: Despite their unusual appearance, sea pigs perform important work in the deep-sea ecosystem. By consuming dead organic matter, they help recycle nutrients that support other marine life. Their soft, seemingly vulnerable bodies also provide an unexpected benefit to other animals. Young king crabs have been observed using sea pigs as shelter from predators.
paras.zh: 尽管它们的外表不寻常，但海猪在深海生态系统中发挥着重要作用。通过消耗死去的有机物，它们有助于回收养分，以支持其他海洋生物。它们柔软、看似脆弱的身体也为其他动物带来了意想不到的好处。人们观察到幼年帝王蟹利用海猪作为躲避掠食者的庇护所。

paras.en: Many aspects of sea pig biology, however, remain mysterious. Researchers still do not know how long these animals live or precisely why they have long, waving projections resembling antennae on their heads. Another important unanswered question concerns the bacteria that inhabit the layers beneath their outer surfaces.
paras.zh: 然而，海猪生物学的许多方面仍然是个谜。研究人员仍然不知道这些动物的寿命有多长，也不知道为什么它们的头上有长长的、波浪形的、类似触角的突起。另一个尚未解答的重要问题涉及居住在其外表面下层的细菌。

paras.en: Sea pigs belong to a group of marine invertebrates called echinoderms (marine invertebrates including sea cucumbers and sea stars). Like other members of this group, they can harbor bacteria beneath their outer body covering. Scientists are particularly interested in understanding how these microorganisms interact with their hosts and how such relationships evolved. This research is also ecologically important because sea cucumbers make up more than 90% of the biomass of large seafloor animals in some deep-ocean environments.
paras.zh: 海猪属于一种称为棘皮动物（海洋无脊椎动物，包括海参和海星）的海洋无脊椎动物。与该群体的其他成员一样，它们的身体外壳下也藏有细菌。科学家们特别感兴趣的是了解这些微生物如何与其宿主相互作用以及这种关系如何进化。这项研究在生态上也很重要，因为在一些深海环境中，海参占大型海底动物生物量的 90% 以上。

paras.en: "Taxonomic and genomic information about these body-wall inhabiting bacteria is scarce, and very few studies of deep-sea species have linked this information to the bacteria's location within host tissues," said Yu Yoshida, a Ph.D. student at the University of Tokyo's Graduate School of Frontier Sciences and a lead author of the study.
paras.zh: “关于这些体壁栖息细菌的分类学和基因组信息很少，而且很少有对深海物种的研究将这些信息与细菌在宿主组织内的位置联系起来，”吉田博士说。东京大学前沿科学研究生院的学生，也是该研究的主要作者。

paras.en: Scientists Discover a Dominant Bacterium Beneath Sea Pig Skin
paras.zh: 科学家在海猪皮肤下发现了一种主要细菌

paras.en: To investigate these hidden microorganisms, researchers from several Japanese institutions, including the University of Tokyo, examined eight sea pigs collected during deep-sea research expeditions.
paras.zh: 为了研究这些隐藏的微生物，包括东京大学在内的几个日本机构的研究人员检查了深海研究探险期间收集的八只海猪。

paras.en: The team extracted DNA from different tissues to identify the bacteria present throughout the animals' bodies. They also reconstructed the genomes of the most abundant bacterial groups, allowing them to investigate their genetic characteristics. Finally, they used fluorescence imaging, a technique that makes selected biological structures visible through fluorescent signals, to determine precisely where the bacteria lived within the sea pig tissues.
paras.zh: 研究小组从不同组织中提取 DNA，以鉴定动物体内存在的细菌。他们还重建了最丰富的细菌群的基因组，使他们能够研究它们的遗传特征。最后，他们使用荧光成像技术，通过荧光信号使选定的生物结构可见，从而精确确定细菌在海猪组织内的生存位置。

paras.en: The results revealed that one particular bacterium was remarkably abundant in the animals' body walls.
paras.zh: 结果显示，动物体壁中的一种特殊细菌含量非常丰富。

paras.en: "What we found was that in body-wall samples from the three sea pig species, one bacterium accounted for more than 70% of bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences (a genetic marker used in identifying bacteria), so it truly dominated the body wall," explained Yoshida.
paras.zh: “我们发现，在三种海猪的体壁样本中，一种细菌占细菌 16S rRNA 基因序列（用于识别细菌的遗传标记）的 70% 以上，因此它确实在体壁中占主导地位，”吉田解释道。

paras.en: Further investigation showed that this dominant bacterium belongs to a broader group of microorganisms known to live in close association with marine invertebrates. However, its genetic characteristics differ substantially from those of previously identified members of that group.
paras.zh: 进一步的研究表明，这种优势细菌属于一个更广泛的微生物群，已知与海洋无脊椎动物密切相关。然而，它的遗传特征与之前确定的该群体成员的遗传特征有很大不同。

paras.en: Because of these differences, the researchers have proposed recognizing Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola as a new bacterial genus and species.
paras.zh: 由于这些差异，研究人员提出将 Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola 识别为新的细菌属和种。

paras.en: A Tiny Genome Packed With Giant Proteins
paras.zh: 充满巨大蛋白质的微小基因组

paras.en: One of the most surprising findings emerged when the scientists examined the bacterium's DNA. Its genome was exceptionally compact, containing only 649,000 bases, the chemical units that make up genetic material.
paras.zh: 当科学家检查细菌的 DNA 时，出现了最令人惊讶的发现之一。它的基因组异常紧凑，仅包含 649,000 个碱基，即构成遗传物质的化学单位。

paras.en: By comparison, the genome of Escherichia coli, a widely studied bacterium commonly found in the intestines of humans and other animals, is roughly seven times larger.
paras.zh: 相比之下，大肠杆菌（一种广泛研究的细菌，常见于人类和其他动物的肠道中）的基因组大约大七倍。

paras.en: "The complete genome was very small, only 649,000 bases. By comparison, the E. coli genome is approximately seven times larger. However, we were more surprised by the composition. Genes for some of the energy-generating pathways (used for breaking down nutrients and generating energy) which are commonly found in bacteria were not detected," explained Yoshida.
paras.zh: “完整的基因组非常小，只有649,000个碱基。相比之下，大肠杆菌的基因组大约大七倍。然而，我们更惊讶于其组成。没有检测到细菌中常见的一些能量产生途径（用于分解营养物质并产生能量）的基因，”吉田解释道。

paras.en: The absence of genes involved in certain energy-producing processes suggests that the bacterium may have lost some of the biological machinery that many other bacteria use to survive independently.
paras.zh: 缺乏参与某些能量产生过程的基因表明，这种细菌可能已经失去了许多其他细菌用来独立生存的一些生物机制。

paras.en: Yet even more remarkable was how much of its limited genetic material was devoted to proteins associated with its surface.
paras.zh: 然而更值得注意的是，其有限的遗传物质中有多少专门用于与其表面相关的蛋白质。

paras.en: "Meanwhile, genes for encoding surface-associated protein groups (that is, DNA with the blueprints for building specific proteins on cell surfaces) accounted for 27.6% of the entire genome. This included genes for proteins exceeding 5,000 amino acids. As bacterial proteins average about 300 amino acids in length, 5,000 is exceptionally long. This offers us important clues as to which functions are retained in bacteria which live in close association with their host."
paras.zh: “与此同时，编码表面相关蛋白质组的基因（即带有在细胞表面构建特定蛋白质的蓝图的DNA）占整个基因组的27.6%。其中包括超过5,000个氨基酸的蛋白质基因。由于细菌蛋白质的平均长度约为300个氨基酸，所以5,000个氨基酸非常长。这​​为我们提供了重要的线索，了解与宿主密切相关的细菌中保留了哪些功能。”

paras.en: Proteins are built from chains of amino acids, and their structures help determine the jobs they perform. The unusually large proteins identified in this bacterium could be involved in interactions with sea pig tissues or in helping bacterial cells stick together. Their exact functions remain unknown.
paras.zh: 蛋白质是由氨基酸链构成的，它们的结构有助于决定它们所执行的工作。在这种细菌中发现的异常大的蛋白质可能涉及与海猪组织的相互作用或帮助细菌细胞粘在一起。它们的确切功能仍然未知。

paras.en: The discovery suggests that, as the bacterium evolved to depend more heavily on its host, it may have retained certain specialized capabilities while losing genes needed for other essential processes.
paras.zh: 这一发现表明，随着细菌进化得更加依赖宿主，它可能保留了某些专门的能力，同时失去了其他重要过程所需的基因。

paras.en: What Do Sea Pigs Gain From These Mysterious Bacteria?
paras.zh: 海猪从这些神秘细菌中获得了什么？

paras.en: The bacterium's unusually reduced genome offers an important clue about its lifestyle. Researchers believe Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola relies extensively on its sea pig host to obtain substances it cannot adequately produce for itself.
paras.zh: 这种细菌异常减少的基因组为了解其生活方式提供了重要线索。 Researchers believe Candidatus Abyssoplasma scotoplanesicola relies extensively on its sea pig host to obtain substances it cannot adequately produce for itself.

paras.en: These include amino acids, which are necessary for building proteins, along with nucleic acid precursors, lipids, and mineral nutrients. Nucleic acid precursors are the molecular building blocks used to make DNA and RNA, while lipids are important components of cell membranes and other cellular structures.
paras.zh: 其中包括构建蛋白质所必需的氨基酸，以及核酸前体、脂质和矿物质营养素。核酸前体是用于制造 DNA 和 RNA 的分子构件，而脂质是细胞膜和其他细胞结构的重要组成部分。

paras.en: Because the bacterium lacks some of the genes needed to produce or process essential compounds independently, living within the sea pig's tissues may provide access to resources required for its survival.
paras.zh: 由于这种细菌缺乏独立生产或加工必需化合物所需的一些基因，因此生活在海猪的组织内可能会为其生存提供获取所需资源的途径。

paras.en: What remains unclear is whether the relationship also benefits the sea pig. One possibility is that the bacteria help defend their hosts against pathogens, potentially offering protection from disease-causing microorganisms. However, the researchers emphasize that this potential benefit has not yet been demonstrated.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚这种关系是否也有利于海猪。 One possibility is that the bacteria help defend their hosts against pathogens, potentially offering protection from disease-causing microorganisms.然而，研究人员强调，这种潜在的好处尚未得到证实。

paras.en: Understanding why this particular bacterium becomes so abundant in sea pig body walls is another major question. Scientists also hope to determine what its unusually large surface proteins do, how it competes with other microorganisms, and whether its presence changes the health or biology of its host.
paras.zh: 了解为什么这种特殊细菌在海猪体壁中如此丰富是另一个主要问题。科学家们还希望确定其异常大的表面蛋白的作用、它如何与其他微生物竞争，以及它的存在是否会改变宿主的健康或生物学。

paras.en: "We would really like to understand how this bacterium could become so dominant in the body wall, the functions of the giant surface proteins, what competition it faces from other bacteria, and of course the effects on the host," said Yoshida. "More broadly, further investigation could provide fundamental insights into how bacteria colonize hosts and adopt a host-dependent lifestyle."
paras.zh: 吉田说：“我们真的很想了解这种细菌如何在体壁中变得如此占主导地位，巨型表面蛋白的功能，它面临着来自其他细菌的竞争，当然还有对宿主的影响。” “更广泛地说，进一步的研究可以为细菌如何定植宿主并采取依赖宿主的生活方式提供基本见解。”

paras.en: The findings highlight how much remains to be discovered about life in the deep ocean. By investigating the microscopic organisms living within these unusual animals, scientists hope to better understand the evolutionary processes that allow bacteria to form intimate, long-lasting relationships with their hosts.
paras.zh: 这些发现突显了深海生命还有多少有待发现。通过研究生活在这些不寻常动物体内的微生物，科学家们希望更好地了解细菌与宿主形成亲密、持久关系的进化过程。

paras.en: Funding: This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP22H00557 (to S.Y.) and JST SPRING, Grant Number JPMJSP2108 (to Y.Y.)
paras.zh: 资助：这项工作得到了 JSPS KAKENHI 拨款号 JP22H00557（致 S.Y.）和 JST SPRING 的支持，拨款号 JPMJSP2108（致 Y.Y.）

articles.title: This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history

paras.en: This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history
paras.zh: 这头600万年前的鲸鱼可能拥有哺乳动物历史上最弯曲的脸

paras.en: - A bizarre whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so dramatically crooked that scientists believe it may have been the most asymmetrical of any mammal. Discovered in Peru, the extinct pygmy sperm whale Scaphokogia huachafo had an enormous downward-curving snout and a skull so distorted that researchers initially thought it had been damaged after death. Instead, its strange anatomy appears to have been an extraordinary evolutionary adaptation for hunting along the seafloor.
paras.zh: - 一种生活在大约 600 万年前的奇特鲸鱼，其脸部极其弯曲，科学家认为它可能是哺乳动物中最不对称的。在秘鲁发现的已灭绝的侏儒抹香鲸Scaphokogia huachafo有一个巨大的向下弯曲的鼻子和一个如此扭曲的头骨，以至于研究人员最初认为它是在死后受损的。相反，它奇怪的解剖结构似乎是为了适应海底狩猎而进行的非凡的进化适应。

paras.en: A bizarre prehistoric whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so crooked that researchers initially suspected its fossilized skull had been distorted after death. Instead, its extraordinary shape was completely natural and may represent the most extreme facial asymmetry ever documented in a mammal.
paras.zh: 生活在大约 600 万年前的一种奇怪的史前鲸鱼的脸非常弯曲，以至于研究人员最初怀疑它的头骨化石在死后已经变形。相反，它非凡的形状是完全自然的，可能代表了哺乳动物有史以来最极端的面部不对称。

paras.en: Sperm whales and pygmy sperm whales are already known for having some of the strangest head shapes among mammals. While most vertebrates have bodies and skulls that are roughly symmetrical on both sides, toothed whales have evolved uneven skull structures to accommodate specialized organs responsible for producing sound and navigating through echolocation.
paras.zh: 抹香鲸和侏儒抹香鲸因拥有哺乳动物中最奇怪的头部形状而闻名。虽然大多数脊椎动物的身体和头骨两侧大致对称，但齿鲸进化出了不均匀的头骨结构，以容纳负责产生声音和通过回声定位进行导航的专门器官。

paras.en: Now, an international team of scientists has identified an extinct pygmy sperm whale species that took this unusual anatomy to an entirely new level. Named Scaphokogia huachafo, the whale lived during the Late Miocene, between 6.3 and 5.6 million years ago, and measured approximately 2.7 meters in length. Its fossilized skull displays the most extreme facial asymmetry known in any whale or dolphin, and possibly in any mammal.
paras.zh: 现在，一个国际科学家小组发现了一种已经灭绝的侏儒抹香鲸物种，它将这种不寻常的解剖结构提升到了一个全新的水平。这种鲸鱼名为 Scaphokogia huachafo，生活在中新世晚期，距今 6.3 至 560 万年前，体长约 2.7 米。它的头骨化石显示出鲸鱼或海豚，甚至可能是哺乳动物中已知的最极端的面部不对称性。

paras.en: A Prehistoric Whale With an Extraordinary Skull
paras.zh: 拥有非凡头骨的史前鲸鱼

paras.en: "Cranial asymmetry in toothed whales is directly linked to the development of fatty structures in the forehead that are involved in sound production. But in Scaphokogia huachafo, this asymmetry went far beyond the area around the blowhole. Both bony nostrils are shifted entirely to the left side of the skull, while the facial bones differ dramatically in size and position. The skull looks completely crooked," explains Aldo Benites-Palomino, lead author of the study.
paras.zh: “齿鲸的颅骨不对称与前额脂肪结构的发育直接相关，而这些脂肪结构参与发声。但在 Scaphokogia huachafo 中，这种不对称远远超出了气孔周围的区域。两个骨质鼻孔完全移至头骨的左侧，而面部骨骼的大小和位置差异很大。头骨看起来完全弯曲，”该研究的主要作者 Aldo Benites-Palomino 解释道。

paras.en: Benites-Palomino investigated the fossil during his doctoral research at the University of Zurich's Department of Paleontology. He is currently an assistant professor at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU).
paras.zh: 贝尼特斯-帕洛米诺在苏黎世大学古生物学系进行博士研究期间对这块化石进行了研究。他目前是埃尔兰根-纽伦堡弗里德里希-亚历山大大学 (FAU) 的助理教授。

paras.en: The whale's extraordinary appearance also inspired its scientific name. The word huachafo comes from Peruvian Spanish and is commonly used to describe something excessively flashy, bizarre, extravagant, or even tacky.
paras.zh: 鲸鱼非凡的外表也启发了它的学名。 huachafo 这个词来自秘鲁西班牙语，通常用来形容过于浮华、奇异、奢侈甚至俗气的东西。

paras.en: "In Peru, huachafo is an everyday word for anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically," says Benites-Palomino.
paras.zh: “在秘鲁，huachafo 是一个日常用语，指的是任何华丽、夸张、奇异、奢侈或难以从美学角度分类的事物，”贝尼特斯-帕洛米诺说。

paras.en: "When we looked at the proportions of this whale - with its face strongly shifted to the left and its oversized, downward-curving snout - it broke every rule of symmetry and elegance seen in living cetaceans. Its anatomy is so extravagant and odd that huachafo seemed the perfect name for it."
paras.zh: “当我们观察这头鲸鱼的比例时，它的脸明显向左倾斜，鼻子又大又向下弯曲，它打破了现存鲸目动物中对称和优雅的所有规则。它的解剖结构是如此夸张和奇怪，以至于“huachafo”似乎是它的完美名字。”

paras.en: Scientists Initially Suspected the Skull Was Deformed
paras.zh: 科学家最初怀疑头骨变形

paras.en: The remarkable fossil was originally recovered during the mid-1990s from the Pisco Formation in southern Peru. This desert region is famous among paleontologists for its exceptionally preserved fossils of ancient marine animals.
paras.zh: 这块非凡的化石最初是在 20 世纪 90 年代中期从秘鲁南部的皮斯科地层中发现的。这个沙漠地区因其保存完好的古代海洋动物化石而闻名于古生物学家。

paras.en: Benites-Palomino first encountered the specimen in 2015 while preparing his Bachelor's thesis at the Museo de Historia Natural in Lima. Its dramatically uneven shape immediately raised an important question: Was the skull genuinely this crooked when the whale was alive, or had millions of years of geological pressure distorted it?
paras.zh: 2015 年，贝尼特斯-帕洛米诺 (Benites-Palomino) 在利马自然历史博物馆准备学士论文时首次遇到了该标本。它那极其不均匀的形状立刻引发了一个重要的问题：头骨在鲸鱼活着的时候真的是这样弯曲的，还是数百万年的地质压力使它扭曲了？

paras.en: "The initial suspicion with skulls this distorted is always taphonomy - that the specimen may have been flattened or twisted by sediment pressure over millions of years," says Benites-Palomino.
paras.zh: 贝尼特斯-帕洛米诺说：“对头骨如此扭曲的最初怀疑总是埋藏学——标本可能在数百万年的沉积压力下被压扁或扭曲。”

paras.en: "But the sutures are fully closed, and there are no fractures, pathologies or deformations elsewhere on the skull. This was genuine biology, not a result of poor preservation."
paras.zh: “但缝合线完全闭合，头骨其他地方没有骨折、病变或变形。这是真正的生物学，而不是保存不当的结果。”

paras.en: The findings confirmed that the extraordinary asymmetry was part of the whale's natural anatomy, rather than damage caused by burial, fossilization, or disease.
paras.zh: 研究结果证实，这种非凡的不对称性是鲸鱼自然解剖结构的一部分，而不是由掩埋、石化或疾病造成的损害。

paras.en: A Bizarre Adaptation for Hunting Along the Seafloor
paras.zh: 海底狩猎的奇异适应

paras.en: The whale's unusual skull also offers clues about how it survived. Modern sperm whales typically pursue squid in deep ocean waters, but Scaphokogia huachafo appears to have followed a very different hunting strategy. Its anatomy suggests that it was highly adapted to searching for food along the bottom of shallow coastal waters.
paras.zh: 鲸鱼不同寻常的头骨也提供了有关它如何生存的线索。现代抹香鲸通常在深海水域捕猎鱿鱼，但 Scaphokogia huachafo 似乎遵循了一种截然不同的捕猎策略。它的解剖结构表明它非常适合沿着浅海沿岸水域的底部寻找食物。

paras.en: One of its most distinctive features was a large, tube-shaped snout strengthened by dense bone and cartilage that had hardened into bone. These heavy structures served as natural ballast, moving the whale's center of gravity forward and downward.
paras.zh: 它最显着的特征之一是一个巨大的管状鼻子，由致密的骨头和硬化成骨头的软骨加固。这些沉重的结构充当天然压舱物，将鲸鱼的重心向前和向下移动。

paras.en: Its snout also pointed downward at an angle of 31 degrees relative to the rest of its skull. By reconstructing the joint connecting the skull to the first neck vertebra, known as the atlas, scientists determined that Scaphokogia could bend its head downward by as much as 55 degrees.
paras.zh: 它的鼻子也相对于头骨的其余部分以 31 度的角度指向下方。通过重建连接头骨和第一颈椎（称为寰椎）的关节，科学家确定 Scaphokogia 的头部可以向下弯曲多达 55 度。

paras.en: "The entire cranio-cervical complex is modified to point the snout directly toward the bottom," explains Gabriel Aguirre-Fernández, co-author of the study and doctoral advisor at the University of Zurich.
paras.zh: 该研究的合著者、苏黎世大学博士生导师加布里埃尔·阿吉雷·费尔南德斯 (Gabriel Aguirre-Fernández) 解释说：“整个颅颈复合体经过改造，使鼻子直接指向底部。”

paras.en: "The combination of dense bone, the downward-curving snout and the flexible neck articulation allowed the animal to move directly above the seabed and feed close to the sediment."
paras.zh: “致密的骨骼、向下弯曲的鼻子和灵活的颈部关节的结合使动物能够直接在海床上方移动并靠近沉积物进食。”

paras.en: Researchers also believe the whale may have relied on its highly specialized echolocation system to locate prey beneath the soft sediment of coastal environments. Unlike other marine mammals that forage along the ocean floor, Scaphokogia lacked the sensitive facial whiskers or specialized visual adaptations that can help animals find food near the bottom.
paras.zh: 研究人员还认为，鲸鱼可能依靠其高度专业化的回声定位系统来定位沿海环境软沉积物下的猎物。与其他沿着海底觅食的海洋哺乳动物不同，Scaphokogia缺乏敏感的面部胡须或专门的视觉适应能力，无法帮助动物在海底附近寻找食物。

paras.en: Instead, its extraordinarily asymmetrical skull may have supported a sophisticated biological sonar system that allowed it to detect hidden prey.
paras.zh: 相反，它极其不对称的头骨可能支撑着复杂的生物声纳系统，使其能够探测隐藏的猎物。

paras.en: This unusual feeding strategy represents a specialized way of life that no longer exists among modern marine mammals. As ocean conditions shifted toward the end of the Miocene, the ecological niche occupied by Scaphokogia disappeared, eventually giving way to the marine mammal communities familiar today.
paras.zh: 这种不寻常的进食策略代表了现代海洋哺乳动物中不再存在的一种特殊生活方式。随着海洋条件在中新世末期发生变化，Scaphokogia 占据的生态位消失了，最终让位于今天熟悉的海洋哺乳动物群落。

paras.en: The discovery provides a remarkable glimpse into how far evolution once pushed the anatomy of whales, producing a creature whose dramatically crooked face was not a deformity, but an adaptation to a vanished underwater world.
paras.zh: 这一发现让人们得以一睹鲸鱼的解剖结构在进化过程中所取得的巨大进展，产生了一种生物，其巨大的弯曲面孔并不是一种畸形，而是对消失的水下世界的适应。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Zurich. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由苏黎世大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。
